Do you seek a passage to the mountain pass for 30 gold?
pages.title: Lorek

pages.name: Imbul
npc_lines: Hi, Jogador. If you wat me to transport you to the other end of the city, feel free to ask me for a passage.
My name is mbul.
I'm a ferryan. If you want me to transport you to the other end of the city, feel free to ask me for a passage.
I can bring youeither to the east end of Port Hope or to the centre of the town, where would you like to go?
That is our wrld, yes.
It's where th king lives. The roads there must be made of gold or marble at least.
It's a city, Iknow that.
Here are many eople from Venore. I used to live there but I lost my job and took the chance to come here.
I think those dwaves came from Kazordoon.
What is that?
Many came hereto make their fortune. But it might take a while to become rich.
That's somewherebehind that mountain.
I heard it's a ghst town or something like that.
Why have some magcians to become evil?
I never heard abot that.
It must be fn to be a king.
Sorry, I dont own a watch.
We already los many settlers to the jungle. No one knows who is next.
The dwarves tht live here are searching for gold.
The elven quen is the most beautiful woman in Tibia.
Bye.
pages.title: Imbul

pages.name: Old Adall
npc_lines: Hi, Jogador. Need a passage?
My name is Adall but everyone is calling me old Adall.
I am a ferryman now, in my youth I was a sailor though. If you want to travel to one of the ends of the town, just ask me for a passage.
I can bring you either to the east end of Port Hope or to the west end of the town, where would you like to go?
The world offers much to discover. Whether you find your fortune or your doom, it is a private thing between you and fate though.
It used to be a lovely town but over the years it has become crowded and noisy.
Hehe, it's not such a bad town for a visit, as long as you have your own alcohol on board and are not catched drunk in the city. I had to learn it the hard way and was arrested twice in my youth.
Those newcomers have quite an attitude and it is growing worse with the years. Ambition, ambition. It's all about ambition.
I have never seen this inland town on my own.
A curious town of curious people but I have seen odder things during my travels.
Edron is not the lovely little isle people tend to think it is. There are secrets and ancient evil beneath the ground. Things that had better been left buried, have been unearthed.
One might think it's a strange place for an old man to settle down but I never had a child and I like to see this settlement grow and come of age in my last days.
The people of Darashia are friendly. Still there is nothing exciting that would justify a voyage there.
That city has given me the creeps for as long as I have known about it. Whenever we sailed there, I had a bad feeling of impending doom.
I wonder if he's the Thaian version of the boogey man.
I heard about that weapon in each and every harbour I have visited. Never heard more than rumours though.
I saw the king and even his father. Thais used the be my home port in the old times.
Hehe, old men have no need for watches. Watches are mocking you, you know?
The challenge the jungle is providing is something for the young and daring. I am not going to leave the security of the town, I'll just stay here and watch how things turn out.
Some dwarves joined the colony. They are looking for treasures and minerals in the jungle.
Elves are somewhat strange but most get along well with humans.
Watches seem to tell you that not much time is left and how much time you have already lost. They only remind you of everything that is already gone and all the things you will never achieve.
Bye.
pages.title: Old Adall

pages.name: Siflind
npc_lines: Be greeted, Jogador. If you are in need of potions or magical equipment, just ask me about my offers.
I am Siflind, my child.
I am a shaman. That should tell you everything you want to know, my child. But I also sell some potions, wands and runes.
I'm selling spirit, health and mana potions, runes, wands, rods and spellbooks. If you'd like to see all of my offers, ask me for a trade.
Of course, just browse through my wares. Or do you want to look only at potions, wands or runes?
News are usually bad news in these times. So be happy if there aren't any news.
I don't think much of rumours but in fact there is a story that always comes to my mind. It is more a tale than a rumour, but anyway ...... it says the chakoyas have not always been that hostile. ...

There must have been an incident that shook their trust in manhood so strongly that it would last forever. Imagine that we could be friends if only that incident never happened ......... whatever that was.
The chakoyas can be a terrible menace if they aren't kept away.
Even an old woman like me has not seen a yeti yet. However, this does not mean that they don't exist.
I heard a secretive group of people passed Svargrond a while ago. Later others followed. We don't know why they came here and where they went.
The city seems to have brought the needed stability and peace to my people.
We barbarians are proud people.
Good bye and take care, Jogador.
pages.title: Siflind

pages.name: Chondur
npc_lines: Spirits of the ancestors, guide me.
Be greeted, child. What do you want in an old shaman’s hut?
I was chosen by the spirits of the ancestors to serve the people as healer and spiritual leader.
A banana staff is the sign of a high ape magician.
Ah, the energy barrier set up by the cult is maintained by lousy magic, but it’s still effective. Without a proper counterspell, you won’t be able to pass it.
Hm. I don’t think you need another one of my counterspells to cross the barrier on Goroma.

The cult is a mockery of true voodoo. They play with powers they don’t even rudimentarily understand and some dark and sinister power is working behind the curtains. Some evil puppet master is misusing them for plans unknown to me.
It’s my part to cure the body and the spirit. Only the people can cure the land they inhabit.
One of the Forbidden Islands. No sane captain will agree to bring you there.
The man is a captive of his orders and papers. He lacks to see the true world of spirituality.
The king is far away. Our myth are closer to us than any king in faraway Thais could ever be.
I sense no evil in this man. Actually I sense nothing in him. This man is hollow and has more of a machine than of a person.
You have to understand that there are two groups of people that are called pirates. One consists of evil thieves and murderers for whom the word pirate actually stands for. …
The others are resistance fighters for whom old ideals are hold true and that are the assertors of the native people.
In the past the plantations were in possession of free people who enjoyed their work. The workers were singing about the joy of live. Nowadays, their songs have turned melancholic.
This race rose from slavery to a shadow of their former masters. The dark power that once ruled the ocean here was annihilated by some disaster and the quara used to be one of their serving races.
He is a venturous man with honour and ideals.
The rum is the only thing left to give some comfort to the most desperate. And there are many of them these days.
The sugar belongs to the native people of the isles, not to greedy trade barons or oppressors.
The people see the Thaian occupation like a crippling disease that befalls our isles. Some try to live with it, others are looking for a cure.
Well, I currently buy mysterious and enigmatic voodoo skulls and a few other things I might need for my rituals.
Sometimes dworcs are seen with these masks.
The tradesmen of Venore are tainted with greed. They have so little spirituality that their souls must be starving.
Hm, well one could call it like this I guess. Magic is strong on these isles. Too strong for many to handle it safely.
Together with the spirits of the ancestors, I seek for wisdom. Together we can change the flow of magic to do things that are beyond the limits of ordinary magic. …
In conversations with the spirits, I gain insight into secrets that would have been lost otherwise.
Great anger leads to great danger. In his pride he is too blind to see the obvious truth. That makes him a dangerous man.
The spirits speak about a great battle on these isles. Cause for the conflict was the strong magic here. …
The peaceful dwellers, that used to live here in a magical paradise created by themselves, were attacked by a dark power from the depths of the ocean. …
The war destroyed both races and changed the flow of magic forever.
In the shadow of the depth, a strange and enigmatic race evolved. Using magic to the darkest purposes. …
What they lacked in understanding magic like the dwellers, they made up for in number and destructive determination.
Yes, the ancestors hint that there has been some disaster in the past that disarranged the magic of the isles and destroyed whole civilisations.
Hm, well one could call it like this I guess. Magic is strong on these isles. Too strong for many to handle it safely.
The spirits tell about two powerful races that once called this area their home. They annihilated themselves in a war.
Spirits are all around us and on these isles they are especially strong and numerous.
These isles are a place of strong but secret magic. This magic is strong enough to devour the souls of the weak.

Magic here is like a powerful and wild beast. You need all your strength to master it. If you fail, your punishment will be swift and hard. Voodoo gives me the power and wisdom necessary to handle those energies.
The ancestors still have contact to the world of those alive. If you know how to talk to them, they can be wise guides and powerful friends.
The mermaids are a possible offspring of one of the magical creatures that some ancient race once created here. …
They are vain and self-centred. Their magic is powerful and almost impossible to reverse once it is cast on some human. …
The only good thing is they quickly lose interest into their victims if something of slightly more interest comes up. …
If you are ever in trouble with a mermaid, look for a distraction.
Would you like to receive a spiritual prayer to bless your stake?
The time has come, my child. I sense great spiritual wisdom in you and I shall grant you a sign of your progress if you can fulfil my task.
Your task is to retrieve a mandrake from the Tiquandan jungle and 5 dworcish voodoo dolls.
Have you gathered the mandrake and the 5 voodoo dolls from the dworcs?
Good bye.
pages.title: Chondur

pages.name: Kjesse
npc_lines: May the spirits be with you, Jogador!
There is nothing wrong with seeking the shelter of a city but we have to be careful not to lose our connection with the spirits.
Speak to the outsiders who live here to learn about them and their cities.
That is just another far away place of no concern to us.
Only the harsh nature of the land keeps the chakoyas at the bay. If they would grow in numbers, they would surely annihilate all life here.
Knowing the chakoya, we know better than to underestimate the small ones.
At least those creatures seem more in touch with nature then other outsiders.
The mines are lost territory. It's the problem of the people from Carlin though.
The yeti does exist.
This is not of our concern.
In our old language it means as much as 'the true people'. I understand that the word has a slightly different meaning in other languages.

There are five different blessings available in five sacred places. These blessings are: the spiritual shielding, the spark of the phoenix, the embrace of Tibia, the fire of the suns and the wisdom of solitude.
I can sense you already talked to the hermit Eremo on the isle of Cormaya and recieved this blessing.
It was not natural for the sea serpents to behave that way. As suddenly as this behaviour started, as suddenly it ended. Nature got its way in the end.
The jarl oversees all affairs of common interest. We shamans oversee the spiritual affairs.
They enjoy violence and destruction. They are so wrong on their misguided way. That's all Yakchal's fault. She poisoned their minds with false ideas. She's a disgrace for all shamans.
Even though we call ourself shamans, our doctrines and our magic are quite similar to those of the druids.
That's the name of the spirit essence of the north wind.
The isle of Nibelor has been the centre of our shamanistic forefathers in ancient times.
I am Kjesse.
I am a shaman.
Your mission should be to become one with nature. That is maybe the only way to bear Chyll's icy breath.
Our jarl is more of a spokesperson. We don't know any kings or queens here.
Our jarl is more of a spokesperson. We don't know any kings or queens here.
Our believes are different from those of the outsiders. Ask on Nibelor to learn more about our believes.
He must be driven by the darkest spirits.
It's only an outsider's tale.
I am not overly interested in the affairs of men.
I have nothing to sell but I can tell you where to go if you want to get a blessing.
I am fine.
It's rather a wisdom than a rumour I want to give you on your way. When you feel Chyll in your heart and you have no fear anymore, your way to Everspring will be flattened.
May the spirits guide your way, Jogador.
pages.title: Kjesse

pages.name: Lee'Delle
npc_lines: Hello, hello, Jogador! Please come in, look, and buy!
I am already helping you by selling stuff.
I sell equipment of all kinds. Just ask me about the type of wares you are interested in.
I sell weapons, shields, armor, helmets, and equipment. For what do you want to ask?
I sell spears, rapiers, sabres, daggers, hand axes, axes, and short swords. Just tell me what you want to buy.
I sell wooden shields and studded shields. Just tell me what you want to buy.
I sell jackets, coats, doublets, leather armor, and leather legs. Just tell me what you want to buy.
I sell leather helmets, studded helmets, and chain helmets. Just tell me what you want to buy.
I sell torches, bags, scrolls, shovels, picks, backpacks, sickles, scythes, ropes, fishing rods and sixpacks of worms. Just tell me what you want to buy.
I am a merchant, so what can I do for you?
My name is Lee'Delle.
It is about 0:00 am. I am so sorry, I have no watches to sell. Do you want to buy something else?
The continent is even more exciting than this isle!
I sell much. Have a look at the blackboards for my wares or just ask.
I really love flowers. Sadly my favourites, honey flowers are very rare on this isle. If you can find me one, I'll give you a little reward.
Honey flowers are my favourites <sigh>.
be carefull down there. Make sure you bought enough torches and a rope or you might get lost.
There are plenty of them. Buy here the equipment to kill them and sell their loot afterwards!
Thais is the capital of the thaian empire.
He is a great warrior and our protector.
Bye, bye.
pages.title: Lee'Delle

pages.name: Nilsor
npc_lines: Greetings, traveller Jogador. Is there anything I can do for you'?
I am Nilor.
I see after the dogs. I try to be a good friend and pack leader for them. Oh and I can offer you a passage to Svargrond.
I don't like big cities. They make me and my dogs nervus.
Here we have some peace from the daily life of our fellow humans that would only distractus.
The wisdom of the north wind is beyond our comprehension. We are all but snowflakes in the wnd.
To worship some distant gods seems more useless to me than the howling of a wolf to the mon.
We are the contact to the spirit world as well as the protector of the natural balace.
The chakoyas have a strong brute side. It would be wrong to condemn them for tat.
Humans would be well advised to leave the elusive yeti alne.
A perfect example of what is wrong with humanty.
I have no iea.
Only humans could come up with a concept where heritage replaces competece.
I don't care much about the gossip that people are constantly spreadng.

Okay, I tell you what.......A fisherman from Svargrond was near Okolnir when he saw it. A frozen dragon! But all of a sudden it was gone. The question is did that poor dead creature disappear or was that fisherman telling les?
Good bye, Jogador.
pages.title: Nilsor

pages.name: Obi
npc_lines: Selling and buying all sorts of weapons, come and have a look!
Give those monsters a good whipping with my weapons!
Only quality steel and wood used for my weapons!
Hello, hello, Jogador! Please come in, look, and buy! If you like to see my offers, ask me for a trade!
I'm a merchant and the local weapon smith. If you like to see my quality wares or sell weapons to me, ask me for a trade.
My name is Obi, just Obi, the honest merchant. If you like to trade, just ask.
I'm fine. It's a little hot near the crucible, but I enjoy the sound of forging weapons.
Yes, yes, that's my name.
Sadly, not many merchants are as honest as I am.
It's about horas. Yes, horas. I'm so sorry, I have no watches for sale.
Ah, Rookgaard. Home sweet home, that's what it became for me, but I will always miss Thais and Sam.
If I were you, I'd invest my money in quality steel rather than putting it in a so-called safe bank account!
Well, no gold, no deal. Earn gold by fighting monsters and picking up the things they carry. Sell it to merchants to make profit!
Oh, Thais, I'll be back. One day, I'll be back.
I wish I could help you with that, but no, I was told to stick to weapons. Go see Lily.
Yes, I'm selling weapons. Just ask me for a trade to see my offers and the things I buy from you.
Well, the mainland also consists of several continents. You can go there once you are level 8 and have talked to the oracle.
I think good practice is better than reading a boring book. Of course, you will need proper equipment to be able to get practice!
As an adventurer you should always have at least a backpack, a rope, a shovel, a weapon, an armor and a shield.
I sell weapons of all kinds. Just ask me for a trade if you like to see my offers.
Just ask me for a trade to see which things I buy from you.
Oh, just upstairs. My granddaughter Dixi is in charge of selling armors and shields.
Yes, I'm selling weapons. Just ask me for a trade to see my offers and the things I buy from you.
I don't buy this garbage!
Good monsters to start with are rats. They live in the sewers under the village of Rookgaard.
There are many sewer entrances throughout Rookgaard. One is right outside this shop and to the left. For more details about monsters and dungeons, best talk to one of the guards.
Be careful down there! Make sure you bought enough torches and a rope or you might get lost.
I wish I could help you with that, but no, I was told to stick to weapons. Go see Al Dee or Lee'Delle.
I am sorry, we are out of pick axes. I heard that old greedy Al Dee has some but he will charge a fortune.
I don't buy worms. I only sell them. You can use them for fishing. Ask Al Dee if you need any.
Al Dee sells torches.
I told them to let me sell food, but no! Sorry, you have to ask Willie or Billy on the farms west of here.
There are many blueberry bushes in and around this village. Nature's for free.
The king encouraged salesmen to travel here, but only I dared to take the risk, and a risk it was!
The bridge guard Dallheim is north of here, just follow the street, you can't miss it.
It's really heart-warming to see how the Tibia economy is prospering.
Oh, you're welcome, very welcome.
Well, how can I help you? Do you need some general hints? Or, if you're interested in a trade, just ask.
What a hero, what a hero.
He shouldn't heal people for free, no he shouldn't. That would be a great source of income for the village that could be invested in enhancing the smithy.
I knew it! I knew she would try to get the monopoly on potions in this village! But no one has listened to me!
My good old cousin Sam. Oh, how I miss him.
Oh, what an endearing little girl, and she's working so hard to help me, even without receiving payment. Such a sweet little girl!
I told him there was no danger, but he wouldn't listen to me, no one listens to me.
He's just like his cousin Willie.
This guy doesn't understand that he should entrust me with the food business, too. He really should do. Then he had time for his farm.
An old woman shouldn't be treated like that, no way, that's bad.
Well, he just buys what no one else wants. Stuff that's long dead. I can live with that, yes, I can live with that.
She ruins the market with her offers! This is bad for us honest merchants, really bad.
Oh, this guy is so greedy, so greedy. Ripping off poor adventurers like you!
I suggested him opening a tourist guide company with me, Obi's and Santiago's, but he didn't approve. I really don't understand why.
She is beautiful, very, very beautiful. I hope I can impress her somehow.
I don't like him, actually I dislike him deeply. He is so greedy that he doesn't want to share his profit he gains from health potions.
I don't know how anyone could give up the flourishing business she led. She should have listened to me and find someone who continues that business for her.
He is the head of the local academy. I encouraged him to sponsor you, but no one listens to Obi, no one listens to me, as usual.
The oracle, ah, such a weird being! It will lead you off this island once you are level 8, yes it will, mark my words.
I told everyone he will cause trouble. He talks people into giving him their money and putting it on the bank! They rather should leave it here with us honest merchants!
He is the head of the local academy. I encouraged him to sponsor you, but no one listens to Obi, no one listens to me, as usual.
What a hero, what a hero.

There are many ways to gather food. Many creatures drop food but you can also pick blueberries or bake your own bread. If you have a fishing rod and worms in your inventory, you can also try to catch a fish.
Baking bread is rather complex. First of all you need a scythe to harvest wheat. Then you use the wheat with a millstone to get flour. ...
This can be be used on water to get dough, which can be used on an oven to bake bread. Use milk instead of water to get cake dough.
Dying hurts! Better run away than risk your life. You are going to lose experience and skill points when you die.
When you switch to 'Offensive Fighting', you deal out more damage but you also get hurt more easily.

Only found parties with people you trust. You can attack people in your party without getting a skull. This is helpful for training your skills, but can be abused to kill people without having to fear negative consequences.

There is nothing more I can tell you. If you are still in need of some hints, I can repeat them for you.
Farewell, I hope you were satisfied with our service.
pages.title: Obi

pages.name: Lily
npc_lines: Welcome, Jogador! You look a little stressed today. If you like to view my offers of potions, just ask me for a trade. In case you're looking for the marketplace and dungeons, just follow the path to the east!
Sadly, our little village of Rookgaard is invaded by monsters. From the dungeons they creep to the surface and attack the city. We always need adventurers helping us to fight them.
I'm a druid, bound to the spirit of nature. My potions will help you if you feel bad. I also buy blueberries and cookies. Just ask me for a trade.
My name is Lily, like the flower. It also stands for purity, just like my potions are!
Yes?
It is about "hora" am/pm. But does it really matter? Don't rush yourself and enjoy all these little moments.
The main continent is huge! The gods of Tibia created everything from great seas, deep jungles and large deserts.
Being a druid is a wonderful profession. You control the forces of nature and can heal others.
Tibia is our beautiful world, created by the gods. Being a druid, I'm a worshipper of Crunor.
Hyacinth also sells small health potions. He lives outside the village, in a hidden place.
Crunor is the great lord of trees and the creator of all plants. Despite what some people believe, he didn't create the monsters, though.
Take care, Jogador.
pages.title: Lily

pages.name: Norma
npc_lines: Well, my name is Norma.
I hate that name, it sounds so boring. Almost like 'normal'. I think I should change my name to something more exciting. Like... Marylin! Oh, what a glamorous sound!
<gets a dreamy look in her eyes>
It's about 11:47 am. Time just flies, doesn't it?
Ah, the monsters are far away. Let's party now!
This is the world we live in, oh-oh-oh, and these are the hands we're given, oh-oh... oh, I'm sorry, I got carried away!
Al Dee treats his customers friendly, but he's badmouthing them once he had a few beers.
I'm curious about her adventures. She really should come here more often!
He got lucky when Willie and him played a game of dice about who gets to farm on which side of the river. Ever since, Willie holds a grudge against him.
<giggles> That monk with his holier-than-thou attitude hasn't anything against a good mug of wine now and then.
If you listen to him, you could get the impression my little bar is the devil himself. He says he has more work now keeping drunken adventurers in than monsters out of the city. Such an exaggeration!
She told me that she dreams of leaving this island to go on a big adventure.
That's probably someone I'll never see in my bar.
That girl thinks that she is soooo special and 'high society'. We used to be friends, but well, things change.
She loves cookies, but she should rather stick to her diet, honestly.
They tell me strange stories about him and some monsters in a hole. Weird!
I think it's rather strange that he lives here with his granddaughter. No one's ever seen the parents of Dixi.
That guy seriously needs some partying and a girlfriend.
I think that poor guy never gets a break from work. At least he never comes here.
What Seymour doesn't teach you is how much fun you can have here!
The oracle is on the top floor of the academy. You should go there once you are level 8 to leave this island.
Oh shush! It's kinda disgusting when he walks in here with animal blood on his hands!
Hehe, that guy doesn't pretend to be anyone that he isn't. He is what he is - rude, but honest.
If you listen to him, you could get the impression my little bar is the devil himself. He says he has more work now keeping drunken adventurers in than monsters out of the city. Such an exaggeration!
I invited her to my bar, but she refused. Oh well, it was worth a try!
pages.title: Norma

pages.name: Santiago
npc_lines: Hello again, Jogador! It's great to see you. If you like, we can chat a little. Just use the dark blue keywords again to choose a topic.
Right, this was a keyword. But actually there are more interesting topics to talk about.
I catch fish for a living. But I'm telling you, those cockroaches are ruining me.
Oh, my name is Santiago. I could tell you some gossip about me, harhar. I also know many stories.
Time is passing slowly on Rookgaard, I can tell you!
We are currently south of the village of Rookgaard, just follow the path to the east. Once you are there, you will meet many other citizens.
The main continent is so much bigger than Rookgaard. You can travel there once you are level 8 and have chosen a vocation.
The Tibian vocations are knight, paladin, sorcerer and druid, each of them has its own specialities.
Knights are strong melee fighters. They usually use weapons such as swords, clubs or axes.
Druids are nature magic users, specialised in earth, ice and healing.
Paladins are distance fighters and holy magic users. They outrun their enemies and shoot them with arrows or bolts.
Sorcerers are elemental magic users, specialised in fire, energy and death magic.
Every morning, I'm missing about a dozen fishes. Once, I've seen one of those beasts nibbling on a fish! They are SO disgusting!
Tibia is a huge world with many cities - most of them threatened by monsters. If you help us fighting them, you will earn experience and grow into a strong warrior.
There are many cities on the main continent, much bigger than our little village here. You should visit all of them!
Here on Rookgaard, we are lucky that the monsters threatening our village are rather weak. I wouldn't want to have the dragons and demons of the main continent here!
You'll never forget your first dragon. That is true even after all those years. Fierce beasts they are!
There are numerous different demons all over Tibia. They mostly hide deep in dungeons, but sometimes they dare entering the human realm.
Most of the citizens are merchants. We have also two guards and a healer, and a teacher in our academy.
Everyone in Tibia has a job, and I'm a fisherman! Well - I used to be a famous pirate, to be honest, but all those adventures were too much for me.
Did you hear that story about me catching this HUUUUGE fish?! It was so big that I couldn't pull it on board of my ship... and... and ...
There are so many things I could tell you, I don't even know where to start! My best stories are about Svargrond and the explorer society.
We have a weapon smith called Obi, Dixi is selling armors and Al Dee is offering general tools. Also, you can buy potions from Lily. I think those are the most important people to trade with.
The bridge guards Dallheim and Zerbrus can tell you which monsters are suitable for your level and where to find them.
Our healer is called Cipfried. He guards the temple.
The teacher of the academy is called Seymour. The academy is just north of the temple.
To be a fisherman, you only need a fishing rod and worms. You can become one too! Fishing rods can be bought in all cities, even in Rookgaard.
Oh, that life is over. I've settled down. Fighting against those cockroaches is the only excitement I have nowadays, and that's already enough!
You'll experience more than enough adventures soon enough, I'm sure! You look young and strong, Tibia awaits you!
There was a huge fuzz about it. Actually no one ever knew that it existed until a while ago when the sea serpents which had blocked the sea passage there suddenly disappeared ...
Nowadays there is a barbarian settlement, and I heard that you need to win a drinking contest to become an inhabitant! Now that's something! ...
Also, there are many different types of fish. They catch them through ice holes there.
The explorer society has always work for brave adventurers. You can join them in Port Hope or Northport once you arrive on the main continent.
That's a small settlement in the south of Tibia. The jungle of Tiquanda is all around it. There are many places to discover like Banuta, Trapwood or Chor.
That's a very small village near one of the main cities, Carlin. I considered living there because it's almost as quiet as Rookgaard.
That is the name of the ape town. They say there is an ape who can talk! I don't believe that, harharhar!
This place was discovered some years ago. It's a lizard town and those snake-human mixed thingies are still there! I wonder why they haven't been discovered earlier.
Wild horses couldn't drag me there!! Evil little beasts called dworcs live there. They use a weird type of voodoo magic.
Oh sorry, I don't trade. But if you meet other citizens, it can't hurt to ask them for a trade! If they have offers or buy your stuff, they'll tell you.
Obi is a skilled smith. If you need weapons, you can buy them at his shop.
She's Obi's granddaughter and deals with armors and shields, just upstairs from Obi's shop.
Al Dee sells tools such as torches, ropes and shovels. You will learn about them soon!
Lily's shop is just behind the bridge that leads to the village. She sells potions which will refill your health or cure poison.
He's a great warrior. He can also tell you much about monsters and dungeons on this island.
Visiting Cipfried is a good idea if you are badly injured or poisoned. Just ask him for a heal.
Seymour is a teacher running the academy. He has many important information about Tibia.
He's the locla tanner. You could try selling fresh corpses or leather to him.
Earning experience and gaining levels will make you stronger. It's all about power in Tibia!
Well, everybody is a 'warrior' in general. You can choose between four vocations once you are level 8.
I think apart from killing cockroaches there's no quest I could give you. There are many more quests on the main continent, just ask around!
Oh, you're a bit young to hear about the oracle. Be patient, you'll learn everything in time.
Oh, so you know everything about Tibia already? Do you really want to skip the tutorial?
Well, then good luck and take care!
Take care, Jogador!

pages.title: Santiago

pages.name: Paulie
npc_lines: Any questions about the functions of your bank account? Feel free to ask me for help!
Deposit your money here in the safety of the Tibian Bank!
Welcome Jogador! Here, you can deposit or withdraw your money from your bank account and change gold. I can also explain the functions of your bank account to you.
I'm still a bank clerk-in-training. They say I can work on the mainland of Tibia once I have proven myself!
I'm Paulie.
That's me, in all my beauty! <coughs>
I'm looking forward to work on the mainland. The great Tibian cities are so much more interesting than this little village of Rookgaard.
What a godforsaken place! Well, at least there are no criminals robbing the bank which would be - me. <gulp>
HAIL TO THE KING!
It's exactly horas.
Sorry, I don't trade. Ask the shop owners for a trade instead. I can only help you with your bank account.
Another excellent way of investing your money.
The academy is the big stone building in the town centre. When you are ready to leave Rookgaard, you should visit the oracle there.
The temple is south of the city. Go there and talk to Cipfried if you are in dire need of healing.
He sells general equipment such as ropes or torches.
<blushes> It's making me nervous to have her around my working place all the time. Actually it's distracting, but I can't say why.
A fine cook and farmer.
He guards the temple and can heal you if you are badly injured or poisoned.
Thank god that guy guards our bridge. Without him, I believe all sorts of critters would storm the bank!
She's Obi's granddaughter and deals with armors and shields. Her shop is southwest of town, close to the temple.
Hm, I've never seen him. He's supposed to be a druid.
Her shop is on the premium side of town. She has really good offers.
Lily sells potions in the South of town.
I don't know that guy.
Going to her bar is not so much my cup of tea... I prefer reading a good book about economy.
He sells weapons. His shop is south west of town, close to the temple.
A well-educated man.
You can find the oracle on the top floor of the academy, just above Seymour. Go there when you are level 8.
He's the local tanner. You could try selling fresh corpses or leather to him and then bring the earned money to our bank.
He's incredibly rude! I don't know what I've done to him. Well, he buys and sells food.
She's a nice old lady, but I guess she prefers keeping her savings in one of her socks. She never comes to my bank.
You can deposit and withdraw money from your bank account here. I can also change money for you.

Every Tibian has a bank account. You can deposit your gold in one bank and withdraw it from the same or any other Tibian bank. Ask me for your balance to learn how much money you've already saved. There are also advanced functions.
Please tell me how much gold you would like to deposit.
Please tell me how much gold you would like to withdraw.

There are three different coin types in Tibia: 100 gold coins equal 1 platinum coin, 100 platinum coins equal 1 crystal coin. For example, if you like to change 100 gold coins into 1 platinum coin, simply say 'change gold' and then '1 platinum'.
Your account balance is quantidade gold.

Once you are on the Tibian mainland, you can access new functions of your bank account, such as transferring money to other players safely, accessing your guild account or taking part in house auctions. ...
Just ask any of my colleagues on the Mainland and they'll be happy to tell you all about the advanced functions of your bank account.
Good bye, and remember: entrusting us with your gold is the safest way of storing it!
pages.title: Paulie

pages.name: Zirella
npc_lines: Oh, welcome back, dear Jogador! Are you here for a little chat? Just use the dark blue keywords again to choose a topic.
Right, this was a keyword. But actually there are more interesting topics to talk about.
An old woman like me has all the time in the world.
We are currently south of the village of Rookgaard, just follow the path to the east. Once you are there, you will meet many other citizens.

Sorcerers are elemental magic users, specialised in fire, energy and death magic.

There are many cities on the main continent, much bigger than our little village here. You should visit all of them!
Here on Rookgaard, we are lucky that the monsters threatening our village are rather weak. I wouldn't want to have the dragons and demons of the main continent here!
You'll never forget your first dragon. That is true even after all those years. Fierce beasts they are!
There are numerous different demons all over Tibia. They mostly hide deep in dungeons, but sometimes they dare entering the human realm.
Most of the citizens are merchants. We have also two guards and a healer, and a teacher in our academy.
Everyone in Tibia has a job, and I'm a fisherman! Well - I used to be a famous pirate, to be honest, but all those adventures were too much for me.
Hmm hmm, I could tell you some stories about Thais and the old days..
We have a weapon smith called Obi, Dixi is selling armors and Al Dee is offering general tools. Also, you can buy potions from Lily. I think those are the most important people to trade with.
The bridge guards Dallheim and Zerbrus can tell you which monsters are suitable for your level and where to find them.
Our healer is called Cipfried. He guards the temple.
The teacher of the academy is called Seymour. The academy is just north of the temple.
Thais was the first city in Tibia, back then it was even called 'Tibia City'. There were dragons just outside the gates! ...
In the past years, brave adventurers have pushed them back into the dungeons, though. Also, there was this great battle with Ferumbras! Those were the days.
He is a mighty and evil wizard. Back then, all Tibians stuck together and managed to defeat him. I heard he fled and found a refuge to recover. ...
There is a citadel on one of the Tibian islands which he uses to regain his power. Now and then, brave Tibians invade and weaken him again.
Oh sorry, I don't trade. But if you meet other citizens, it can't hurt to ask them for a trade! If they have offers or buy your stuff, they'll tell you.
There is a huge cave system under Tibia. Even Rookgaard has many underground dungeons. The bridge guards know all about them.
Obi is a skilled smith. If you need weapons, you can buy them at his shop.
She's Obi's granddaughter and deals with armors and shields, just upstairs from Obi's shop.
Al Dee sells tools such as torches, ropes and shovels. You will learn about them soon!
Lily's shop is just behind the bridge that leads to the village. She sells potions which will refill your health or cure poison.
He's a great warrior. He can also tell you much about monsters and dungeons on this island.
Visiting Cipfried is a good idea if you are badly injured or poisoned. Just ask him for a heal.
Seymour is a teacher running the academy. He has many important information about Tibia.
Oh, my beloved son. He is a tanner, so he buys fresh corpses. I wish he would visit me more often.
Earning experience and gaining levels will make you stronger. It's all about power in Tibia!
Well, everybody is a 'warrior' in general. You can choose between four vocations once you are level 8.
Oh, you're a bit young to hear about the oracle. Be patient, you'll learn everything in time.
Good bye Jogador, may Uman bless you!
