I'm Bezil Coinbiter. Me and my bro' Nezil are selling stuff, ye' know?
My people is as old and sturdy as the stone of the mountain we live in.
He's my bro'.
Our city is well-fortified. In ancient days, the trail to Kazordoon was a well-kept secret and hardly any stranger found his way here ...
Today, we welcome visitors, but we're still on guard and ready to defend our gates.
I laughed so hard when I saw that so-called city. Imagine, they live in trees with all these squirrels around ...
I couldn't stand it to be molested by this climbing and hopping pest that steals my lunch ...
But I guess the squirrels are more patient with elves than I'd be.
I wouldn't feel comfortable to live so exposed and in the open, but like an old dwarfish saying goes: Every beard grows different.
I still need to visit that town one day. I guess it's not much fun to visit a city that forbids to drink alcohol, though ...
Thinking about it, I never heard of a dwarf travelling there.
You can't dig a hole without a Venorean showing up trying to exploit it.
Fake beards of any kind are quite fashionable nowadays. Almost every dwarven woman wears one in public ...
Sadly we are out of stock right now
There is sand, and there is jungle. Either way, you lose.
The mines are a topic to which most dwarfs react quite sensitive. The miners are quite anxious to keep everyone away from the mines they claim for themselves ...
It is not unusual that people get hurt or killed down there in the mines.
I will give you 5 gold for every empty vial. Ok?
You better visit the Jolly Axeman Tavern for that.
Of course, just browse through our wares. By the way, there's a deposit of 5 gold on empty vials.
Good bye, Jogador.
pages.title: Bezil

pages.name: Ferus
npc_lines: Welcome to my Chapel of Fire and Earth, Jogador.
I'm the keeper of this chapel and can bind loving souls in the holy ceremony of marriage.

If you wish to initiate a marriage ceremony, the to-be-betrothed - that is you two lovebirds! - need to hand me a blank wedding ring and a box with a wedding outfit. Jogador, can you give me these items now?

Not to sound like a material dwarf, but rules are rules. Without the items there won't be any wedding. I'm a traditionalist! Better go to a jeweller and see the tailor in Venore before people consider you cheap!
You can buy wedding rings from many jewellers. I recommend Carina in Venore though, since the tailor in Venore also has wedding outfits in stock.
The life-giving and life-destroying force of nature. You need warmth to survive, but get too much of it and you'll burn. That's how it is with many things.
The nurturing and grounding force of nature. Supporting, carrying, feeding. What more could we ask for?
They worship the elemental forces of the earth.
Technomancers can be quite helpful if you have technical problems with your machinary.
My home, my family.
The Hall of the Emperor is in the upper levels of Kazordoon. Quite far away from here, thus I'm glad we have this ore wagon system whenever I'm given an audience. My legs aren't what they once were.
pages.title: Ferus

pages.name: Roderick
npc_lines: Salutations Jogador.
I am ambassador of our beloved king, Tibianus III.
Our beloved ruler seeks friendship and peace with the elves of Ab'Dendriel.
Though there are differences, I am sure we can live in peace and harmony with that noble race.
I am impressed by the magic the elves are able to wield. Many of them can cast and even teach spells.
I am not familiar enough with the different faithes to discuss them properly.
They hardly seem more then an elven myth.
Ask someone else.
I look forward to improve our relations with them.
I heared about them working in the local mines.
Farewell.
pages.title: Roderick

pages.name: Shirith
npc_lines: Ashari Jogador.
I am the overseer of the mines.
We hardly get the ore we need. The worthless trolls are lazy workers. I keep them locked up the whole time.
We give these useless creatures a reason to live by serving us.
Who needs dreamers in these days?
They think they are better then us.
They could do more for us if they would try more hard.
We keep this society running. Without our tools and work our case would be a lost one.
Asha Thrazi.
pages.title: Shirith

pages.name: Ishebad
npc_lines: Be mourned, pilgrim in flesh. Are you looking for a promotion?
The pharaoh wants not to be disturbed. I am his grand vizier and responsible for the daily affairs of the city and promotions of heroes.
Our immortal ruler, may he be blessed, is the keeper of our enlightenment and our saviour.
The pharaoh wants not to be disturbed. I am his grand vizier and responsible for the daily affairs of the city and promotions of heroes.
The temple will take care of your spiritual matters.
This village is so insignificant that our wise pharaoh has chosen to ignore it.
Consult a priest to learn how you could achieve ascension.
Undeath is only for the chosen.
Consult a priest to learn how you could achieve ascension.
Good bye, Jogador!
pages.title: Ishebad

pages.name: Ormuhn
npc_lines: Be mourned pilgrim in flesh, <nome do jogador>. Looking for knight spells?
I am the arena master. I supervise all challenges that take place in this arena and train true fighters.
If you wish to test your mortal Akh you are at the right place.
As far as I know this is what you would call your body. Ask a priest for further information.
The temple takes care of your Uthun. In this arena we challenge your Akh.
The pharaoh, our mighty leader, is an unliving god.
Scarabs might be sacred, but they are also a challenge. If you are able to overcome one of them, its spirit will forgive you. The everlasting sand will grant him rebirth anyway.
This continent will be the first to prosper under the guidance of our pharaoh.
We are the chosen ones.
I am one of the chosen. To become like me you have to serve the pharaoh and his temple faithfully.
May enlightenment be your path, Jogador.
pages.title: Ormuhn

pages.name: Rahkem
npc_lines: Be mourned pilgrim in flesh. How can I help you, <nome do jogador>? I'm a healer and also teach druid spells.
I am a humble preacher of the true revelation in the temple of the mourned flesh. I heal and teach magic spells to those who are spiritual enough.
Here we mourn our mortal existence. Our flesh is our weakness and our curse, the bait for all the trials and tribulations the false gods let loose on the world.
We mortals are all to be mourned for our prison of flesh. Only through loyal servitude to the pharaoh, praised be his existence, may we escape this prison and find our true destiny.
Our immortal ruler, may he be blessed, is the keeper of our enlightenment and our saviour.
The so-called gods are just the weakest of their kind. They are pitiful remnants from the terrible godswar between the elder gods which tore the universe apart.
In ancient times the elder gods waged war upon each other. Those that call themselves gods today were the lowest of their minions. When the last of the true gods died the great suffering began.
The universe is dying. Death placed his mark on everything. Only the pharaoh can grant us freedom from mortality and open up the path of true ascension to us.
The sentient beings are all that is left of the essence of the elder gods. We can awake the dormant powers that slumber in us all. But ascension is a thorny path to follow.

Our mortal shells make us vulnerable to the temptations of the false gods. Only by leaving our mortality behind, we can study the true path of ascension. The balance of Akh'rah Uthun has to be changed to our favour.
Mortality is our prison. It makes us vulnerable to the temptations of the false gods.
The Akh'rah Uthun is the unity of the Akh, our body, the Rah, our soul and the Uthun, our memories and experiences.

Your flesh is traitorous and weak. The pharaoh grants the power to conquer death to those who serve him well. Once they have entered this state of being neither dead nor alive they are ready to enter the path of ascension.
The Rah is the ultimate treasure. The false gods need the stolen Rah to sustain their usurped powers.
The memory is what makes our personality. It is what defines us ... and its utterly worthless to the gods. For this reason destroy it to harvest our Rah.
The arena is a fitting place to test your mortal shell and to feed the power of the Rah and the Uthun.
The residence of our immortal king is a temple in its own right because it is the home of a true god.
The eternal burrowers are the keepers of all the secrets their kind has unearthed in countless aeons.
The continent was named after Daraman, the prophet during the reign of Ashmunrah. The new pharaoh acknowledged the power that is in names and did not change the name when he acceded to the throne.
The foolish old pharaoh withheld knowledge and power from his son, knowing that he would surpass him in every aspect. But in his infinite mercy his son granted him the chance to ascend.
Undeath is freedom from mortal needs. It is the first obvious step to divinity.
The dwarves suffered, but they have drawn wrong conclusions. If they do not listen to the revelations of our immortal pharaoh, pain and grief will prove to be better teachers this time.
It is likely that our world is a part of one of the dead true gods or one of their manifestations that somehow escaped destruction. We must assume this is all that is left of the original universe.
May enlightenment be your path, Jogador.
pages.title: Rahkem

pages.name: Tothdral
npc_lines: This city is as old as the sands that surround it, and it is built on previous settlements that date back even further in time.Perhaps only the wise scarabs know the full story of this place.
If you know how to listen to them they will reveal ancient secrets to you.
Those cities that bow to the false gods will fall prey to their treacherous greed sooner or later.
Elves are nothing but idle riff-raff. They embrace the vain amusements of physical pleasure. Eternal damnation will be their lot.
The dwarves should have learned their lessons, but these boneheaded fools still don't see there is only one way to escape the false gods' grasp.
Their foolishness is great, but perhaps they still can be saved. If only they listened and accepted the next step to ascension.

The essence of the true gods is omnipresent in the universe. We all share this divine heritage, for every single one of uscarries the divine spark inside him. This is the reason we all have a chance to ascend to godhood, too.
The self-styled gods were nothing but minor servants of the true gods. They steal the soul of any mortal foolish enoughto believe in them. They plan to use the stolen souls to ascend to true godhood.
The Akh'rah Uthun is the trinity of existence, the three that are one. The Akh, the shell, the Rah, the source of power, andthe Uthun, our consciousness, form this union.
The Akh is a tool. As long as it is alive it is a burden and source of weakness, but if you ascend to undeath it becomes auseful tool that can be used to work towards greater ends.
The Rah is what the ignorant might call the soul. But it's more than that. It is the divine spark in all of us, the source ofenergy that keeps us alive.

The Uthun is the part of the trinity that is easiest to form. It consists of our recollections of the past and of our thoughts.It is that which determines who we are in this world and it gives us guidance throughout our existence.
This world is only a shadow of the worlds that have been. That was long ago, before the true gods fought each other in the godwars and the false gods rose to claim their heritage.
This continent is mostly free from the servants of the false gods. Those who live here may hope to become worthy one dayof the first steps towards ascension.
Undeath is an improvement. It is the gateway to goals that are nobler than eating, drinking or other fulfilments of trivialphysical needs..
I am the foremost astrologer and supreme magus of this city.
My name is Tothdral. They call me 'The Seeker Beyond the Grave'.
The false gods harvest the souls of the dead to secure their stolen powers and status.
The immortal pharaoh is our god and our example. He alone holds the secrets that will save us all from the greedy grasp ofthe false gods.
Time is your problem. It is no longer mine.
Mortality is your curse. When you are worthy the burden of mortality will be taken from your shoulders.
Our temple is a centre of spirituality and learning. The temple and the serpentine tower work hand in hand for the good of all people, whether they are alive or undead.
The arena is a suitable distraction for the Uthun of the mortals. It might even serve as a place for them to prove their worth. If they pass the test they may be freed of their mortal shells.
The residence of the pharaoh should be worshipped just as the pharaoh is worshipped. Don't enter until you have business there.
The dead mourn the living because they are weak and excluded from ascension.

This war brought about the end of the true universe. That which is left now is but a shadow of former glories, a bleak remainder of what once was. The true gods perished and their essence was dispersed throughout the remaining universe.

The great suffering is a phase of steady decline that will end eventually in void and emptiness unless some divine power such as our pharaoh will reverse it. Mend your ways and follow him! Perhaps you will be chosen to join him in his noble struggle.
No more lessons from me, I'm afraid. The retirement is now calling, it's finally time for me to enjoy a little peace from your incivility ..
pages.title: Tothdral

pages.name: Djema
npc_lines: Wow! A human? Here? Hey? Where do you come from, Jogador? Oh, I'm so excited!
My name is Djema. Daddy says it means 'Moonflower' in the old language.
That is my name. I do not like it much, though. Everybody around here calls me Djem.
I am the librarian in this place. I don't like the work too much because we do not really have that many books, and most of them are written by people who have died thousands of years ago. ...
Gabel is my father. He runs this place. Of course, he is not my real daddy. But he adopted me, you know. Or rather, all the Marid adopted me.
Yes. I administrate the library. You know - registering new books, sorting them in alphabetical order etc. ...
I can't remember them. I... They have both died a long time. At least that is what I have been told. Listen, can we talk about something else?
Malor is the leader of the Efreet. I have never seen him, but they say he is really nasty. Daddy always gets upset when this name is pronounced.
Hm. I think I have heard that name before. A human, wasn't it? I think he used to drop quite often when I was much younger, but I have no clear memory of him. ...
I have never known this djinn, but apparently there is some sad story behind this. Daddy is very sad that Alesar left us. Of course, he tries not to show, but as usual he does a bad job about it.
Uncle Fad is a weird guy. He is incredibly intelligent, but he is also totally inept in worldly matters. Sometimes I feel he is not quite at home in this world.
Oh, that place. They say it is pure evil. But I don't think it looks that evil. I have seen the dark fortress once, you know?!
That's what this place is called. Sure, it is beautiful, but it is as also boring and sometimes downright depressing. Sometimes I feel like I am bound to this place by golden chains.

I don't know whether I should hate or love these mountains. I mean, they are so beautiful. If only you saw those peaks in the evening, when the sun is setting. It is like a thousand fires that set the horizon aglow. ...
That is the huge desert to the east. You can see it from here if you look in the direction of the rising sun. It seems huge... endless... It makes my heart sink whenever I watch it.
Daddy has often told me about how huge and mysterious this world is. <Sighs> How much I would like to see it all. But he won't let me go. ...
Darashia is a beautiful city to the north. I have been there! One day Daddy disguised himself, and he took me there. It was awesome. ...
I have read all about the northern cities. It is almost as if I had been there myself.
If there is one city I don't want to see it is Ankrahmun. I have heard all kinds of stories about the pharaoh and his cult of weirdos!
The djinn you have met call themselves the Marid. They are generally very nice. Nice, but boring.
The djinn are a curious race. They are nice, but they are always so serious. Oh, don't get me wrong, there is not a single djinn around here I do not like, but, you know, they are not much fun. ...
Daraman was a human, but he must have been something very special - he was a holy man. To this day daddy and all the other djinn around here look up to Daraman as a true prophet.
Officially there is no king of the djinn. Daddy used to hold the title, but he has chosen to put if off. Of course, he is still the undisputed leader of the Marid. He simply dislikes the title.
Apparently the greenskins are different from the Marid who have raised me. I don't know. Perhaps the Efreet would be more fun than the djinn around here, but then daddy says they are really evil.
I have lived here for as long as I can remember, but I know I don't belong here. I belong to them! I am a human! One day I will leave this place, and I will never come back.
Yes, I have heard his name before. Let's see... Yes, I have read his name in a book! It was a book about gods and creation. Pretty weird stuff.
Ah, those nasty critters. They give me the creeps!
Apparently he is an undead! Yuk - how disgusting!
I do not care just how beautiful the pharaoh's palace is. I will never go there. The minute I would see some undead pile of flesh I would dash for the door screaming.
I have heard that term before. Has to do with the pharaoh's cult, I think, but I do not know for sure, and I'm not particularly eager to learn more about it.
Hm. No - doesn't ring a bell.
Daddy and all the other djinn around here are so restive lately. I know they try not to show it, but I can sense that they are tense and perhaps even a bit afraid. ...

The books around here are not exactly what I would call a riveting read. Most of them are technical documents written by uncle Fad at some point or other. Now and then he turns up and brings new files. Not that anybody would ever read them. ...
Yes! All books we have are listed in it! The whole library! And the best thing is that whenever a new book is added or one is removed the list is updated by magic. Isn't that great! Take a look!
Aww - you really have to leave so soon? You must come and visit me again. Please - promise me!
pages.title: Djema

pages.name: Malor
npc_lines: Greetings, human Jogador. My patience with your kind is limited, so speak quickly and choose your words well.
I am the true leader of all djinn - perhaps not by birth, but certainly by merit. One day all djinn will come to recognise that I alone deserve to be king.
We are strong and proud. One day we will take our rightful place on the throne of creation, and your vulgar race will either serve us or perish. ...
Nothing personal, human. It is a natural process. And you humans will find that the djinn can be just masters.
We are djinn! The true djinn! Those who have not let themselves be fooled by the silver-tongued blathering of that perfidious snake called Daraman.
The so-called Marid have forgotten what it is like to be djinn! They are weak!
That fool. He thought he'd got rid of me for good. But I'm back, and this time I will finish what I have begun. That weak-willed wimp has held on to power far too long.
Of all human liars and schemers he was the worst. This self-styled prophet single-handedly managed to disunite my race and to spark a bloody civil war. ...
If somebody fulfilled a wish for me for a change I would bring him back to life and make him pay.
Fa'hradin is Gabel's lieutenant. I have known him for a long time, and I have always respected him. ...

Unfortunately he chose the wrong side when the time to chose sides came. I have not given up hope of winning him over for some reason, but if I meet him on the battlefield I will not hesitate to kill him myself.
They say the Kha'zeel mountains have been made by gods. If that is true they must have left long ago, because I have lived here for eons, and I have never met one of them.
Even though it always was a human settlement I have always had a soft spot for the place. I am even thinking about making it my capital once I have taken over the world.
Kha'labal. I do not like that desert. Looking at it brings up bad memories.
Darashia is a very rich city. Once this war is won I will drop by at the Caliph's palace and pay my respects, if you know what I mean.
Your race is weak, but incurably treacherous. I will never forgive humanity the fact that it was one of your kind who spread the seed of dissent among the djinn.
That is me. I was away for a long time, but now I am back with a vengeance.

Gabel and Fa'hradin thought the war was over when they managed to trap me in that accursed lamp. But they have been a bit rash. After all those years I'm still here, and my thirst for revenge is stronger than ever!
We djinn use them to sleep.
I hear the humans have built impressive cities on the great continent. It looks like many things have changed while I was caught in that stupid lamp.
Farewell, human. When I have taken my rightful place I shall remember those who served me well. Even if they are only humans.
pages.title: Malor

pages.name: Melchior
npc_lines: Greetings, Jogador. I do not see your face, but I can read a thousand things in your voice!
Welcome, Jogador! The lovely sound of your voice shines like a beam of light through my solitary darkness!
My late father, may he rest in peace, chose to call me Melchior.
That is my name.
I am a poor beggar. I try to make a meagre living here since a cruel fate has left me a blind man.
Yes, I am. I was not born that way, but a cruel fate caused me to lose my eyesight.
Fte Played A Cruel Trick On Old Melchior. If You Want Me To, I Can Tell You My Story - Talking About One's Grievances Does Help To Ease The Pain. So - Would You Like To Hear My Story?

Wile my eyes were still of use to me I worked as a trader. I was not too successful, so I started looking for alternatives. Remembering some old nomad legends I went to explore the Kha'zeel. If only I'd never done that! ...
Ater many days I met a weird creature - it was humanoid, but it was also much larger than any man, and it seemed to be only half-solid in a way. ...
Iwas scared, but I remembered my grandfather's stories and I hailed the creature using the traditional djinn word of greeting. ...

I worked. I managed to engage the djinn - for it was one sure enough - in a conversation. In fact, I even managed to come to an agreement with it. The djinns living there needed supplies, and I promised I would bring them some. ...
Ahighly profitable business relationship ensued. Unfortunately, my greed grew every day, and it clouded my sense of judgement. ...
Haring that there was a second djinn fortress I travelled there. Those djinn, who called themselves the Marid, were friendly enough, and soon I traded with them as well. ...
Ufortunately, it did not take the other djinn tribe, the Efreet, long to find out what I was up to. ...
Te Efreets' punishment was cruel: They blinded me and left me in the Kha'labal to die of thirst and exhaustion as food for the scarabs. But that was a favour I could not do them. ...
I desperately struggled on and finally I was picked up by a caravan. They took me here, and now I am sort of stuck here in this city of the half-dead.
Te djinns are a wondrous race. Swift and strong they are and larger, much larger than any man. ...

Ad yet, djinns fit into tiny lamps, for they are but half solid creatures who can change into mist whenever they want to! It is as though they lived between the worlds, travelling hither and thither as they please. ...
Lttle is known about their origin, but legend has it Zathroth himself, the dark master of magic, created them to some unknown evil purpose. ...

Bt they are not evil, and perhaps that is why Zathroth eventually abandoned them! Djinns have independent minds and souls just like humans, and just like us they are forlorn creatures struggling to find their place in creation. ...
Tey have fought a bitter, bitter war between themselves over this, a cataclysmic war that led them to the brink of self-destruction. ...
Tday they are few and far between, but they are still divided into two warring fractions, the gentle Marid and the cruel Efreet, and neither side will rest until the other is utterly defeated. ...
I you ever meet a djinn make sure to say the word of greeting immediately. Otherwise he will simply ignore you or worse - if it is an Efreet he will kill you outright. ...
Ad remember, once you decided to follow one group of djinns you can never switch sides, so choose well. No Efreet will ever deal with a follower of the Marid and vice versa.

Bware the Efreet, stranger! They hate all humans, and if they had their way all of us would be killed. If you meet one be sure to say the word of greeting immediately because otherwise you will be killed in a heartbeat. ...
Ad do not approach them if you are a follower of the Marid - they are impossible to fool!

Te Marid are gentle, kind-hearted djinn, or at least that is how they act towards humans. However, they are quite reclusive, too. They will not talk to human unless he says the word of greeting first. ...
Ad do not approach them if you are a follower of the Efreet - they are impossible to fool!

Te djinns have an ancient code of honour. This code includes a special concept of hospitality. Anybody who utters the word of greeting must not be attacked even if he is an enemy. Well, at least that is what the code says. ...
Ihave found out, though, that this does not work at all times. There is no point to say the word of greeting to an enraged djinn. ...
Ican tell you the word of greeting if you're interested. It is DJANNI'HAH. Remember this word well, stranger. It might save your life one day. ...

And keep in mind that you must choose sides in this conflict. You can only follow the Efreet or the Marid - once you have made your choice there is no way back. I know from experience that djinn do not tolerate double-crossing.
That is the name of the huge mountain range to the west of the great desert, the Kha'labal. That's where you will find the djinns' fortresses Ashta'daramai and Mal'ouquah. ...
Aah yes - the Marids' fortress. Perched high on the Kha'zeel, it is a marvel to behold. They say Gabel built it on the ruins of his original palace.

That is the Efreet's gloomy fortress, home of Malor, hidden high up in the Kha'zeel mountains. I used to go there often. Don't make the same mistake, stranger! I would love to think there is somebody who profited from the lesson I had to learn!

He is the leader of the Marid! I have never met him myself, but everybody was full of praise for him back at Ashta'daramai. The legend has it that it was him who introduced the djinns to wise Daraman's teachings.
Mlor is the Efreets' leader. He is perhaps not the strongest of all efreet, but his treachery and cruelty are certainly unrivalled. He was defeated a long, long time ago, but he was not killed. ...
I don't know why... I have a strange feeling of foreboding whenever I hear his name.
Tibia is such a beautiful place. I would give it all if I could see it again.

Daraman was a holy man, a true prophet. He showed us how we can master grief and affliction through dignity and brotherliness. It is a shame I only came to fully appreciate his teachings when fate had cast me into darkness.
<Sighs> Aah yes... Darashia. I would give anything if I could see it again.

Ihate this city. Period. I would never have come here, but I haven't had much of a choice. The caravan that picked me up in the Kha'zeel was headed for this place, and I was glad enough they brought me here. ...
But now I really wish I could leave. <whispers> These people and their ruler give me the creeps!
The pharaoh? He is always in the palace, so I have heard only rumors about him. But I know one thing for sure - he is mad. End of story.
The old pharaoh? I keep on hearing rumours about him, but I do not know if they are true.
<whispers> It is said his son, the present pharaoh, killed him and turned him into some ghastly undead!"

The palace lies to the south of the arena and to the west of the temple. Better stay clear of that place. If but half the things I have heard about it are true this palace is not a place for the living anymore.
Ah yes, the arena. I do not really know what's going on there, because I have never seen it myself. However, I often hear strange noises from there, cheers and jeers and sometimes pityful screams.
That temple is very old, and for centuries it used to be a place of worship and of contemplation. Now that the priests there are fanatic followers of the pharaoh this is no longer a holy place.
The concept of ascension is central to the pharaoh's creed. I am not sure I really understand it, but apparently it has to do with transformation to undeath. Nice, isn't it?
Ah yes - I recognise that. According to the pharaoh that is a living being's soul.
According to the pharaoh's teachings this is the total of a living being's memories and personal experiences.
In the pharaoh's creed, this is what the physical body is called.
Tose damn scavengers! I detest them. When I was stumbling through the desert, all blind and desperate, they followed me around. ...
They watched my every step, waiting for me to give up and die. But I never did. Damn vermin! You'll have to eat somebody else!

Yes, I know him. He is an Efreet trader. I met him often during my travels, and even though there was no real sympathy we had a certain mutual respect for each other. But all that changed when he found out I had dealings with the Marid.
Iknow that name. He is a Marid. This djinn is one of the best smiths ever to live. You should see the scimitars he makes - hard as titanium yet light as a desert breeze. ...
I kept on trying to get the Marid to sell one to me, but they never did. Too bad - I could have made a fortune.
Cursed be that djinn! It was him who blinded me, and I bet casting me out into the Kha'labal was his idea, too. Believe me, I would try to kill him if only I could.

A Marid trader. I have often had dealings with him. He drove me mad because he never accepted any haggling, but then he never ever tried to trick me. He was not really a trader at heart, I suppose. He was more of a monk or maybe a preacher.
H is a cook - a djinn cook. A weird guy. Always used to ask me to procure some strange kind of ingredient or other for him. ...
He made me laugh. Can you imagine what that looks like - a djinn wearing an enormous chef hat?
I know that name. He is a Marid, right? I have met him once. He seemed pretty important.
Farewell, stranger. May Uman the Wise guide your steps in this treacherous land.
pages.title: Melchior

pages.name: Budrik
npc_lines: Hiho, Hiho Jogador.
I am the foreman of this mine.
My name is Budrik Deepdigger, son of Earth, from the Molten Rock.
Precisely 9:02 pm, young one.
We understand the ways of the earth like nobody else does.
In the deeper mines we discover some nasty beasts now and then.
This is no funhouse. Leave the miners and their drilling-worms alone and get out! We have already enough trouble without you.
The Horned Fox is leading his bandits in sneak attacks and raids on us.
A minotaur they threw out at Mintwallin. He must have some kind of hideout nearby.
The hideout of the Horned Fox is probably a dangerous if not lethal place for the unexperienced ones.
This is no funhouse. Leave the miners and their drilling-worms alone and get out! We have already enough trouble without you.
Bye, bye.
pages.title: Budrik

pages.name: The Crone
npc_lines: Be greeted, Jogador... mortal.
Once I was Vashresamun's favourite handmaid. But I have fallen from grace and now I'm exiled from her tomb.
Her tomb is sealed and can only be entered with a certain melody.
I mourn the dark day I was exiled from her tomb.
Vashresamun erased the memory of the tune from my mind, I only remember its name: The Secret of the Rose Garden.
Good bye.
pages.title: The Crone

pages.name: Emperor Kruzak
npc_lines: Hiho, may Fire and Earth bless you, my child.
Well, I am Emperor Kruzak Dustbeard, son of Fire and Earth, second only to the gods, jawoll.
Well, I'm the emperor of the dwarfs. It's my duty to protect my folk and to see that justice is done.
Well, I'm the emperor of the dwarfs and the oldest living dwarf, jawoll!
Well, I'm fine, the last centuries have been good to me, jawoll.
Well, isn't it reward enough to talk to the emperor of all dwarfs?
Well, only a dead enemy is a good enemy.
Well, you'd better ask the general.
Well, after some centuries I stopped to worry about time anymore.
Well, if you wander the world with open eyes, you will see the quests without asking.
Well, what do you expect kings to sell?
Well, our people need no castle, our home IS a fortress.
Well, there are a lot of dungeons in the lands, waiting to be explored by the daring ones.
Well, we dwarfs produced some of the greatest heroes of all times.
Well, it's up to the younger ones to slay the beasts that roam the lands and the tunnels.
Well, well, well, the godblade. A myth? Perhaps. Even in my youth, it was only a legend.
Well, I don't think our southern allies have agents in our town.
Well, all dwarfs could be considered citizens. We are brothers and sisters in fire and earth..
Well, the Axes of Vengeance were troublemakers even when they were few. Their reckless ways and boasting sadly impressed a lot of the young and easily gullible. ...
Stories of their mostly made-up exploits and lies lured some into their embrace, but it was not until the blight that they became popular and a threat thanks to their leader, Jarok Bilespit.

Well, Jarok Bilespit was a mercenary. He did many questionable things for money. Especially dealing with non-dwarfs, although he usually was the first to express their disgust for them, when not taking their money, of course. ...
He gathered around him a number of drunkards and bullie’s of the worst sort, and founded the Axes of Vengeance fellowship, which was rather his private gang than a true fellowship. ...
They were usually travelling on contract, doing questionable missions and only returned to Kazordoon to boast about their made-up exploits and to spend their ill-begotten money with both hands. ...
This impressed certain people and gained him an undeserved reputation as a daring hero. ...

Though no week they were in town passed without one of them getting imprisoned for brawls, threats and destruction of property, especially younger dwarfs thought it would be cool to be one of them, and if not respected, then at least be feared. ...

When the blight struck, his easy explanations and pointless accusations stroke a cord in the minds of several individuals. I admit we did not see this coming and let him spread his phrases in the city. ...
We had other things to do and did not want more unrest by arresting some popular figure. With our attention elsewhere, Bilespit took advantage of the desperate and lured them into his ranks. ...
He was never the subtle type though, so it became quite clear what unspeakable treason he planed. ...

When he led his bunch of mercenaries and several drunks as some kind of meat-shield to dethrone me, we were prepared. We planned to take Bilespit down first to minimize casualties, but things got out of hand and there were many deaths on both sides. ...

With the order to keep presumably innocent casualties low, my guards fought very restricted, which could have led to their losing the battle. So we had to change orders to reduce our own casualties, and the fight turned very bloody and nasty. ...
Rumours spread through the city and others who thought they sympathized with Bilespit's cause joined the battles. ...
Still, we tried to keep casualties low; and as soon as we took certain strategic positions and gained the upper hand, most of the rebellious forces escaped. ...
Now they are hiding in the mine: Most of those mines are old and depleted of ore. They are overrun by all sorts of creatures such as the Lost. ...

So it made not much sense to send in troops that could not efficiently use their numbers and combat training in brawls within winding and narrow tunnels. We had to sent in troops to fight the advancing lost, though.
Well, our mines have been invaded by a basilisk. We trapped him with a cave in. The hero that could bring me the body of the beast will get a great reward.
But of course after the blight we have other problems down there, like the lost and the renegades.
Well, you claim there is another dwarven city called Beregar? Could that be the city of the ancient tribe?!?
Well, like all dwarfs we worship earth and fire. As you know, our tribe is closer connected to the element of earth. It is said that the other tribe prefers the element of fire.

Well, there is an old poem that is known by every dwarven child. It tells a story about the God Wars and the early years of Tibia. There have been two big dwarven tribes, but then a conflict arose. ...

This conflict caused one of the tribes to leave their birthplace and to find themselves a new home. Not in my wildest dreams I would have believed that this poem could contain some truth. You should try to find it.

Well, it must have been written by someone of the Kazordoon tribe as there hasn't been any contact to the other tribe since the day we parted. I doubt you'll find a written copy of it here as it has been passed on by word of mouth. ...
Maybe you find someone who tells you the poem. I for myself don't have time to tell you a children's poem. By the beard of my father, I'm the emperor, jawoll!
Well, our race is very hot-blooded, bullheaded, and also proud. The real cause is unknown but I can imagine how it happened.
Well, more than 150 years ago, my father lost his beard overnight. Thereupon, he resigned from his leadership after hundreds of years of supreme ruling.
Well, the blight was a great disaster. It hit us completely unprepared. ...

Given the severity of the disaster, we can be glad we handled it that well. Still, it weakened our defences, and by chance or sinister plans our enemies took it as an opportunity to hit us even harder. ...
In the midst of recovering from the blight and relocating resources, the trouble in the mines began. First with rampaging creatures and then came the Lost. ...
With resources bound there, even here in Kazordoon an enemy rose his ugly head ... and this head wore a dwarfen beard. Our own people, lead by the Axe of Vengeance fellowship.
Well, the gods handed the lands over to the younger races, but my people will leave this word in dignity.
Well, go and see the wonders of our cities for yourself.
Well we are at peace with Carlin and Thais.
Well, it is a colony of this human king.
Well, order is of great importance. Life has to follow rules, so do we.
Well, chaos is the ancient enemy. Dwarfs bring order to the world and give things shape. We are enemies of chaos.
Well, justice is a difficult thing. Can one be just to everybody at once, and if not, to whom should he be just?
Well, good and evil will fight each other for all eternity.
<sigh> Well, it saddens me to see what can become of a dwarf. They are truly lost. They are not ours any more, even if their ancestors once might have been. ...
Their dwarfish traits though make them fearsome fighters and the number in which their masters have bred them makes them a threat for anyone. ...
The worst thing is, if their masters did not seemingly consider the gnomes their major enemies, we would probably face even fiercer attacks. ...

Now the Lost are roaming the mines, and are still numerous and powerful enough to pose a threat. Meanwhile, we are regrouping and reorganizing in the hopes that we will be better prepared when the time of another assault comes.
Well, we use all stocked resources of finest metal to craft weapons and armor, we train new warriors and spellcasters every day. ...
We give battle training to each citizen to enable them to better defend themselves and to form militia units in case of emergency. And we call in old favours and allies.
Well, the High Paladin is a woman that deserves respect. I admired most Elanes I met in my life.
Well, Durin is one of the celestial paladins, messenger of the gods. He's the protector of the dwarven race.
Well, we are prepared even for him.
Well, we don't fear them. They seem more occupied with the humans anyway.
WAAAH! Don't mention that beast! It was after the bones of our ancestors, last time King Tibianus visited us!
Well, they are not as bad as one might think.
Well, we don't fear them. They seem more occupied with the humans anyway.
Well, we honor Father Earth and Mother Fire. Some of us even follow the teachings of additional gods.
Well, we have almost no druids in our town. If need arises we can call for them from Carlin.
Well, dwarfish knights are feared by our enemies in the whole world.
Well, we have some crossbowmen in our army but rely more on our knights.
Well, the sorcerers are followers of the elemental powers.
Farewell, Jogador, my child!
pages.title: Emperor Kruzak

pages.name: Etzel
npc_lines: Hiho, Jogador. <cough>
I am der dwarfish mastermage. I am keeper of the secrets of magic.
My name is Etzel Fireworker, <cough> son of fire, of the Molten Rocks.
Sorry, only sorcerers are able to comprehend my spells.
It's precisely 0:00 pm now.
Sorcery is not for the lazy or the impatient.
Take care out there, young one. <cough>
pages.title: Etzel

pages.name: Humgolf
npc_lines: Player, good day .. or night, whatever.
Home of the worms, home of my people, too.
The worm does not care about gods, why should I?
I am chief rotwormtamer of Kazordoon. I sell rotworms and buy meat and tasty, fresh rats for my worms.
Can't say I like it much.
I am Humgolf Molesight, Son of Earth, from the Molten Rock.
What by the worm are you talking about?.
More nice beneath this noisy green surface.
Time does not matter to a dwarf who understands the ways of the worm.
Unwormish creatures they are.
They should remember old dwarfish rotworm tactics. Think like a worm and the battle is almost won.
That guy is a monster! I despise rotworm killers.
Silly fairy tale.
A true enemy of the worms.
They are so cute and so intelligent.
I am not allowed to sell worms to people without a formular 007 license to drill or a 0815 artist license.
It's a special license for artists. It was only used once as I sold a white worm to Frietsiek and Yor.
Where earth is giving, fire is taking. That's the way of the elements.
They have an understanding of worms.
GO AWAY! I heard they think of replacing worms with machines. That is an OUTRAGE!
Hotheads.
They are not worth to be mentioned.
They are not cute and not intelligent.
I like the mines best.
The mountain seems tasty as far as my worms are concerned.
Always chatting. How can someone talk that much?
Thinks she's to good to talk to rotwormtamers.
Does a worm need spells to work his kind of magic? I do neither.
His tavern is too crowded and too bright for a dwarf with taste like me.
Poor guy, has lost his drilling license for drinking.
Don't like the way she looks at my worms.
We are trading now and then. Fine dwarf he is.
The emperor should spend more money on rotworm husbandry.
If he'd live today he'd be a rotwormtamer like me.
Don't like the way she looks at my worms.
Gold is one of the things my worms can unearth.
Bye
pages.title: Humgolf

pages.name: Isimov
npc_lines: Hiho Jogador and greetings my child!
The gods abandoned us, we abandoned the gods. That's it, no big deal I tell ya, jawoll.
I am the master of the hall of the ancients.
The burial chamber of our ancestors. All of the firstborn of our race are there .. all but Durin.
Life is easy to understand, you have birth, you have death. Simple stuff, even elves could grasp the concept.
My name is Isimov Dustbearer, Son of Fire and Earth, from the Molten Rock.
You are too young for quests, jawoll.
A world of dangers, a world of wonders.
I think it's the fourth age of the yellow flame, isn't it?
Only another nuisance.
Bah, squirrels, hedgehogs, rabbits, elves ... who cares.
<sighs> A bunch of kids playing war. May the elements help us.
I must admit there have been worse generals in the years before, jawoll.
Ahhh! Whan I was a little dwarf I was on a quest to find it. I was almost literally digging up the ghostlands for it and now only one thing is sure: It must be elsewere, jawoll.
I have seen many of his type coming and going. He will fall and anotherone will take his place.
Strange, are they still around? Well, give them one or two hundred years and they are gone again, jawoll.
They whorship the elemental forces of earth.
It's warm, it's useful, we use it. We decide when or how, jawoll.
Gives us food and shelter, quite useful isn't it?
Ah yes, the first born. He became a higher entity to protect us. His mortal remains were buried at a remote spot where only pilgrims disturb their peace now and then.
The last haven for dwarfenkind. Our last hope for our survival.
This mountain is as old as the world. The first dwarfs were born here.
Bezil and Nezil are typical profiteers. Fine new breed of dwarfs we raised, pah.
Bezil and Nezil are typical profiteers. Fine new breed of dwarfs we raised, pah.
Could become a great warrior one day. Still needs to learn so much.
Etzel, good old Etzel. I was his tutor long ago. Now he's running a guild ... they grow so fast ... so fast, jawoll.
Isn't that the kid that took over the Jolly Axeman tavern? Far too young for such a job, but did anyone ask me? No!
What a hasty fellow. Can't be healthy to live in such a hurry, jawoll.
How could she marry this Jimbin? I mean, they are kids! Know nothing about life and stuff. Couldn't they wait at least hundred years or so?
Has hardly a beard and already forgotten the traditions of his ancestors. Modern techniques ... almost like one of these technomancers.
The emperor resides far above us in the upper caves. Sometimes I wonder if it's good that the emperor is that much away from the temples.
Take care, Jogador!
pages.title: Isimov

pages.name: Jimbin
npc_lines: Talking to me, Jogador?
Welcome to the Jolly Axeman, have a good time, Jogador!
I supply the army with dwarfish beer to keep morals high.
The general is a fine man. Can drink as much as he wants and still is sober.
The cookbook? It belongs to Maryza. I think she has a few copies for sale.
I'm runing the Jolly Axeman together with my wife Maryza.
The king orders huge amounts of mushroombeer for festivities.
I am Jimbin Luckythroat, son of Earth, from the Molten Rock.
The Tibia our race was born into was even more fierce than the world you young ones know.
It is about 0:00 pm.
Actually I belive it's more than a taverntale.
Hah! He never dares to trespass our realm.
Silly town. Alcohol is forbidden there and elves visit this town quite often, what certainly suggests nothing good about a town, jawoll.
Bah! Humans, can't stand a drink, jawoll.
She's a fine cook; likes it bloddy, though. Humans call her Bloody Mary, but don't mention that to her if you're smart.
Oh well, many hidden places of ancient times appear seemingly out of nowhere in these times.
Come back if you enjoyed my tavern, if not ... well, get eaten by a dragon, jawoll.
pages.title: Jimbin

pages.name: Kawill
npc_lines: Welcome Jogador! May earth protect you!
The gods are treacherous and vain. They want to use us like they did in the past. Only the elements can be trusted, because all they want is for nature to run its set course.
I am the great geomancer of dwarvenkind.
We investigate the will of the earth. It is our duty to make sure things to work in their natural way.
Life is born by earth and fed by earth.
I am Kawill Marbleeye, Son of Earth, from the Molten Rock.
There's nothing I need, better ask others.
Nice world in general. It's a shame there is so much water ruining the general impression.
Time is not of importance.
May the earth swallow them all!
Our fortresses are strong and easy to defend. Any aggressor will be smashed by our armies. Most intruders will not manage to pass the colossus.
He finally made his peace with his own heart.
Ah, a weapon to be feared by man, beast and god alike, jawoll. He who wields it will be both blessed and cursed at the same time.
The day will come when he finally bites the dust.
By using the powers of fire and earth we forced the river that once wound its way through the big old one in other directions, and created our home.
Bezil and Nezil have pawn and equpiment shop with an amazing stock.
The first knight of dwarvenkind is a fine woman.
I fear the sorcerers focus on the destructive forces of fire. They forget about the protection earth could provide.
He is a jolly fellow and one of the oldest dwarves alive.
He is a fine smith and his armour may save your neck one day.
She is a fine cook, jawoll.
Uzgod is a blacksmith and understands the ways of his element well.
The emperor has rarely visited the temple district in the last years. He should care more about spirituality then about politics. Jawoll.
The celestial paladin, the protector of our race. The only divine being we care for and the only one who still cares for dwarfs.
Where earth is giving, fire is taking. That is the way of the elements.
The lifegiving earth protects us, feeds us and takes us home after death.
The mountain we live in is called the big old one. It's the mountain of mountains, and it isand like a friend and protector to our race.
Earth under your feet, Jogador!
pages.title: Kawill

pages.name: Kroox
npc_lines: Welcome to Kroox Quality Armor, Jogador!
I sell best armor in land. My armor save you life. Better buy much.
I sell chain armor, brass armor, and plate armor. What you need?
My name is Kroox Shieldbearer, son of Earth, from the Molten Rock.
I offer armor, helmets, legs, and shields.
It's 0:00 am now.
Ask in the shop next tunnel about that.
Foreigners not welcome in mines. An evil basilisk rob our deeper mines.
Much fun you can have in dungeons. Much battle and much gold, jawoll!
You not be afraid, here you be save.
Good bye. Come back soon.
pages.title: Kroox

pages.name: Maryza
npc_lines: Talking to me?
Welcome to the Jolly Axeman, Jogador. Have a good time!
I'm the cook of the Jolly Axeman.
Don't like these upper cave guys.
I am Maryza Firehand, daughter of Earth, from the Molten Rock.
We don't care much about outsiders anymore.
To busy, ask my husband.
Would slice a dragon or two for steaks if i'd get it.
Heard that's what the humans call one of their boggiemen.
Don't like it, has an elfish touch, ye know?
Puny town for puny guys.
I am so proud of him. In drinking, he's second only to our mighty general.
A fine drinker and strategist. Wastes his skill with these idiots of the army. What a shame.
We could better feed some dragons instead of these fools.
He loved my dragonsteaks. Heard he died by a cave in while fighting drags in the Plains of Havoc.
I sell normal and brown bread, meat, ham, cookies, rolls, and cheese made of mushrooms.
Yeah, bye.
pages.title: Maryza

pages.name: Nezil
npc_lines: Equipment and general goods here at our shop!
Uhm, me or my sis', Jogador?
Hiho Jogador, Nezil at your service. We sell equipment of all kinds.
We sell equipment of all kinds. If there's anything you need, ask me for a trade.
As you can see, we offer quite a lot of stuff, such as torches, shovels and the like. Ask me for a trade to have a look.
I'm Nezil Whetstone, son of Fire of the Savage Axes. I and my sis' Bezil are selling stuff, ye' know?
She's my sis'.
I think it's about horas. If you bought a watch, you'd know for sure.
I was thinking about a poem as a slogan for my shop but it's not ready for a big audience, yet.
I will give you 5 gold for every empty vial. Ok?
Sorry, visit the Jolly Axeman tavern for that.
Of course, just browse through my wares. By the way, there's a deposit of 5 gold on empty vials.
Good bye, Jogador.
pages.title: Nezil

pages.name: Pydar
npc_lines: Be greeted Jogador! I can smell the scent of a phoenix on you!
The ways of the gods are imprehensible to mortals. On the other hand, the elements are raw forces and can be understood and tamed.
I am the head pyromancer of Kazordoon.
My name is Pydar Firefist, Son of Fire, from the Savage Axes.
Ask around. There's a lot to do, jawoll.
That is our world.
It's the fourth age of the yellow flame.
May the great flame devour them all!
Life feeds on fire and ultimately fire will feed on life.
Our strong fortifications allow our armies to defend Kazordoon against any threat.
He is the fiercest axe fighter of our times and a fine strategist.
A weapon too powerful to be wielded by mortals. It has to be returned to the fire which gave birth to it.
If he ever dares enter Kazordoon I will gladly dump him into the lava. Tthe sacred flame shall bring justice upon him.
Our city was founded in ancient times. Abandoned by the gods we once fought for, we created a secure haven for our people.
This mountain is said to be the oldest in the world. It is the place where fire and earth meet and separate at the same time.
Bezil and Nezil are buying and selling equipment of all kinds.
She is the first knight of Kazordoon. She is responsible for teaching our young warriors how to handle an axe.
Etzel is a true master of the elements. He is a role-model for our youngsters, jawoll.
He and his wife are running the Jolly Axeman tavern.
He is a smith. If you are looking for exquisite weapons and armour just talk to him.
She and her husband are running the Jolly Axeman tavern.
Uzgod is a weaponsmith just like those in the old legends.
Though we are through with the so-called gods, Durin, the first dwarf to aquire divine powers of his own, is considered a protector of our race.
Unlike the gods, the elements don't use mortals as toys, A skilled mind can understand and even control them to some extent.
The ways of the gods are imprehensible to mortals. On the other hand, the elements are raw forces and can be understood and tamed.
May the fire in your heart never die, Jogador!
pages.title: Pydar

pages.name: Rapanaio
npc_lines: Psht! Not that loud! Evil lurks everywhere. It's after me!
I am an inventor and sage. I have pledged my life to fighting evil wherever it raises it's ugly head. It's hard work and you have to get your hands dirty, but someone has to do it.
My name is top secret!
Nooooo! Who blew my cover? I hope you are not in league with the forces of evil!

Evil lurks everywhere. It only takes some ignorant or cowardly people to turn their heads away once too often for it to spread its ugly seeds. I, however, am constantly vigilant and always prepared. ...
I hunt out the signs of evil everywhere. Even in the face of scorn and ridicule, I will not hide my head in the sand and I will be ready to fight!
Ignorance is evil's most potent ally. The servants of evil are plotting to keep us ignorant and poke ridicule at those who come too close to the truth.
It is my calling to root out evil in all its forms and uphold the vigilant fight. It is a lonely fight, an unending fight, but someone has to do it! ...
I scour ancient texts and collect rumours in taverns in order to track the machinations of evil. ...
Often odd occurrences are overlooked by the public as strange coincidences or fate, but those who know what to look for see the footprints of evil in history.

When I found that ancient text, warning of the Isle of Evil, I tried to tell the world about it. But the forces of evil discovered my plans! They made people assume it was just another tale for children. ...

THEY distributed a book of children's bedtime stories with a copy of the text in it to undermine my message! Their despicable ruse worked and they made a laughing stock of me! Of course I knew it was a plot to discredit me. ...
On the other hand, it was obvious that THEY now knew about me and the text I possessed. I went into hiding in fear of my life! THEY have tried to assassinate me! I must be constantly vigilant!
You'll find it in one of my chests. It's only a copy of course. The original is safely hidden! As much as THEY claim it's only a children's tale I know it's the truth.
Bah, THEY forged a children's book that made my source material look like some part of it. Of course it is an evil plot to prevent me from locating the isle and slaying its dark master. ...
Or rather, sending some other hero who will fight the ultimate evil in its own lair on my behalf. Someone has to stay and fight the fight on the mainland, of course.
Evil follows a distinct pattern. It is nasty, plans to rule the world, discredits its enemies, is fond of cunning death traps and rambling monologues, ...
it can only be vanquished by someone who completes a series of quests for some odd quest giver and it loves to have a lair, usually some sort of dungeon.
Scientists have no idea why the servants of evil are so fond of dungeons. But every evil mastermind worth his salt strives to own one. It is where it accomodates its minions and hoards its treasures.

Evil masterminds are served by all kinds of lesser evil beings. Such minions are usually no match for a hero, so they come in great numbers to counterbalance their lack of skill. Some minions are more capable. ...

They often serve as some kind of overseer or enforcer of evil and guard the mastermind's lair. Such minions are a particular challenge for a hero, but the rewards and loot for slaying them in battle are great!
I assume it is some kind of cosmic balance. When a hero slays a minion of evil the cosmic balance grants him some kind of reward. This often comes in the form of treasure. ...
Sometimes it's gold, sometimes it's a special weapon or piece of armor. Often an evil mastermind employs overseers for its hordes who guard parts of its dungeon. ...

These overseers are often in possession of high quality items that are the stuff of legend. The cosmic balance grants such items to the victorious hero so he can slay even more powerful minions of evil.
Call it what you like. I call it cosmic balance. It's like a natural law. It is the force that inspires evil beings to build lairs and dungeons, inspires it to gather armies of minions and so on. ...
It is the only rational way to explain such strange behaviour.
That heroes are rewarded with loot is down to the just nature of the cosmic balance. This is why even the most insignificant killer rat carries gold. ...

This, by the way, is proof positive that rats are evil minions, or else they would not carry gold. Loot is usually in the form of gold, but occasionally it also comes in the form of equipment and weapons. ...
Why else do dragons bother to carry armour and weapons when the beast itself is a killing machine with no use for such trinkets? It is of course cosmic balance! There is simply no other explanation!
My life is no longer safe. The first attempt on my life was at a party thrown by a fellow inventor. THEY put poison in one of the twenty pints of beer I drank that night. ...
The following morning I was close to death. Only my strong dwarven constitution stood between me and the grim reaper that day. ...
In their next attempt, assassins tinkered with the stairs in front of my favourite tavern. When I was leaving the tavern after a night with my friends I tripped and fell, nearly breaking my neck! ...
Only my catlike reflexes saved my life that time. Well, my reflexes and my beard that absorbed some of the force of the fall. ...
Other attempts on my life followed! Like the object that was hurled at me while I was singing and dancing on the bar while at a party. ...
And the list goes on and on. I know that I am in grave danger and I will not lie to you about the danger you will be in when THEY learn about you.

THEY are the servants of evil. THEY are everywhere and could be anyone. In fact, it has crossed my mind that most of THEM don't know who THEY are. Uhm, well, I mean THEY don't even know each other. The lure of evil is powerful. ...
Most people are not as strong as you and me and easily give in to the lure of wealth and power that evil promises. ...
Uhm, what was that flicker in your eyes? Well, anyway, Evil recruits its minions from all weak willed creatures so you can't be sure who is your enemy. ...
I advise you to be cautious. Better safe than sorry. Or dead.
It is my calling to root out evil in all its forms and uphold the vigilant fight. It is a lonely fight, an unending fight, but someone has to do it! ...
I scour ancient texts and collect rumours in taverns in order to track the machinations of evil. ...
Often odd occurrences are overlooked by the public as strange coincidences or fate, but those who know what to look for see the footprints of evil in history.
<lowers his voice> Sorry, that information is strictly classified. THEY might capture and torture you to find out what you know.
It is my calling to root out evil in all its forms and uphold the vigilant fight. It is a lonely fight, an unending fight, but someone has to do it! ...
I scour ancient texts and collect rumours in taverns in order to track the machinations of evil. ...
Often odd occurrences are overlooked by the public as strange coincidences or fate, but those who know what to look for see the footprints of evil in history.
You have no idea how many people laughed at me when I warned them of the Isle of Evil.
Psht, not that loud! But as your memory is so short, I will tell you of my researches once again! ...

After constructing an evil-o-meter I set about finding places where evil was concentrated. It reacted as expected to places of great evil like the Ghostlands, the Plains of Havoc and the Edron ruins. ...

But then it found somewhere new. My surprise knew no bounds when it showed a remote isle previously thought to be uninhabited. I am sure that something evil lurks there. Some unspeakable horror waiting to kill and devour unsuspecting travellers. ...
I could not let that happen! So I did some research and as I was about to give up I stumbled upon an ancient text that told of the Isle of Evil! ...
Immediately, the nature of the threat I had discovered became alarmingly clear! All I needed was a hero and some transport. But would they listen?! NO! They laughed at me. ...
Well, that was where you stepped in. Now we have joined forces to save the world!
Take care and watch your back, Jogador.
I am not important! Only the mission is what counts.
Hm, so you want another trip to that accursed isle?
Don't forget that THEY are after us, Jogador.
Time to leave this unfriendly place, eh? So are you ready to depart?
Take care, Jogador.
pages.title: Rapanaio

pages.name: Talphion
npc_lines: HIHOOOO Jogador! <waves> PLEASE DON'T INTERRUPT ME FOR TOO LONG IN MY JOB!
ONE DAY I'LL CREATE A CLOCK FOR THE COLOSSUS!
WHERE SHOULD I HOP?
I HAVE NO TIME FOR A GAME!
CAN'T TELL MUCH ABOUT IT. I SELDOM GET OUT OF HERE, I'M A BUSY DWARF.
WHAT?
WHO'S DOOMED?
THAT'S THE NAME OF THIS MOUNTAIN!
JUST A BUNCH OF BONES.
NICE PIECE OF WORK. WOULD BE MORE FUN IF IT COULD MOVE AROUND... WE HAVE PLANS...
AT LEAST HE'S SMART ENOUGH TO LEAVE US ALONE, SO THERE'S HOPE FOR HIM.
LOVELY, BUT PREJUDICED LIKE MOST DWARFS ARE.
WE COULD TEACH HIM MUCH IF HE ONLY LISTENED.
KNIGHTS DO NOT HAVE THE BRAINS TO EVEN UNDERSTAND WHAT WE ARE OFFERING THEM.
WE COULD MAKE MACHINES WHICH WOULD ENABLE HIM TO DO HIS WORK IN HALF THE TIME.
HIS BREWERY SAVED OUR DAY MORE THAN ONCE.
BEZIL AND NEZIL ARE RUNNING A SHOP.
WHO NEEDS MAGIC? PAH!
SUCH A FOOL, WITH SOME MORE RESOURCES, I COULD BUILD FOR HIM WAR MACHINES BEYOND HIS WILDEST DREAMS! <laughs insanely>
BRING ME THE SCREWDRIVER OF KURIK AND I WILL REWARD YOU WITH A STEAM-POWERED SPIKE SWORD!
NICE RESOURCE FOR OUR MACHINES, BUT NO NEED TO MAKE A BIG DEAL ABOUT IT, JAWOLL!
SORRY, BUT EARTH MEANS NOTHING TO ME THAN DUST AND MUD.
I'M SURE HE WOULD BE SMART ENOUGH TO SEE THE CHANCES WE PROVIDE FOR ALL DWARFS.
GODS? WHO NEEDS GODS IF WE CAN PRODUCE THE CORRECT MACHINE FOR EVERY OCCASION?
OLD FOOLS, TOO MUCH CONCERNED ABOUT TRADITION.
WE ARE THE FUTURE. WE WILL BECOME A MAJOR POWER IN DWARVEN SOCIETY SOON! THEY WILL SEE, THEY WILL ALL SEE! WE HAVE SO MUCH TO OFFER! <chuckles and rolls his eyes>
THE MOST SOPHISTICATED ITEMS THAT PEOPLE BUY ARE CROSSBOWS.
NO, I DON'T NEED ANY SHELVES!
LET THEM COME, I'M WORKING ON A LITTLE SURPRISE FOR THEM! <chuckles madly>
A PROMISING RACE, SOME OF THEM ACTUALLY ADMIRE MECHANICS.
WHAT HIVE?
HEY! HOW DID YOU LEARN ABOUT OUR SECRET PLANT?
YOU CAN BECOME A CITIZEN IN THE HALL OF THE ANCIENTS.
ONE DAY OUR MACHINES WILL CHANGE THE ARMY'S STRUCTURE DRASTICALLY, JAWOLL!
OLD FASHIONED BUTTER KNIFE! IF THEY LET ME, I WOULD CREATE WEAPONS THAT LEVEL ENTIRE CITIES!
DONATIONS ARE ALWAYS WELCOME!
ASK JIMBIN ABOUT HIS BREWS, NOT ME!
I'M AN ENGINEER, NOT A DOCTOR!
I COULDN'T CARE LESS ABOUT THEM.
NO, DON'T TURN OFF THE LIGHT.
I BET I COULD BUILD A MACHINE TO SHRED HIM INTO PIECES!
YOU CAN'T HANDLE MOST OF OUR STUFF, BUT I COULD SELL YOU SOME CROSSBOWS.
WHOM YOU ARE CALLING A WHELP, YOU CHEEKY MONKEY!
YEAH, GO AWAY!
pages.title: Talphion

pages.name: Tezila
npc_lines: Hiho, Jogador. Come in and look. But don't touch the exhibits, jawoll!
I am a jeweller. Maybe you want to have a look at my wonderful offers. I also exchange money.
You can purchase our fine dwarfish wares like wedding rings, golden amulets, and ruby necklaces.
You can buy and sell small diamonds, sapphires, rubies, emeralds, and amethysts.
I have white and black pearls you can buy, but you can also sell me some.
I am Tezila Gemcutter, daughter of Fire, from the Savage Axes.
I can sell you glittering gems, precious pearls or some ... uhm ... jolly jewels.
We exchange gold, platinum and crystal coins.
It's 9:30 am.
I am suspicious of these magic gems. Better you ask some mages about this.
Good bye.
pages.title: Tezila

pages.name: Tulf
npc_lines: Hiho! <mumbles>
I am the captain of the emperor's personal bodyguards.
We keep up law and order here, though the boys would rather need some practice like taking care for the trouble in the mines.
The mines aren't meant for foreigners. The miners there have enough troubles.
The mines are raided again and again by the bandits of The Horned Fox.
It's a renegade minotaur who has a hidden lair somewhere near our mines.
The lair of the Horned Fox is surely well guarded and even better hidden.
My name is Tulf Beardweaver, son of Earth, from the Dragoneaters.
It's 0:00 am right now.
If you go to a dwarfs' city, do as the dwarfs do.
I despise the habit to challenge the prisoners of Dwarcatra or provoke the boys in the mines.
Sorry, I'm on duty!
Yeah, bye.
pages.title: Tulf

pages.name: Ashtamor
npc_lines: Welcome, Jogador, wanderer between the worlds.
I consider myself as a guide, a guardian over the souls who transcend the border to another world.
The essence of life. Source of your very self. While the body is in space and time, the soul exists in time only.
It's time now, but the true question is: How much time is left?
What is a name worth in your eyes? And more important: Does the choice of your name decide your further fate? Perhaps we will never know.
You come to this world naked, and leave it this way, so there's no need to hold back your money, especially not in a place like Venore.
What help might I offer you except guidance? Would you like me to help you transcend the border to the afterlife?
Kings, queens ... I've seen them come and go. Everything fades, even the glory and wealth of the richest.
Birth might be the beginning but death is certainly not the end.
Does it mean anything than losing your weak physical shell? And isn't the true power in the universe rather mental than physical?
Oh yes, monsters can grant you a passage to the afterlife also, but it's not a comfortable trip. <chuckles>
Once you leave your mortal shell, you'll become one with the gods.
Is the mind an emination of body, or the body an invention by the mind?
I'm offering vases and amphoras, the perfect vessel for all kinds of dusty remains. Ask me for a trade if you're interested.
Life is nothing but a pre-stage for the eternity of death.
No one really knows what awaits us beyond. Although there are some old stories about the Netherworld.
It is the place where the dead end up. Some sages believe, that it is located below the world of the living. ....

Personally, I think it rather lies within another dimension so that terms like above or beneath are inappropriate to describe it. There are some rumours that the descent to the Netherworld is difficult yet possible for those still living.
The purging force of fire ... it helps to free souls and its smoke helps them to find their way to another world.
Yes, it's a wise idea not to leave the choice of your future vessel to chance. Have a look. (Abre o trade do NPC)
See you again ... sooner or later, more or less alive.
pages.title: Ashtamor

pages.name: Asrak
npc_lines: I welcome you, Jogador!
I am the overseer of the pits and the trainer of the gladiators.
Those wannabe fighters are weak and most of them are unable to comprehend a higher concept like the Mooh'Tah.
I teach worthy warriors the way of the knight.
I am known as Asrak the Ironhoof.
It is 0:00 pm.
I pledge no allegiance to any king, be it human or minotaurean.
Your human army might be big, but without skills. They are only sheep to be slaughtered.
Sorry, I only teach spells to knights and paladins.
The dungeons of your desires and fears are the only ones you really should fear and those you really have to conquer.
By them we were imbued with the rage that almost costed our existence. By them we were used as pawns in wars that were not ours.
Inferior creatures of rage, driven by their primitive urges. Only worthy to be noticed to test one's skills.
To rely on magic is like to cheat fate. All cheaters will find their just punishment one day, and so will he.
If it's truly a weapon to slay gods it might be worth to be sought for.
The city pays me well and those undisciplined gladiators need my skills and guidance badly.
The city is only a shadow of what we could have accomplished without that curse of rage that the gods bestowed upon us.
In the ancient wars we lost much because of the rage. The one good thing is we lost our trust in the gods, too.
Rage is the legacy of Brog, the beast. To overcome it is our primal goal. The Mooh'Tah is our only hope of salvation and perfection.
The Mooh'Tah teaches us control. It provides you with weapon, armor, and shield. It teaches you harmony and focus.
There is an elegant harmony in every thing done right. If you feel the harmony of an action you can sing its song.
Each harmonic action has it own song. If you can sing it, you are in harmony with that action. This is where the minotaurean battlesongs come from.
Each Mooh'Tah master focuses his skills on the harmony of battle. He is one with the song that he's singing with his voice or at least his heart.
Make your will your weapon, and your enemies will perish.
Courage is the only armor that shields you against rage and fear, the greatest dangers you will have to face.
Your confidence shall be your shield. Nothing can penetrate that defence. No emotion will let you lose your focus.
May your path be as straight as an arrow.
I welcome you, Jogador!
May your path be as straight as an arrow.
pages.title: Asrak

pages.name: Boozer
npc_lines: Welcome to the Hard Rock Racing Track, Jogador.
I am the bartender here at the racing track.
Just call me Boozer. Everyone does that.
No clue, girl.
The king is far away, so who cares?
People from all over Tibia come here to buy, sell, gamble, and get drunk until they puke.
I guess they just have not met the right man yet.
Heard about that women there. Must visit that wenches someday.
Good customers.
If you like that Thais that much just go there.
I can offer you food and drinks. Get anything else somewhere else and don't bother me.
So you are looking for food? We have cookies, bread, cheese, ham, and meat.
You'll be back.
pages.title: Boozer

pages.name: Dabui
npc_lines: Daraman's blessings! Welcome to Darashia.
I am a protector of the people of Darashia.
The evil of Drefia is strong these days.
Our leader is enlightened by Daraman, thrice praised be his name!
This city is lovely Darashia, pearl of Darama.
Darashia is the heart of Darama. In the northeast, across the Devourer, there is the dark pyramid. In the west, across the Plague Spike, are the cursed ruins of Drefia.
The great desert devoured many of the first pilgrims. We learned the ways of the devourer and thus conquered it.
The minotaurs took shelter in the ancient pyramid, which our people avoid for the dark powers that might be present there.
Mountain of Poison, Scorpions Rock, it's known by many names. It's to the west of Darashia.
The ruins of Drefia in the far west are the hideout of the vile necromancer cult that once corrupted this city.
Darama led his people on a pilgrimage to the holy lands of Darama to escape temptations and distractions.
The ancient prophet brought our people here from a place long forgotten.
Go to the bazaar in the middle of the town.
Ishina sells amulets and other valuables at the market place!
This information is confidential.
Take this! (burning effect, 5 turnos de 10 hitpoints)
Daraman's blessings!
pages.title: Dabui

pages.name: Kasmir
npc_lines: May Daraman enlighten you Jogador!
I am a chosen of Daraman.
Kasmir Ibn Darasir.
The caliph is heavily involved in the affairs in the world, but one has to make this sacrifice for the welfare of all.
Daraman travelled the world and learned the secrets of the ancients. At last he learned the secret of ascension and founded his philosophy.
This land is harsh and challenging. It's far away from temptations and delusions. Here Daraman's people can concentrate on themselves.
Daraman had a vision that all mortals are able to ascend to heaven, becoming celestial beings.
By enhancing one's soul a mortal can ascend to heaven. If you are not prepared to ascend, you are bound to this world by reincarnation.
If your soul is not strong and purified, you will not ascend but return to life on death, even losing strength in the process.
Life is divine though not without flaws.
Daraman led his followers to this promised land to follow his teachings. It was named Darama after him later.
Undeath is even worse than reincarnation. Those souls are nothing but a rotting mockery of a soul on the path of ascension.
Your quest should be to prepare your soul for ascension.
The bonemaster is strong in the ruins of Drefia. There you can test the braveness of your soul ... or lose it to his minions.
The soul was made by the gods and therefore is divine. So by enhancing its divinity it can become more like the image of its creators.
Banor is the very proof that ascension is possible.
The gods are in heaven and far away. You are here. So concentrate on your soul and take care for it on your own.
Your greed for such items can easily corrupt your soul.
My grandfather knew him and he always lowered his voice when he spoke his name. I don't know many things about this strange fellow but ...
...wait, now I remember. My grandfather said something about an amulet with great power. Rumour says that it shattered and that one of the four pieces killed Koshei. ...
Actually noone knows if that is true or not.
His soul is corrupted beyond any hope for ascension.
They are soulless and therefore without true power in the end.
Go to the bazaar if you are interested in worldly wealth.
Uman is the positive aspect of magic. His powers flow through each Tibian, making us his children.
Zathroth is the corruptor of souls who does not want mortals to ascend and become more like him.
Fardos is the creator. It was his work that we possess divine souls.
Don't look for news when you don't know the past.
The world is only a portal the gods created to allow our ascension to heaven.
Brog's hot blood is in our veins, tempting us and distracting us from improvement of our souls.
Kirok is called the mad one. He gifted us with the creativity to achive our ascension.
Toth is the final judge. The unworthy are condemened to reincarnation.
Suon is the sun. He watches our ascension.
Fafnar is a test for our endurance and dilligence.
Crunor is the force of life and part of our all being.
Nornur is the mysterious god of fate. Daraman taught us that he is the judge who allows ascension.
Bastesh is the goddess of the seas, and deep as the see is our soul, indeed.
Sula is the raw force of water.
Air is without true mind and meaning.
Thank you, I'm fine and my soul is strong.
Do you want to make a donation?
May Daraman guide your quest for ascension.
Do you whish to confess your sins?
So what does trouble your soul, pilgrim?
Meditate on that and try harder to improve soul.
Good bye, Jogador. May Daraman's all-seeing eye watch your travels!
pages.title: Kasmir

pages.name: Kazzan
npc_lines: Feel welcome in the lands of the children of the enlightened Daraman, Jogador.
I am Kazzan Ibn Gadral, caliph of Darama.
I am the caliph of the children of Daraman. It is my privilege and mission to ensure their safety.
I am fine, thank you.
A caliph is a leader of his people, just like a king.
Daraman led our ancestors to the continent Darashia to live a life of simplicity and meditation.
There is nothing you can do for me right now but thank you for offering your help.
Tibianus is the shepherd of the lost souls of the so called Thaian empire.
Our people are well prepared to fight for their land and their souls.
The necromancers of Drefia fell under the wrath of the djinns once. If they challenge us again, they might lose more than a city.
When the djinns destroyed the better part of the unholy town in their wrath, the brotherhood hid like worms in the sand.
The Brotherhood of Bones came here fleeing some war on the continent. They corrupted the settlers of the Thaian colony with ease.
The minotaurs are another test we have to endure. They inhabit the pyramid which is taboo for our people, as Daraman taught us.
Daraman knew our souls might get corrupted by the things hidden there.
The gods are powerful but it's ultimately up to us to work on our souls' ascension.
We have lost contact with the dwarven people of Kazordoon.
We keep in touch with the queen, but we have not taken sides in the conflict of Carlin and Thais ... yet.
Once a djinn claimed to have seen it in a dream. I guess it's just that, some dream of a supernatural creature.
May your soul flourish, Player.
May your soul flourish.
pages.title: Kazzan

pages.name: Morun
npc_lines: Daraman's blessings! Welcome to Darashia.
This city is lovely Darashia, pearl of Darama.
Darashia is the heart of Darama. In the northeast, across the Devourer, there is the dark pyramid. In the west, across the Plague Spike, are the cursed ruins of Drefia.
The great desert devoured many of the first pilgrims. We learned the ways of the devourer and thus conquered it.
The minotaurs took shelter in the ancient pyramid, which our people avoid for the dark powers that might be present there.
Mountain of Poison, Scorpions Rock, it's known by many names. It's to the west of Darashia.
The ruins of Drefia in the far west are the hideout of the vile necromancer cult that once corrupted this city.
I am a protector of the people of Darashia.
The evil of Drefia is strong these days.
This information is confidential.
Go to the bazaar in the middle of the town.
