Nothing I would talk to you about.
Buy a watch.
I was guest at his castle on my visits to Thais.
Do I look as if I'd fraternize with such people?
A disgusting person indeed.
I am not interested in tales only kids belive in.
Isn't it a wonderful town?
A city full of disgusting people with ill manners.
I plan to visit this city one day.
The world is a place of barbarianism.
Good bye, Jogador, please come back soon.
pages.title: Sandra

pages.name: Telas
npc_lines: I'm so close.
So much to be done.
If I could only get that one to work.
We did it!
Incredible!
I can't believe it! Success at last!
Hello! Sorry I’m a bit busy.
As you know I’m a scientist, specialising in the field of creating golems. That is my mission so to say.
My name is Telas.
I guess, my job is my passion.
I think a king’s job should be to keep things running and not to pursue his own ambitions.

He is a genius when it comes to theories. He has written some of the greatest scientific texts I have ever read. Although not all of his suppositions are based on empirical evidence, some of his theories are revolutionary. ...
He should be more than happy to have some of his theories put into practice and I have no doubt that he will share his research with me quite willingly.
The city itself deeply affects me for many different reasons. …
For one, the wonders and the technology to be found in the city fill me with awe. …
And then I am filled with sadness for the decline of their technology and the loss of their knowledge that is palpable everywhere in the city.
Kazordoon is the capital city of the dwarves. It is hidden in a huge mountain on the route between Thais and Ab'Dendriel. I think there is a street or a path that takes you there from Thais. ...
As soon as you cross a huge bridge to the north and find yourself standing in front of a mountain, you're there.
In my opinion, Thais is far too political. All that kingdom and empire stuff serves to entertain the upper classes. …
It doesn’t change anything for the common man and is all about accumulating power and wealth for the powerful and wealthy.
Although the city of Carlin has some rivalry with Thais it can be reached from most major harbours by ship.
I came here to study at the academy for a while. …
I grew curious about the northern ruins and for a long time hoped that I’d be allowed to lead an expedition there. …
This came to a halt of course when the criminals and fallen knights took over the ruins. …
Since then I have shifted my focus to creating golems.
The northern ruins are probably the remains of one of the extinct races that preceded humanity during the God Wars …
There are numerous ruins all over the world that tell the silent tales of the rise and the fall of their architects. …
For instance, adventurers discovered subterranean ruins in the Ghostlands. …
The remains of the bonelord civilisation are one of the most notable remnants of such ancient races. …
All over the world you can still see the black pyramids which were typical bonelord structures. Some are still inhabited by a small population of bonelords. …
We can only estimate how many races might been wiped out without a trace. …
However, the ruins in the north are certainly one such relic of the past and that is probably why those renegade knights went there. …
Whoever finds out how to unlock their secrets and make use of them stands to gain considerable wealth and power.
The academy holds a wealth of knowledge in many fields. Unfortunately, magic has become far too important in my opinion. …
It’s a pity that other fields are shunned by researchers. …
It makes it quite hard for anyone interested in different fields of science to find appropriate reference material. …
The magicians who lock themselves up in ivory towers, far removed from the ordinary people, is an apt metaphor for how distanced magic has become from everyday life. …
I think a breakthrough coming from the area of independent research might serve as a wake up call for the academy’s board.
My main laboratory in the cellar is stuffed with sophisticated gadgets and gizmos. …
I don’t like having visitors down there and honestly, I don’t find the time to tidy it up, so it’s quite a mess. …
When we manage to assemble a golem I will invite you downstairs for the activation. …
It would be a shame to let you assist me and then exclude you from the moment itself.
The Yalahari are a race of contrasts. Though admittedly it’s probably better to regard the Yalahari of the past and the Yalahari of today as two completely different races. …
In the past the Yalahari were reclusive but brilliant. You can still see all the marvels of their city and all the knowledge in different fields of science that they must have possessed. …
Then, at some point in their history something must have happened, causing a shift in their society. …
Science stopped progressing and was gradually forgotten. No new wonders were built and the old ones slowly fell into decay. …
It seems that over the course of generations, the Yalahari increasingly lost touch with their own inventions. …
We can only speculate what might have happened. …
I, for my part, think that scientific knowledge was probably exclusive to a small group of Yalaharian elite. …
I have seen with my own eyes that one quarter of their city was devastated by an explosion and another sunk into the sea because of an earthquake. …
My theory is that the scientific elite perished along with one of these quarters, thus leading to the downfall of the Yalaharian civilisation. …
The Yalahari of today are quite reclusive and don’t like visitors in their inner sanctum – as I learnt the hard way. …
I used a lot of influence and wealth to gain admittance to their inner city. Unfortunately, they quickly cast me out because they found me too curious.
The term golem is a bit too broad to describe the actual diversity of these beings. …
Roughly speaking, most golems are based on an element which is concentrated until it gains a semblance of sentience. …
The element that is concentrated can be changed to get a different kind of golem. …
The ‘element’ does not necessarily have to be earth, fire, water or air but, purely theoretically, concentrations of other matter are possible. …
It is still under debate whether most of the other concentrations of matter could be traced back to one of the core elements. …
Since this science is still in its infancy there is a lot to be specified and researched.
Because elves look similar to humans, it is easy to forget that they are completely different. …
They are their own race with their own morals and values. …
Most misunderstandings between humans and elves arise from the fact that humans just assume that elves think like themselves. …
However, the elves are not a scientifically inclined people, so there is little in their culture that would interest me personally. …
Some colleagues of mine at the academy took an interest in elven sorcery though. You might ask there for more information.
I honestly admire the dwarfs for their craftsmanship. Admittedly, they are a bit tight lipped about their secrets, but who can blame them for that? ...
Their technomancers are special though. I would love to converse with them about science and mechanics but as an outsider there is little chance for me to learn anything from them. ...
Luckily, there are some rare exceptions to the rule. But that's a different story.
The bonelords are a race fighting extinction. …
Unlike other elder races they have proved themselves to be more resilient, but as far as I can tell, they are only postponing the inevitable. …

How ironical it is that the bonelords refuse to admit that they are on the brink of extinction. You would have thought that their skills in necromancy would have given them some insight into their situation.
So far, science has recognized four elements: water, fire, air and earth. It is speculated that there are more elements in existence, such as lightning, magic, life and unlife.
Many people actually mean magic when they say ‘science’. But there are so many other fields to be explored. …
The more mundane sciences hold many secrets of their own and can be profoundly rewarding for a researcher.
Earth is a rather basic element for golem construction. Earth golems can be created without much effort and are quite common.
Water can sometimes be concentrated by using its ice form as a base. …
Although concentrating water is not as problematic as with most of the other elements, it is difficult to keep the concentrated water stable for an extended period of time.
The brute force of fire makes it dangerous to contain and difficult to concentrate without risk of an explosion.
Air is elusive and the techniques to concentrate it are exceptionatly complicated.
Lightning is still an unexplained phenomenon. Some assume it is an element in its own right, others claim it is the product of opposing elements. …
Others suggest it belongs to the element of magic and finally there are those who claim that lightning is a Godly element.
Magic is a fascinating field, both in terms of theory and practice. Unfortunately, with all the manpower and resources that have been put into that area, other areas have been somewhat neglected …

When confronted with a problem people have grown used to turning to magic for a solution. We’ll never know how many inventions might have been discovered if there weren’t already a spell for everything.
Life, as an element, is rather speculative. …
Some argue that we are a form of concentrated life and therefore would qualify as life golems. …
This is an intriguing concept and when I am done with my current research I will probably give that a closer look.
Well there are necromantic golems. ...
That alone is seen as proof by many people although it is dangerously simplified. Still, this subject bears scientific analysis.
Spells have a tendency to make things easy. Too easy for my taste. People stop thinking for themselves if they have a spell for each and every occasion at hand. …
All the bookish knowledge of a studied master does not make up for the practical experience of an ordinary man who has to solve his problems by original thinking.
I admit I have little use for the Gods in my own life. I like to think that I make my own decisions. …
I really can’t understand devout believers who follow the doctrines of a God, or rather, his priests and subordinate their life to the agenda of some heavenly power. …
If the stories of the God Wars are true, then I am not sure I feel comfortable with the idea of being some kind of a weapon and not an individual.
Well, we all know that the Gods fight over creation. We’re supposed to help them in some way, aren’t we? …
I have to admit, I find it impossible to regard my life merely as a means to further that war for one side or the other. …
On the other hand, we should probably be thankful that we are not involved in an all out war. …
Still, I try to avoid dwelling on this. It is disturbing to be constantly faced with the possibility of war breaking out.
I have focused my research on the creation of golems. While this does involve a lot of magic, it also requires a wide range of knowledge in the other fields of science as well.
Necromancy is referred to as one of the dark arts. Even from a scientific point of view, I can’t deny that this holds a grain of truth. …
Through dabbling with necromancy, one is exposed to certain unhealthy thoughts that can easily corrupt a man. …
So I only study the theory behind the creation of necromantic golems. …
It is an interesting topic but, as I said, it requires some questionable assumptions and a willingness to cross certain boundaries a human shouldn’t ever cross for his own good.

After all this effort we have made it, my friend! I can’t figure out why the golem is behaving so strangely. I can only assume the experimental head was not completely indoctrinated with all the usual golem routines …
But that might even prove helpful. I will try to teach the golem what he needs to know, but it will take some time. Feel free to visit whenever you like if you want to hear about my progress. …
By the way, I could also need certain rare metals and crystals for my experiments. Just in case you have any of those I need, ask me for a trade to exchange them for good money!
Admittedly, I am at a bit of a loss as to specifying exactly what it is that we have created here. It is a functional golem and it is working. …
On the other hand, it seems odd and a bit self-preoccupied. It’s almost as if it had some kind of sentience. …
It’s even more of a marvel than I had hoped for! Absolutely fascinating! I will run a series of tests and .. and .. there is so much to be done. …
It seems my work has only just begun!
Seen any of those metals, stones or crystals? I’ll happily buy them! I also buy crystal pedestals.
Well you don’t have any, but in case you find some, let me know!
Good bye, Jogador.
pages.title: Telas

pages.name: Eliza
npc_lines: Welcome, Jogador. If you're interested in spells to support your party, I can be your teacher.
I'm sorry to tell you, but I'm no longer allowed to teach you spells due to my retirement.
I used to be a teacher for party spells. But these days are now over, since I can now finally retire.
My name is Eliza.
It's horas.
Well, the new spells we recently discovered could prove to be quite valuable. Time will tell.
The king is a quite impressive man. Even though his deeds are often criticised, I'm sure that he only wants the best for Tibia.
Talented magicians gather in these towers and work together in researching spells. That's why the most powerful spells are only taught in Edron.
I've only been to Thais once or twice. I prefer a quieter place to live and study.
I don't like the attitude of the women there. They are all a little trigger-happy, if you know what I mean.
People call me pessimistic, but I think this world will go down the drain sooner or later.
Having a party is a good thing. You can kill much stronger monsters than when you're on your own.
I have no idea, I’m sorry. You could ask Fiona or Zoltan, though.
Goodbye, Jogador.
pages.title: Eliza

pages.name: Gundralph
npc_lines: Utevo vis lux!
Oh, be welcome Jogador. You look like you're interested in the world of magic.
Sorry, but we had a slight restructuring of spell lessons in order to be able to focus better on one group of students. You should go and see whether Puffels and Zoltan are still teaching you spells.
I used to train young casters like you... but the magic flows differently now. You'll understand it sooner than later.
I used to be a teacher for some powerful spells.
They call me Gundralph.
I have heard nothing of intrest lately, sorry.
Let me see, it's horas.
How low can a sorcerer go.
An awesome weapon if it exists.
Unfortunately, I never met King Tibianus III in person.
They live in the castle to the west.
I see Thais as a lost course.
The world is so big and we have only so little time to travel.
Carlin is a fine place for druids.
Sciences are thriving on this isle.
Please ask the stationer in the west tower for that.
Goodbye, Jogador!
pages.title: Gundralph

pages.name: Puffels
npc_lines: Yeah, another fool disturbing me, what a joy.
Well, I used to teach some fools. However these day are now finally over! Where was the cheese wheel again?
Not really. Due to some new &#&$*# academy rules I'm not allowed to teach anyone now. Me! .. ah, whatever. Better than having to only teach knights, I tell you!
I am Magister Puffels, any problem with that?
I heard in Thais the new brand of cheese was... uhm...
Hugo? I heared it was an accident that created this beast.
I don't know more about it.
Sciences are thriving on this isle.
I don't care about some remote cities.
I was there once, almost died. The fools there mistook me for an ordinary rat, can you believe that!?
Bah, the whole Tibia can &#&$*# my #$&*!
I give nothing for kings, queens... or other people at all.
Fine army that is. Half of them have already deserted.
The day will come even he makes a fatal casting mistake... I know what I am talking about.
I have no use for such stuff.
Where might I hide a watch, you fool?
Whatever.
pages.title: Puffels

pages.name: Zoltan
npc_lines: Welcome Jogador, student of the arcane arts. I teach the fiercest spells available.
I was once a teacher of the most powerful spells in Tibia. That time has come to an end.
I was once a master of the arcane arts, but I've left the teaching behind. Nowadays I focus more an collecting wisdom and exploring the world we live in.
I am known in this world as Zoltan.
I have no time for chit chat.
It's horas.
You will need no weapon if you manipulate the essence of magic.
King Tibianus III was the founder of our academy.
They rely too much on their brawn instead of their brain.
Thais is a place of barbary.
There is still much left to be explored in this world.
Carlin's druids waste the influence they have in enviromentalism.
Sciences are thriving on this isle.
He is an old and wise man that has seen a lot of Tibia. He is also one of the best magicians. Visit him on his little island.
You should visit Eremo on his little island. Just ask Pemaret on Cormaya for passage.
Yenny? Which Yenny? That is a common name.
Ah, Yenny the Gentle was one of the founders of the druid order called Crunor's Caress, that has been originated in her hometown Carlin.
I am quite busy, ask another time!
Don't bother me with that. Ask in the shops for it.
Orshabaal is one of the demon lords in service of the Ruthless Seven. His raids on our isle Edron are already legendary and usually end up with numerous casualties.
I see no reason to discuss this matter with you.
I see, you managed to reach Kharos, the harbinger isle, and discovered the gates to Ferumbras' citadel, and now you are here full of questions. Are you ready to listen?
So know that destroying the mortal shell of the being called Ferumbras was the best we were able to achieve with our combined efforts in the past. ...
He was destroyed not only once but several times. Eventually we were able to figure out the secret of his seeming immortality. ...
On one of the most remote islands of the Shattered Isles, he built a citadel with demonic aid right around a powerful magical nexus. ...

The only reason for the whole complex was to establish a point of return into our world. Whenever he is slain, his soul retreats to some demonic dimension to regain enough strength to re-enter the world. ...
We were not able to destroy his citadel, this unholy construct. To make matters worse, the nexus makes it easy for demons of all kind to pass into our world. ...
The best thing we could do was to seal the citadel and to install a device that will alarm us whenever Ferumbras tries to re-enter our world. ...
We grant heroes like you the permission to pass our seals and enter Ferumbras' citadel. ...

Just ask for the permission if you are ready to go there. Be warned that the citadel is no holiday place though. You will encounter large amounts of demons and traps that scare off most adventurers. ...
On the other hand, WHEN Ferumbras re-enters the world we need heroes like you to face him on his very own ground before he can escape. ...
His return is not very likely but it can happen each and every day. If you should manage to defeat him, bring a proof of his death here and you will be rewarded.

The attuning to our seals is a costly process and it will grant you access to the citadel ONLY ONCE. Each time you want to enter, you will need a new attuning. Are you willing to pay 500 gold pieces to become attuned to the seal of the citadel?
SO BE IT!
Use your knowledge wisely, Jogador.
pages.title: Zoltan

pages.name: Albert
npc_lines: Welcome in my humble hut, Jogador. If you are heavily wounded or poisoned, I can heal you.
I'm a healer.
My Name is Albert Fibulanian.
You aren't looking really bad. Sorry, I can't help you.
Tibia is a world big enough for everyone. I wish people would realize that.
The sinful city of Thais is a monument of corruption and murder. I am glad I left for Edron and thank the gods every day for this isle.
The gods of good take care of us.
The king does much to enhance the life of his people, but he could do more.
I dream of times which see no need for armies or warriors.
The fallen one is a perfect example where evil leads us to.
It's only another instrument of pain and destruction.
I have only news about weather, taxes, and harvests. I heared nothing that might interest a traveller like you.
I healed his wounds, but nothing can heal his soul after the betrayal of some of his knightly brethren.
Oh better ask the knights about that issue. I know only little about that tragic story. Some knights betrayed their order and joined some sinister cult in the northern ruins.
Another victim of his own ambitions. I mourn for his soul.

My family used to live on the isle of Fibula. At this time it wasn't overrun by soldiers of fortune. Later, I was sent to Thais to learn the art of healing, while my family was amongst the first settlers of Edron.
Now, it is horas.
Good bye, Jogador!
pages.title: Albert

pages.name: Amanda
npc_lines: Welcome to the temple of Banor's blood Jogador. If you are heavily wounded or poisoned, I can heal you.
I'm a humble nun that came to Edron to help.
I'm sister Amanda.
Sorry, I rarely have time to chat.
Now, it is horas.
He is a pawn of evil.
Only a being loyal to Banor will wield this blade.
Our king is a religious man - a shining example.
Our army lives in accordance with the ideals of the god Banor.
Edron is in grave danger. I arrived here too late to witness the events myself, but I will share everything with you that I've heard ...
A false priestess seduced some knights to abandon their noble cause and to free some prisoners. Then they headed to some ruins in the North where they practice a dark cult and consort with demons.
The ruins are probably older than humankind. We have to assume it's a place of dark power. The recent appearances of the fiend Orshabaal hint that the Ruthless Seven are somehow involved.
The taint he spreads on the land is unbearable. This creature has to be destroyed once and for all.
I'm not sure if they even exist. Demons usually don't form such partnerships.
It takes heroes to defeat demons!
Heroes gain equipment and experience by fulfilling dangerous quests.
That's our world.
We can expect little help from Thais in these troubled days. We need some heroes to help us with these sinister things going on here.
They created the world and all life on it.
Farewell, Jogador!
pages.title: Amanda

pages.name: Avar Tar
npc_lines: Greetings, traveller Player!
I'm Avar Tar, slayer of monsters, saviour of princesses, and defender of the weak.
I'm a professional hero.
I think I'm the greatest hero in Tibia, but my humility forbids me to make an issue out of it.
I've seen it all and done it all ... at least twice.
It's 9:45 am right now.
I fought him several times, sometimes he killed me, sometimes I killed him. I'd say we are even right now, but I'm getting better and more powerful each day.
I am sure it's hidden in a vault of the Nightmare Knights beneath the Plains of Havoc. I'm planning an expedition to go there and to rout out the Ruthless Seven, but I have to save the world first.
Oh come on. Let the noobs take care of them. Call me if they are fourteen or so.
I'm on a quest for the Thaian king ... as usual.
Ah, my trusty old sword. I left it on Rookgaard years ago when I left for the main continent.
Rookgaard is full of memories of my first heroic accomplishments ...
I heard that after all these years, the Minotaur Mage there refuses to leave his room as he is still afraid of me.
If I had time, I would restore peace in this once proud city, but there's too much to do before I can start that quest.
I saved the women there once or twice.
I had to master the magic of all 4 vocations for one of the quests.
There is a great evil lurking beneath this isle ... and beneath the Plains of Havoc, and in the ancient necropolis, and beneath the Ghostlands ... well basically everywhere.
Demons know and fear my name! It's not always easy to be a hero, you know?
See you later, Player.
pages.title: Avar Tar

pages.name: Captain Seahorse
npc_lines: Passages to Thais, Carlin, Ab'Dendriel, Venore, Port Hope, Ankrahmun, Liberty Bay, Oramond, Cormaya, Gray Island and Krailos.
Welcome on board, Sir Jogador. Where can I sail you today?

Where do you want to go? To Thais, Carlin, Ab'Dendriel, Venore, Port Hope, Ankrahmun, Liberty Bay or the isle Cormaya? I could also bring you to Gray Island, Oramond, Krailos - or to Travora - a place between the worlds.
I'm the captain of this sailing ship.
My name is Captain Seahorse from the Royal Tibia Line.
The Royal Tibia Line connects all seaside towns of Tibia.
This is Edron. Where do you want to go?
I'm sorry, but we don't serve the routes to the Ice Islands.
We would like to welcome you on board.
We can transport everything you want.
I'm not sailing there. This route is afflicted by a ghost ship! However, I heard that Captain Fearless sails there from Venore.
The only cities on Darama I travel to are Ankrahmun, and Port Hope.
Many people who sailed to Darashia never returned because they were attacked by a ghost ship! I'll never sail there!
Good bye. Recommend us if you were satisfied with our service.
pages.title: Captain Seahorse

pages.name: Chief Grarkharok
npc_lines: Grarkharok make new tribe here! Me Chief now!
Me like to throw rocks, me also like frogs! Yumyum!
Grarkharok's bestest troll tribe! Yeee, good name!
Me Chief Grarkharok! No do nothing!
Me be Grarkharok. No me name Job!
Me be Grarkharok!!
Me tribe in production! Only need troll lady!
Found lady for Grarkharok?!? Must be good-looking, hairy lady, y’know! Go find!!
Me no nothing! Need all money to make Grarkharok tribe!
Grarkharok like BOOM, BOOM sound! Go mountain, push rock and BOOM!
Like it?? Hope troll lady also like it!
Me no like human. Need quiet to make tribe! Only need troll lady!
Yeye, me stole chief club from Fragratosh, hrhrhrh! Now make me own tribe!
Fragratosh stupid. He chief of me old tribe. No frogs, no snakes, no smashing humans with rocks. Booooooring tribe! Now me make own tribe!!
Grarkharok already say everything! Not want talk! Go away!
Hrhrhrhr! Me no fear of human! Me Chief Grarkharok!!
You have what want! Go go, find lady so be Grarkharok tribe!!
Have dead frog for Grarkharok??
Have tasty snake for Grarkharok??
You say troll speak!! Hmmm, sound like south tribe! You know Ingortrak ?? He chief of big tribe in jungle! Good chief he is!
I Tem?!?!? No know! Maybe YOU Tem?
Tribe Grarkharok will rules Tibia! Me only need troll lady, then start tribe!
Grarkharok destroy human cave down hill! Human away, my mission done, hrhrhrhrhr!
Grarkharok no listen to talk of stinky human! Lalalalalala! Like song? Grarkharok made!
Huh?? No understand!
Grarkharok be chief!
pages.title: Chief Grarkharok

pages.name: Daniel Steelsoul
npc_lines: Greetings and Banor with you, Jogador!
I am Sir Daniel Steelsoul of the Sacred Order of Banor's Blood.
I am the governor of this isle, Edron, and grandmaster of the Knights of Banor's Blood.
The castle was built on elder foundations we found on this isle.
Evil challenges the forces of good in any shape. Be it the claws of vicious monsters or the seductive dark secrets of rotten power.
With this weapon in my hand, I would teach the servants of darkness the true meaning of the word fear.
We cleansed the south of any major enemy, but watch out while travelling the north.
Are you suggesting I am corruptible?
Take this!
Look for Willard, our local blacksmith.
I belong to a sacred order and don't care about mundane politics.
With the Thaian army bound to other duties, our order was entrusted to secure the area. We defeated the evil minotaurs living right here and cleansed the isle of their unholy presence.
It is a peaceful isle next to Edron with a nice village. You should visit the wonderful garden there.
This isle is rumored to have been the home of a powerful ancient race which became extinct before the corpsewars. It was up to King Tibianus III to reclaim it for humanity and to found this colony.
Now and then a dwarf comes to this isle. Most behave secretive about their reason to come here. As far as I can tell, they are looking for some dwarfish artifact which was lost in ancient times.
He was my second in command. After learning about the forbidden ruins, he, the priestess Agaltha, and their followers freed the criminals we brought here as workers and headed to the north.
She was beautiful but seemed cold hearted. She spoke little to me, preferred the company of Kaine.
An ancient taboo forbids to enter the northern ruins.
We thought it was only superstition and no one bothered that Kaine and his friends went there to hunt servants of evil that might have hidden there. So we did not notice the dark cult they started.
We know only little about them. Kaine and his fallen knights were joined by criminals and remaining forces of darkness that escaped us. They were joined by some ominous dark monks.
We don't know if they came here or already hid in the ruins when we arrived. Maybe they seduced Kaine or Agaltha, maybe they were theirs for years.

After the treason of Kaine, we observe these mages closely. If even a knight falls prey to the seduction of the forbidden ruins, no one can tell how easy some of these mystics might betray his people.
The rotten cyclops worship the raging giant of hell.
Do not mention the name of the cursed one!
The army protects the Thaian realm. The order of the Knights of Banor's Blood supports them with all our skills.
We believe that the blood of Banor runs through the veins of all humans. Therefore, we are responsible to live up to Banors standards and not to stain his legacy with sinful acts.
Only those who live a life of bravery, honour, and piety may join our sacred order.
You may join the order of Banor's blood if you prove your honour.
The Order of the Falcon inhabited an impressive stronghold here in Edron. It lies dormant ever since the disappearance of the order and is unlikely to ever be used again. ...
Not many even go near the thing, especially during the night. They told stories about weird lights at the tower after midnight since I was a child. I never saw any myself, naturally.
I think this nun might be a bit young for this position, but I won't question the decisions of the church of Banor's Blood.
His spirit and blood are within us. Honour this fact or be cast into hell.
He and his men fought against Ferumbras somewhere in the north of this isle, long before there were even plans of a colony. Only old Ben returned alive from the battle, but his mind was broken.
Eremo is a very wise man. I visit him sometimes on his little island near Edron. Just ask a fisherman for a passage.
Pemaret is a fisherman on Cormaya.
A promising young fellow.
He searched something in the north of the isle years ago. Probably he needed something from the forbidden ruins. He was chased and fought by the troops of general Benjamin.
Harkath Bloodblade declined the governorship because he's needed more in Thais.
I hardly find the time to visit the tavern.
When he was young, Willard served in the royal army.
The minotaurs, though evil, were worthy opponents. After the treason of the man who is now known as Kaine Kinslayer, we lack the manpower to crush their cyclopean allies, too.
They live in an underground city, known as Cyclopolis in the north of the isle. Constantly forging weapons for the servants of darkness.

You could call her the protector of Grimvale. When she was a girl she lived in Edron with her parents, thus I know her from my days of childhood. Later she moved to Grimvale but now and again she used to visit Edron. ...
But lately I haven't seen her all too often. I guess the unsettling occurrences on Grimvale demand all of her attention.
Grimvale is a small island in the north-east of Edron. Its few inhabitants live quite out of the world but for a long time it was a peaceful place. However, this might have changed lately.

Rumour has it that some of the inhabitants are affected by were-sickness. And yes, I believe it. Not because I am of a facile nature, no. Rather because there are strange things happening right here on Edron that teach me better.

With each full moon monsters are roaming the woods. They look like badgers and foxes who are transforming into humans. Unfortunately it's the other way round: Peaceful citizens transform into feral beasts as soon as the moon is full.

Yes, recently we have a major problem here on Edron. Strange proceedings are troubling me as well as the common citizens. With each full moon, monsters are roaming the woods - monsters that we only knew from tales until now. ...
They look like badgers and foxes who are transforming into humans. Unfortunately, it's the other way round: Peaceful citizens transform into feral beasts as soon as the moon is full. ...

Some hunters even claim that they have spotted monstrous humanoid boars, wolves and bears. I know what is going on on Grimvale so I sent a messenger to Maeryn. She confirmed what I already feared: Those creatures are were-beasts. ...
The so-called Curse of the Full Moon is spreading and reached Edron. I asked Maeryn for help but she has plenty of trouble on Grimvale and can't leave the island. ...
Do you know something about this curse and - even more important - would you be willing to help us?

I'm very relieved to hear that. The most important thing right now is to cure the curse of as many affected people as possible. Maeryn already told me that the purple nightshade is able to revert the effects of lycanthropy. ...

We tried this but it worked only partially. Strangely, we were able to cure the people living outside the town in the more rural parts of Edron. But there are also some affected people in the town itself and the nightshade doesn't have any effect....
I'm neither a sage nor a magician. But I'm the one who is supposed to find a solution for this problem. Please pay a visit to the Magic Academy of Edron. Perhaps one of the mages there can help you.
I'm very happy that you could help the people of Cormaya. May Banor bless you. But I have one last request: The were-beasts are led by alpha leaders. ...

Please seek out the subterranean caves of the lycanthropes on Edron and Cormaya and kill the alpha leader of each kind of were-beast, five altogether. This should weaken them enough to hold them at bay for quite a while.
You defeated the five alpha leaders! Well done, this should weaken them enough to hold them at bay for quite a while. Please take this pendant in return, it may be of use for you. ...

The were-sickness won't disappear completely but it will be easier for us now. At least I hope so! Yesterday a travelling salesman told me that he spotted a feral creature in the Darama desert that looked like half man and half lion. ...
Banor grant that this is just unfounded gossip and that the curse didn't spread further. Well, I guess, we will find out soon. Edron, for the time being, is a safer place now, thanks to you.
Thank you again for your assistance, Jogador! The Curse of the Full Moon still exists on Edron. But thanks to your heroic deeds we can keep it within certain bounds. At least I hope so! ...

Yesterday a travelling salesman told me that he spotted a feral creature in the Darama desert that looked like half man and half lion. Banor grant that this is just unfounded gossip and that the curse didn't spread further. ...
Well, I guess, we will find out soon. Edron, for the time being, is a safer place now, thanks to you.
Lately I heard rumours about the curse. That it has spread to the Darama Desert and that the lions there could also be were-creatures. Do you want to get to the bottom of it?
Then please travel to Darashia and search for a man called Domizian. He lives in a house at the harbour. I know him for many years, he's a trustworthy friend. ...
I'm sure, he can tell you more about the curse in the Darama Desert.
PRAISE TO BANOR!
pages.title: Daniel Steelsoul

pages.name: Edron Guardsman
npc_lines: Move on. If you need help or have questions, talk to Sir Daniel Steelsoul south of here.
pages.title: Edron Guardsman

pages.name: Falk
npc_lines: LONG LIVE KING TIBIANUS! Welcome to the isle of Edron!
I'm the Edron harbour guard. I protect Edron castle and inform visitors about this building and Edron itself.
I'm Lieutenant Falk.
Sorry, that's confidential.
The mysterious isle has many secrets and sights outside the castle. The areas of interest are in the west, the southwest, the north, and the northwest.
The Edron castle is the home of many shops, a tavern, a bank, a depot, a post office and the temple of Banor's blood.
We all live under the benevolent guidance of our king.
The shops are on the eastern side of the castle. Upstairs you'll find a tailor, a blacksmith, and an equipment store.
I'm well prepared for my duty.
Visit the shopkeepers to buy their fine wares.
LONG LIVE THE KING!
The local army consists only of the Knights of Banor's Blood.
The tavern is called the Horn of Plenty, and it's located upstairs in the southwest corner of the castle.
You'll find the bank in the southwest of the castle. Look for Ebenizer, you can't miss him.
The post office, run by the lovely Chrystal is in the southwest corner of the castle, near the Royal Bank.
The temple can be found underground, in the southeast corner of the castle. There you can become a citizen of Edron.
There are rumours of orc buildings in the southeast. They say some daring fellows found a passage to this area in an old cavern beneath the Edron flats.
Don't even think about going there. Renegade Knights of Banor's Blood went there to unearth forbidden secrets in an ancient ruin.
In the north, there is an ancient city of cyclopses, called the cyclopolis. They are wary of us, but trade with servants of evil from any known race.
There are rumours of two tribes of minor monsters who battle each other for dominance over the area. Not worth to crawl the sewers to get there.
In the city there is a furniture store and a jeweller. The Noodles Academy and the cemetery are outside.
The Noodles Academy of the magic arts is in the east of Edron city.
Explore the isle and destroy any enemy forces encountered. The honor shall be your reward.
The cemetery is north of the hamlet of Stonehome, which is at the east coast, northeast of Edron city. The cemetary is rumoured to be haunted.
There are the Dogs of War, the Red Guards, and the Silver Guards.
LONG LIVE THE KING!
In the city there is a furniture store and a jeweller. The Noodles Academy and the cemetary are outside.
The cemetery is north of the hamlet of Stonehome, which is at the east coast, northeast of Edron city. The cemetary is rumoured to be haunted.
pages.title: Falk

pages.name: Milos
npc_lines: What a fascinating idea!
Oh hello. I hardly noticed you. I'm afraid I am a bit distracted at the moment.
I'm a magician and a theoretical scientist. That is, I am of course a real scientist, not a scientist in theory, but I concentrate more on theories than on practice. ...
What I mean is, I do more reading and corresponding with other scientists - not exactly the fast lane to fame and fortune, granted, but it satisfies my humble desires.
Theories are my lifeblood, so to speak. Practice doesn't interest me in the same way. To be honest, I am easily frightened and I lose heart quickly. Theories are more forgiving. ...

I feel more comfortable with numbers and formulas and such. I like the safety of a laboratory and taking my time to develop my ideas. And of course I like the company of books more than the company of men. Sorry, no offence meant.
My name is Milos. Milos of the Edron Academy. Nice to meet you.
He is a very enigmatic person. His wisdom is unrivaled and his intentions are good. Although some people occasionally complain that he only imparts the bare minimum of information that they need. ...
He always leaves you with the feeling that he knows much more than he is willing to tell. Some even claim he is a chosen of Uman.
He is a great and generous man. I owe him so much. I will never be able to even remotely make it up to him.

The academy is a place of learning. We could do with a bigger library, of course. If the White Raven Monastery weren't so far away I would consider going there for the privilege of seeing all those magnificent books. ...
But the cream of Tibian academics, professors and researchers are all based here, so we do have the greatest living knowledge base in the world.
The monastery contains the greatest collection of books in the known world. They own books from every field of knowledge, philosophy and art ...

As far as I am aware, there is not much order in the collection though. The monks are ony collectors of books. They unfortunately lack the skills to catalogue them. Even if they read them I doubt they would understand them. ...
This makes researching there somewhat tedious and time consuming, but if you ever have to research a topic I would suggest starting there.
I am still waiting for a good book about Yalahar. Preferably with some drawings. That would be so interesting.

Knowledge is essential to everything. How can anyone make a decision without knowledge? The more you know, the better you can decide. Our Academy is one of the world's greatest hoards of knowledge. ...
Another, especially in the fields of books is the White Raven Monastery. The single most knowledgeable person in Tibia is, in my opinion, the sage Edowir in the Whiteflower Temple.
Uman is the God of Knowledge who furthers society and stands for the greater good. He is the patron of research and progress.
Zathroth is represents the quest for knowledge in order to gain power. He stands for those who seek to gain knowledge regardless of its cost, and for progress for the sake of progress alone.

You have to distil the crimson nightshade first. You can use the alchemical devices in Sinclair's laboratory, here in the Academy. Then you have to add the silver and gold powder, in this order! At last you add the Shadow Bite Berries.

This is a very rare subspecies of the purple nightshade. It grows exclusively on the small island Grimvale, and even there it is anything but common. In fact, it is so rare, it didn't even have a scientific name as of yet. ...
So, with becoming modesty, I called it 'solanum coccinea'.

We scholars call it the were-sickness or the Curse of the Full Moon, but whether it is a disease or a curse is still unclear. Some claim it is similar to a contagious malady, others take the view that it is a curse in the classical magical sense.
Just have a look at my notes. The required components are listed there.
Most Tibian cultures have some knowledge about those straight lines that run across the landscape, connecting both, natural and sacred sites. Some also call them 'fairy paths' or 'spirit lines'. ...
As far as I know, in Zao they are called 'dragon lines'. Markers connecting the ley lines can be mounds, cairns, standing stones, stone circles, ponds, wells, shrines, temples or cross-roads.
If you have some gold or silver nuggets, grind them into dust. We have a gem grinder here in the Academy which you can use.
The metal has to be in an unprocessed state. Coins or jewellery won't do it. The best bet is to go to a mine and dig up some of the required metal. ...
Deep underneath the Venorean swamps are tunnels where you might find what you are searching for. But beware of the Corym there and be sure to take a pick with you!
I have read some reports about the Yalahari and they sound extremely interesting. Sadly, information about the Yalahari is rather rare due to the fact that they are so elusive.
I am more into theories then into practice but I have come up with several very solid theories that may be invaluable to Telas, if they work in practice ...

I would not go as far as to say that I have reinvented how golems can be constructed but I think some of my approaches are quite unique. Even by disproving some of my ideas Telas stands to gain some significant insights into his chosen field of study. ...
I am only too pleased that my theories are being applied in such a useful way!
A stone of insight! As theoretical scientist and magician I'm highly interested in researching this particular artefact. In exchange, I'd share some of my knowledge with you. ...
Would you like to trade a stone of insight for experiência experience?
Thank you! This is a great step for magical science.
Ah well. This matter was taken out of our hands for now. The inquisition insisted to control the collection of these stones and by royal decree they were granted the exclusive right to do so. ...
As a simple scientist I'm not in a position to question such decision, as hard as it might hit my researches. For now I can not trade any of the stones. You will have to wait for another opportunity.
Good bye.
pages.title: Milos

pages.name: Pino
npc_lines: Feel the wind in your hair during one of my carpet rides!
Greetings, traveller Jogador. Where do you want me to fly you?
I'm a carpet pilot. I can give you a passage to many places.
Pino at your service.
It's horas right now.
I can fly you to Darashia on Darama, to Svargrond on Hrodmir, to Kazordoon, to Zao, to the Femor Hills or to Issavi if you like. Where do you want to go?
What a wonderful world, especially if you look down on it.
Do you seek a ride to Darashia on Darama for 30 gold?
Do you seek a ride to Svargrond for 50 gold?
Do you seek a ride to Kazordoon, for 60 gold?
Do you seek a ride to Zao, near Farmine, for 50 gold?
Do you seek a ride to the Femor Hills for 50 gold?
You are probably talking about the FEMOR hills.
Do you seek a ride to Issavi for 90 gold?
Good bye!
pages.title: Pino

pages.name: Shoddy Beggar
npc_lines: What do you want? Listen to the old madman? If you have nothing to spare, leave me alone.
My name is... not of your concern.
Are you kidding me? Do I look like a... well, we'd better change the topic.
Must be about 11:38 am.
Tibianus? What is a king measured against a scientist? What is wealth measured against wisdom?
I thought this was the city of knowledge, arts and exploration. Instead I found this academy full of... *mumbles*
Ah, the sea of light... we are surrounded by it. It holds the secrets of our very existence, the meaning of - ah you wouldn't even understand.
Pah, he thinks he knows what holds the world together - in fact he's just as clueless as the rest of the academy. *mumbles*
I heard about the legend, but I don't know how much of it is actually true.
Yes, whatever.
pages.title: Shoddy Beggar

pages.name: Ortheus
npc_lines: What's your business here with the magicians, Jogador?
Hm, good question. Maybe old, wise man?
I'm used to being called old man. Simple as that.
I can't imagine a better place to live.
Though the city has seen better days, the quality of life is still much better than in most other cities.
I don't know what you're talking about.
Yes, it's a bit messy down there. Sorry.
Doesn't ring a bell.
He rarely comes here.
A man of the seas.
He used to visit me for a chat, but ever since that new tavern opened I haven't seen him much anymore.
He sometimes delivers fruit and vegetables to this quarter.
It'd be better for you to leave now.
Though the city has seen better days, the quality of life is still much better than in most other cities.
I can't imagine a better place to live
Whatever that's supposed to mean.
I don't have anything that I could give you as a reward. Guess you aren't so selfless after all, huh?
They try to protect the city and do a decent job. Well - no, a poor job, I mean a poor job.
You can bring me a mug of tea if you want to.
Have you actually brought me a mug of tea??
Good bye.
pages.title: Ortheus

pages.name: Tereban
npc_lines: Sigh.
Greetings, friend. Good you are showing up.
My family owns some land here as well as two ships. I have overseers for that though. This allows me to spend my time reading and dabbling in poetry. ...
But considering the circumstances right now, I'm just a troubled father with a mission too hard to accomplish for me.
My name is Tereban.
My sons are quite independent. Even though I had preferred that they stayed at home longer, they decided to leave to make their careers in the great guilds. ...

It was probably only for their best to start their training at an early age, but I miss them badly. I am sure they will become something great in their vocations, but I have always been proud of them anyway.
My wife was a high-ranking member of the Explorer Society. Some years ago her ship was lost in a storm. I still haven't given up to hope for her return, even though I know it is not rational.
My son Vestus trains to become a druid. He has a kind heart and great love for animals and nature, so it’s probably just .. uhm natural for him to become one. ...
He was always somewhat of a loner but as far as I heard he found quite a lot of like-minded friends among the other students and is quite happy.
Melvin has always been as curious as his mother. He shared her and my love for books but did neither like travels nor poetry. ...
He is so analytic and inquisitive. I have to admit there are times I cannot follow what he is talking about. He will become a great sorcerer.
Yelloran loved hunting already as a kid. He had a keen eye and quickly discarded what he called ‘kid bows’ to try out the real ones.
His first bow was almost twice as big as him and he hardly had the strength to pull its string at first. But that changed soon enough and now I hear he is one of the best marksmen in his class.
My son Tereman has always loved stories about brave knights rescuing beautiful princesses. Of all my sons he is probably the bravest, so it suits him well to become a knight.
He has always been so dedicated to become a great knight one day, I sometimes had to stop him so he would get some needed rest.
A sturdy shield is a knight's best friend. I want my son to be protected as good as possible. For the shield we need something that the dwarfs call 'old iron'. ...
You can find it in the deepest reaches of the dwarfish mines of Kazordoon but as far as I've heard, the dwarfs do not welcome visitors, so watch out. ....

We also need some scales of a dragon. The catch is, not any dragon will do. If the dragon is too old, its scales can't be treated by the craftsman, if it is too young, the scales will not provide the necessary protection. ...

The good thing is that the craftsman learnt about a dragon that lives in the caves somewhere north of Thais. For its unusual scales it is called Glitterscale. It sounded like you'd know when you see it.
The most crucial part of a rod are its enchantment. But I have taken care of that. The thing is that an enchantment has to meet certain conditions to work correctly. ...

So we need a special root that can be found under that ape city Banuta as the body of the rod and a special crystal. One was apparently buried in the tomb of some high-ranking official of Ankrahmun. ...
Although his tomb is hidden by the sand, it is rumoured to be somewhere east of the city.
For the bow we need some exquisite wood which can be found in one of the barbarian camps of Hrodmir. It seems the barbarians cut down the only useful tree there and hid its wood. ...

We also need a sinew. The craftsman insisted that only the sinew of an ancient wyvern named Heoni will be acceptable. You will find the beast in the mountain caves of Edron, along with others of its kind.
First we need some of the finest silk the world has to offer. Travel into the depths of the spider caves in Zao and look there for some suitable silk. ...
Then we need some spectral cloth. I fear the only place to find such a piece of cloth are the burial chambers of the Isle of the Kings, deep beneath the White Raven Monastery.
I'm not good enough to find a publisher but it is still fun to write poems for myself.
I like to keep my poems private.
Your bravery earned us this excellent sinew.
The wood you have found is just what we needed.
Thanks to your efforts we have a suitable piece of spectral cloth.
The silk you have brought me is exquisite indeed.
The crystal you have found is absolutely flawless. You did a great job indeed.
It is even recognisable for me that the root you gave me is filled with magic.
The iron that you’ve found will make an ideal base for a shield.
Only someone as daring as you could slay the beast to get the necessary scales.
I already told you everything I know.
I hired the finest craftsmen available to create the birthday presents for my sons.
It will be a great party with my sons, all their friends, and relatives that we haven’t seen here for several years.
I arranged the meal, some music, fireworks, and even jesters and acrobats. It will be a party people will still talk about in years.
I already told you everything I know.
Farewell.
pages.title: Tereban

pages.name: Ursula
npc_lines: Howdy Jogador. I'm a spell teacher of the Edron academy.
I am sorry, Jogador, I no longer teach any spells at all. Some of us spell trainer went into retirement together.
I used to teach some spells for paladins. Now I can finally focus more on experiemts and science.
I am Ursula.
I heard about things you never would believe. Please come back when I have more time to chat.
Sciences are thriving on this isle.
They should have been more careful with this town, before they lost it.
Ah, yes, I remember my time there, old Muriel teaching me the basics.
Isn't it a fine world we live in.
The king spent a lot of money for our library.
I would prefer an army of spellcasters, but they are ok.
Ah, come on, he can't be that poweful and evil as all say.
A myth born out of some knights' inferiority complex.
Sorry, I don't own a watch.
I'm sorry, but I don't have one. Ask Thomas in the west tower about that.
Bye, Jogador.
pages.title: Ursula

pages.name: Clyde
npc_lines: Sit down, have a drink and relax!
Greetings, dear customer. Have a drink and some food.
I’m your host, I run this tavern.
I’m Clyde, your host.
Sure, browse through my offers.
Food and drinks as much as you can pay for. If you like to see my offers, ask me for a trade.
Hm, we are widely known for the wood we export. But we are truly famous for the ivory of the elephant tusks.
Do you want beer, wine, lemonade, or water? Ask me for a trade to make your choice.
We offer cookies, bread, cheese, ham, and meat, as well as eggs and tomatoes. If you like to see my offers, ask me for a trade.
This forest is no ordinary forest. It’s more like a force of nature, like a river or even a storm.
The rumours I overheard did not mention this continent as one of its hiding places.
Don’t worry about the time. Take a seat, have a drink. Time runs differently in Port Hope.
This incarnation of evil seems to concentrate his efforts on Thais and its surroundings, but who knows what comes next into the mind of this madman?
I wish the king would be a bit more concerned about this colony. I’m convinced with a few more resources we could improve Port Hope a lot.
Sadly, Thais is far away and you will notice that in many places. You’ll find out about this yourself, so let’s talk about something else please.
I know only little about Carlin, and nobody cares about it here.
If I were you, I’d stay as far away from this town as possible. It is ruled by an undead abomination and its inhabitants worship death.
I was there quite often, using the flying carpet. It’s quite different from other towns I’ve seen, but surely worth a trip.
If you want to learn something about Kazordoon, you should talk to our local dwarfs.
It’s not always easy to deal with those Venorean tradesmen. I have to admit they don’t show any interest in my area of business. Just between you and me, my friend, sometimes they give me shivers.
When I started business here, I was hoping for a second Edron. I have not shed my hope, yet. After all, this place is called Port Hope, isn’t it?
It’s a continent full of extremes – the jungle in the humid West, and the desert in the dry East.
I’ve seen only little of this world. Probably you should tell me something about the world, and not the other way around.
Sadly it is next to nothing that I know about the elves and their city.
Sadly it is next to nothing that I know about the elves and their city.

The dworcs live in the South in an underground network consisting of caves. They use poisoned weapons and love to build all kind of traps. You don’t want to know the fate of those that have been trapped, believe me.
I wish the king would be a bit more concerned about this colony. I’m convinced with a few more resources we could improve Port Hope a lot.

There was a handful of dwarfs that came here when the colony was founded. They were looking for treasures and gold as far as I know. After some argument, a bunch of them left. They headed into the jungle and were never seen again.
The lizards are hostile to us. They probably see no big difference between us and the ape people.
They seem to live in the depth of the jungle in ruins that show the markings of the lizard folk. I wonder if they now try to conquer our city, too.
Good bye, do visit us again.
pages.title: Clyde

pages.name: Hairycles
npc_lines: Oh! Hello! Hello! Did not notice! So busy.
Me great wizard. Me great doctor of ape people. Me know many plants. Me old and me have seen many things.
We see many things and learning quick. Merlkin magic learn quick, quick. We just watch and learn. Sometimes we try and learn.
We be kongra, sibang and merlkin. Strange hairless ape people live in city called Port Hope.
Kongra verry strong. Kongra verry angry verry fast. Take care when kongra comes. Better climb on highest tree.
Sibang verry fast and funny. Sibang good gather food. Sibang know jungle well.
Merlkin we are. Merlkin verry wise, merlkin learn many things quick. Teach other apes things a lot. Making heal and making magic.
Jungle is dangerous. Jungle also provides us food. Take care when in jungle and safe you be.
You look for food and rest.
We see many things and learning quick. Merlkin magic learn quick, quick. We just watch and learn. Sometimes we try and learn.
Things not good now. Need helper to do mission for me people.
These are dire times for our people. Problems plenty are in this times. But me people not grant trust easy. Are you willing to prove you friend of ape people?
pages.title: Hairycles

pages.name: Wyrdin
npc_lines: <mumbles> If the semi-planar matter correlates with the mana enriched hyperflux ..
<mumbles> Typical - you can never find a hero when you need one!
<mumbles> So where was I again?
<mumbles> If I were to subtract the divergence of the supraplasmatic coefficient ..
<mumbles> The classic theorem of inductive regeneration disproves the assumption of parallel distortion of astral fluctuation ..
<mumbles> Could the bonelord language be the invention of some madman?
<mumbles> The curse algorithm of triplex shadowing has to be two times higher than an overcharged nanoquorx on the peripheral ..
Hello, what brings you here?
I'm responsible for compiling new knowledge for our academy. In this position I often assign missions to daring adventurers.
I'm Wyrdin, researcher and librarian.
It's horas right now.
There is still much that needs to be done before Edron can be called a peaceful place, and I'm convinced there are still many secrets hidden here that need to be unearthed.
The king is an avid supporter of science.
Thais is way too loud and distracting for carrying out decent research.
Sorry, this is not my area of expertise. I believe it is better to be quiet if you know nothing of what you are talking about.

The academy is the foremost facility of research and study in the kingdom. Nothing in the known world rivals the amount of knowledge we've accumulated here. Only the library of the White Raven Monastery comes close.
Good luck on your travels, Jogador.
pages.title: Wyrdin

pages.name: Rosemarie
npc_lines: Greetings and nature's blessing, traveller!
I'm Rosemarie the dryad, and just like my name is linked to flowers, my whole existence is connected to the life of plants.
It has its charm but the more plants I have around me the better I feel.
The elves found the perfect balance between living from the plants and living with the plants. They should be role models for every living being.
I'm here to celebrate life. I will stay with you mortals for a while. I exchange seeds, which you might have found on your adventures, for flowerpots with rare seedlings.
I prefer to stay outside of towns but this spot here is tolerable.
The bringer of life and fertility is worshipped by all dryads.
Dryads are the daughters of Crunor and the protectors of plant life. Sadly, most of my sisters are quite aggressive on their mission.
I accept every way of life but this of the dwarfs is not mine. Without sunlight, I would shrivel within days like a plant.
Flowers are one of the most beautiful gifts that Crunor blessed us with. They are very delicate creatures and must be treated with utmost care.
I love to stroll around in the jungle. The diversity of plants is fantastic there and even the poisonous spit nettle remains calm if it feels the unconditional love for all plants in your heart.
For me, the trees in the jungle of Tiquanda are the kings. Oh, you mean the Tibian king? I'm not interested in human bureaucracy.
Many dryads consider almost everything that is no plant as a threat to plants and the forests ...
Humans that lumber our forests to build their wooden caves and the strange things they use to cross the seas are especially threatening.
If you bring me 5 seeds, I'll give you a flowerpot with a rare seedling. With good care and a little love, it will grow into a beautiful plant.
You will have to water it regularly, then it will flourish and grow. There are several stages of growth that your plant has to pass ...
With good care and luck, it will grow into the next stage until it finally becomes a fully blooming flower. ...
Of course plants won't grow in the darkness of a depot box. On the other hand, it won't dry out there either ...
So if you know you can't take care of your plant for a longer time, it might be a good idea to store it into your depot box.
I love to stroll around in the jungle. The diversity of plants is fantastic there and even the poisonous spit nettle remains calm if it feels the unconditional love for all plants in your heart.
The griffinclaw is the queen among the plants.
I prefer to stay outside of towns to enjoy the nature around me.
Farewell.

Each seed is like a baby to us dryads. For every 5 seeds you bring me, I'll reward you with a flowerpot that contains a seedling that might flourish into a rare and beautiful plant if you care for it. ...
Do you have any seeds that you would like to exchange?
Here, I planted this little baby in a flowerpot for you. Don't forget to water it regularity - buy a watering can somewhere!
pages.title: Rosemarie

pages.name: Uso
npc_lines: Hiho Player. Looking for a knight trainer? I'm your man.
I'm called Uso Oredigger, son of the Flame from the Dragoneaters.
I'm the head of a little mining operation here and I train knights and teach them spells in my spare time to prevent my old body from rusting.
There IS gold out there. Lots of it! I can feel it in my old bones.

I can teach you healing spells, attack spells, support spells and summon spells. What kind of spell do you wish to learn? You can also tell me for which level you would like to learn a spell, if you prefer that.
We dwarfs call it our home since the dawn of time. I miss Kazordoon a lot, but gold is more important. After I have made a fortune here, I will return home and might settle down.
We are a proud race. Dwarfs are strong and fearless. We can even survive in this forsaken jungle, jawoll.
To me one human is just as good as the other. I don't care what city they are from.
That's just a bunch of trees but no city.
I wonder why we see so few elves over here. Those tree people should love this cursed jungle, but even they stay away.
Human kings are not of interest for me.
So long.
pages.title: Uso

pages.name: Clark
npc_lines: Hello, Jogador. Please don’t interrupt me for too long!
I’m the captain of the guards and responsible for upholding law and order in the colony.
My name is Clark.
The guards of Port Hope are led by Lord Seamus, a nobleman from Thais.
He is ill and I’m in charge of upholding the law now.
Dwarfs are impressive fighters. The Venoreans talked about hiring some of them as mercenaries to help us out.
They don’t pose a real threat to us.
Rest assured we’ll handle this problem.
They fear our power and hide in some caves.
He is the enemy number one of the kingdom and all good people.
I heard the knights of Edron hide it somewhere instead of using it for the good of the country.
Our king can be proud of this colony.
The jungle is our first and foremost enemy.
It is horas right now.
Thais is a big city but if we do well enough here, Port Hope might one day rival its size.
The Venoreans are fine and generous people. It’s a good thing that they put all this effort into this colony. I don’t know what we would do if it weren’t for them.

It’s a shame that those women still get away with their independence. Friends told me that too many of Thais’s resources are wasted in useless projects, and the army is too weak to claim back our belongings.
My guess is that those elves are secretly allied with Carlin. I wouldn’t trust an elf if I met one.
As long as the dwarfs stay there, it’s alright for me to let them have this ugly piece of rock.
The knights of Edron are somewhat arrogant. They keep the resources of the isle all to themselves instead of sharing them.
A village of harmless cultists. They pose no real threat and could easily be integrated into the Thaian realm.
This city is a threat to Thais’s domination of Darama. Unfortunately, we are too weak to handle this threat.
This continent will be ours one day.
I guess a good part of the world is under Thaian rule.
Goodbye, Jogador.
pages.title: Clark

pages.name: Chantalle
npc_lines: Hello. What brings you here?
I’m a trader and I sell gems, jewellery and goblets. Just ask me for my offers.
My name is Chantalle.
I sell gems and goblets. If you’d like to see my offers, ask me for a trade.
What? You lost the key? Well… Lucky for you I made a copy. Do not lose it again!
I’d rather kiss a pig.
I don’t know anything about a cult. On the other hand, I wouldn’t be too surprised if this fish smelling natives, that are up to no good anyway, would have some horrible cult.
Isn’t that the name of the governor’s daughter’s dog?
I don’t understand why someone would want to go to some dirty corners of the world or crawl through dusty dungeons. Phew.
You can buy and sell small diamonds, sapphires, rubies, emeralds and amethysts or sell topazes.
Ah, our newest import! We have golden goblets, silver goblets and bronze goblets. All of them have space for a hand-written dedication.
Yes, horrible. Isn’t it?
Currently you can purchase wedding rings, golden amulets, and ruby necklaces. We also buy gold ingots.
The natives had almost massacred themselves before we arrived to rescue them. And what to we get in return? Now they want to massacre us instead! These horrible people.
There are white and black pearls you can buy or sell, as well as giant green and brown pearls which you can sell.

Pirates are scary. Mr. Loveless tries hard to get the army to do more against these horrible pirates. Unfortunately the army people are rather reluctant and always find some excuse for their inactivity.
I better don’t think about all those dirty people that work on the plantations, else I could no longer enjoy my sugared tea. Imagine that their ugly dirty hands have touched this sugar.
These horrible fishmen even haunt me in my dreams! I’m sure the natives are in league with them. It’s no coincidence that they both smell alike.
It tastes horrible. I can’t understand what people like about it.
Sugar is quite important as far as I understand it.
Currently it is horas.
We don’t trade with them.
Here, take a look.
The governor is a fine and polite man. I think he even likes me a bit. <giggles> Sad enough that people who like him or Mr. Loveless are rare here.
The king must be a very special man. I think he’s handsome and tall.
She thinks she is better than everyone else. But I know that a good part of her so-called noble family lives in Carlin, imagine!

You can say that Mr. Loveless is kind of an ambassador of Venore. He is very important and I run his business here. He’s a good friend of the local governor and back in Venore he’s an important figure of the trade association.
That is one of those horrible cutthroats that lead the pirates.
Quite handsome and what a well-trained body he has. I can’t imagine what he sees in this colourless and pale Isolde.
He’s some evil sorcerer. Sorcerers are horrible people anyway.
He’s handsome, yet a bit old. And sadly you’ll never get rich being in the army. It’s a shame but for these reasons he probably will never be able to find an accomplished woman.
It’s the name of a scary old hag that the natives sometimes call if they are sick. Why don’t they just buy some medicine or call for a healer? Silly people.
Who might that be? Probably one of these horrible natives.
She’s a bit younger than me and a bit jealous that I and her father get along with each other so well.

What a horrible, horrible little town. Have you seen those huts some people live in? How can they stand this? Silly people. And that stench! Everything and everyone that is native smells like fish! Horrible, I say it’s just horrible!
Thais must be a wonderful place. Almost comparable to Venore as far as I can tell.
Farewell.
pages.title: Chantalle

pages.name: Admiral Wyrmslicer
npc_lines: Greetings, Jogador. Have you anything to report?
I am admiral of the Thaian fleet and commander of this fort and the local military.
My family is respected for many deeds of heroism. There is a well-known dragon slayer in our bloodline which earned us that name of honour.
Mr. Loveless has a sharp and quick mind. If he were no trader, he would have made a great officer.
LONG LIVE THE KING!
Competent and efficient. I give nothing about ugly rumours, and she never, ever, betrayed the trust put into her.
The governor is a fine man, and I do my best to support him in all his efforts.
This young lady truly graces Liberty Bay with her presence. It is always a pleasure to meet her.
I heard about that man. For some people he is some kind of father figure. If he should ever misuse that, we will take a closer look at him.
I believe she is this old healer in town. I don’t think she is happy with our presence here but she did nothing yet that would justify to arrest her.
A fine knight indeed. I am very pleased with his efforts.
Captain Striker is one of the more cunning pirates. Up to now, he managed to escape but sooner or later he will run out of luck.
Thais is of course the crown of our kingdom and the place our hearts will belong to forever.
It might take some time, but with our guidance the city will flourish and prosper.
Sooner or later Carlin will be nothing more than a footnote in history. Look at the size of our kingdom and compare it with Carlin …
One day they will accept that it is better to rejoin the kingdom and to combine our efforts and resources for the good of all.
The efforts Venore put into this city are admirable. It’s only fair that they gain a certain profit from that.
Excalibug is an inspiring myth, but after all, only a myth.
We welcome the representatives of the society here and will do our best to support them.
I am not familiar with witchcraft and sorcery. Perhaps you should ask someone else.
I heard enough of the gossip and superstitions. I am fed up with that nonsense!
Spare me the nonsense that people made up, like sinister cultists, quara infiltrators, pirate hideouts voodoo curses and whatnot! …
I’ve heard it all, and it is completely rubbish and a waste of my time! We have everything firmly under control. And to ensure this, I warn you not to talk to the townspeople about such issues!
The talks about the cult are getting tiresome. There is no such thing. It is only another superstition here.
The quara are treacherous foes who don’t fight with common tactics. This and the security of the seas, to which they can withdraw, make it difficult to handle them properly.
Pirates are vermin and we will wipe them from the map wherever they raise their ugly heads.
Superstition! We have real sorcerers and none of them uses such prankish trickery.
We need the sugar. We will ensure with everything that is at our command that the supply of sugar is kept up.
Rum can be just as good for morale as it can be bad. It has to be administered with care.
There is always trouble at the plantations, either with the rotworms or with drunken or rebellious workers.
I don’t want to hear talks about ‘natives’ or such. We are all subjects of his majesty, the King of Thais.
Good bye Jogador, you may leave.
pages.title: Admiral Wyrmslicer

pages.name: Marcus
npc_lines: Ahoi. What is your business in the harbour?
I keep an eye on the cargo here in the harbour.
If people would mind their own business, the city could be a better place.
<spits on the floor> I killed my share of pirates in my youth. Dogs that give sailors a bad name. Nothing more than bandits.
The governor's little princess, eh? Too fine and important to care about us ordinary people of course. Why should we care about her?
The governor does his job I guess.
The king lives far away and appears like a fairy tale over here.
Go away with that Thais. I've been there and I've seen it. Not impressive at all.
A horrible town for a sailor. Imagine a town without alcohol, ruled by women! I guess if you are a pirate or some other dog, your afterlife starts in Carlin.
They build fine ships in this town. That's the best I can say about it. If you do not have enough money, you are nothing in Venore.
If people would mind their own business, the city could be a better place.
Just another lousy pirate, although a quite daring and successful one.
He is just some old man about which the townspeople are talking now and then. Who cares.
A klabauterman is some sort of imp that lives on ships and plays quite evil and sometimes lethal pranks on those who annoy him or don't buy his sympathy with little gifts.
The quara are one of the most murderous threats that the sea gave birth too. I would rather face a giant sea serpent than a horde of quara ...
In the case of a sea serpent you know at least that you'll end up devoured, but who knows what the quara will do to you.

I swear I have seen it in the bay just outside of Liberty Bay, deep in the ocean. I was ... uhm catching some fresh air after a night of rum and card games. I looked over the railing into the sea and suddenly I saw that sword in a heap of gold and jewels.
Bye.
pages.title: Marcus

pages.name: Theodore Loveless
npc_lines: Greetings, dear visitor.
I am honoured to humbly serve as the spokesman of the Venorean trading companies.

Venore has become an impressive little point of trade for wares from all over the world. The steady work pays off and brings us a modest state of luxury ... We have learnt much from our big brother Thais which we admire and where we are still searching for guidance.

We put great hope in this settlement. The Venorean traders invested much money in the growth of that community here ... We have to see that the little profit we make will be enough to cover our expenses in the remote future ... But we are happy that our money could help to bring peace and to civilise the natives here ... Thais finally brought order to the locals that were torn from fightings and hunger before our arrival.
Thais is such a lovely city. The bustling centre of civilisation. The world has to thank Thais for so many things.
Sugar is money. Sugar is business. It's as easy as that.
I heard he has some relation to these isles. To learn more about it, you probably talk to the mage from Edron that resides in a tower here in the city.

The king has again proven his great wisdom. The way how he allowed to settle the affairs in Liberty Bays was more than smart ... The trust he has put in the governor, the local military and the help from Venore begins slowly to pay off ... People have work and something to do. The number of fights decreased to the brawls between drunks that are usual for seaports ... As soon as we have the pirates eliminated, we can lower many of the restrictions we had to enforce for the safety of all.

Governor Silverhand is such a fine person. He does so much for the city and receives so little in return. I hope we can cheer him up now and then. That's the least we can do for this great man that sacrifices himself for the good of his people.
Ah, my young friend, you have no idea how many companies have some sort of interest in seeing this settlement prosper.

The pirates are all what is left from the warlords that once terrorised this region. Now that peace and the protection of Liberty Bay byour military moves in, their days are numbered ... One day, hopefully in the near future, the sea will be just as safe as this isle.

I must admit I am a bit suspicious of this young lady. As far as I know she was not overly fond of the Thaian nobility. Add her strong family ties to this rebel townCarlin and you begin to wonder what that woman is up to. All of a sudden she accepted a mission for the nobility that she did not acknowledge before? And this unholy influence on this poor young Tristan whom she seduced with her beauty. I must admit, I am concerned.

What a fine young man. I just wonder what brought him here in the first place. Of course I don't believe into rumours that he left a sick wife and 3 childrensomewhere to begin a new life here. That is probably just made up by those that are jealous of him.
Even the mentionable efforts of this great admiral could not stop the pirates yet. But he will not rest until the last one of this scum will hang for the glory of Thais.
This notorious pirate and cutthroat has killed more men, women and children than the last epidemic we had here in the slums ...
Call it like you want. It is just another form of magic ...
This ugly hag is known as witch and poison brewer. Sadly she is too clever and the citizens too fearful, so the guards could not arrest her yet ...

Chondur was a charismatic leader amongst the settlers that used to lived here. His greed for land and power made him to one of the warlords that were responsible for all those fights and cruelty between the settlers ...
We put great hope in this settlement. The Venorean traders invested much money in the growth of that community here ...

Miss Eleonore is so charming, so beautiful. Her strong will and her independence poses surely a great challenge to every man who wants to marry her. But one look into her beautiful eyes and you will see that she is worth the effort. Perhaps one day I might be allowed to take that challenge ... who knows.
pages.title: Theodore Loveless

pages.name: Janz
npc_lines: Welcome to my shop of wonderful carpentry and furniture.
My name is Janz.
I am selling furniture.
Well, as you can see, I sell furniture. Ask me for a trade if you're interested to see my wares.
We have little use of your southern gods.
The druids are shamans from Carlin.
The shamans are great seers and healers.
That's some evil spirit the people of the south are fearing.
A weapon that would make woodcutting easy.
Nothing exciting has happened lately.
