I visited Carlin once and I was very impressed. They used less wood then I'd expected but it was a marvellous town.
From the tales I heard, it expect it to be a bit like Everspring.
I heard this is some spot in the South which is similar to the place that expects one in the afterlife.
I heard they used much wood, too, to build that town.
If it were not for the wood we've gotten from Carlin, the city would for sure look less impressive.
I heard Thais is even bigger than Carlin.
The people of Carlin are somewhat bothered by Venore.
I heard they are fine woodcutters.
I heard their city is made of living trees! Imagine!
The chakoyas are real. My grandfather got killed by them.
They are rather rare.
The dragons usually stay in their areas, so we have little trouble with them.
Our jarl is a fine man. I named a cupboard after him.
I am proud to be a barbarian, even though a civilised one of course.
They are just greedy for all we have accomplished.
I don't even understand what that means.
The mines are somewhere in the mountains. In the early days of our city, many people from Carlin used to work there.
Father north wind knows best.
Most shamans live there.
That have been hard years in which we were cut off from our main wood supply. Gladly wood does not suffer much in our climate.
It could be worse I guess.
Good bye.
pages.title: Janz

pages.name: Lurik
npc_lines: Welcome to the explorer society headquarter of Svargrond, Jogador!
My name is Lurik. Odd enough you ask though. People hardly do that nowadays. I feel as if my name was painted above my head or something.
I am the explorer's society. I just love it to be at the frontier of all known lands.
No kings or queens rule these remote lands.
We know of father Chyll and his freezing breath. We care little for other gods. It is foolish to meddle with beings that are so powerful ...
We leave it to the druids and shamans to handle such affairs.
Even here we heard about this powerful man. Travellers from the south only dare to whisper his name.
On the campfire, there are numerous tales about this weapon. It's told that it has been missing since ages ...
In my opinion, the power and fame of a weapon shouldn't exceed the power and fame of it's wielder. And I have not heard of any hero whose fame would surpass that of excalibug.
At this remote spot, news are old news. Did you hear that quara attacked Liberty Bay?
I am fine. Thank you. There is a bit less work here than I had expected but I am sure we will have some intriguing discoveries just waiting for us.

I met some of those little people in the past. Considering our experience with the chakoyas, we don't underestimate someone just for its look. And those dwarfs proved indeed to be powerful, courageous and enduring.
Some time ago, a few elves came here but they could not stand the cold and so they left pretty soon. Most likely it was Nibelor in which they have been interested.

Maybe you already heard that we send our dead with a boat on their last journey. A rumour came to my ear that many of the corpses stranded on the small island of Helheim where they walk around as UNDEADS. I wonder if this is true.
Our noble society is dedicated to explore the unknown. No location is too remote for our members to travel there ...
No beast is too wild to be hunted. No treasure buried too deep to be unearthed ...
Only the most dedicated and fearless adventurers may join our ranks.
But you are already a member, Jogador.
You are a novice of the explorer's society.
You have no special badge earned yet.
Sorry, I have no mission available.

This city has seen much in the few days of its existence. At first it was a little trading spot where ships form Carlin landed. Later it became a deposit for ore that has been mined in the mountains ...
Then local people joined the traders from Carlin and supplied them with fish, furs and meat ...
Soon it became a small settlement and the locals, fascinated with the abundance of wood the traders brought with them, begun to build houses ...
It became a centre of conflict when some barbarians decided it was wrong to settle in a town and later on struggled to survive when the contact to Carlin was lost for decades ...
Today, the city got a little boost by the presence of foreigners here. But only the future will tell what the fate of this city will be.

Most shaman and druids of our people live on the sacred isle Nibelor. There, they divine the future, calm the wrath of father Chyll and prepare the dead for their last travel to the lands of Everspring.
Nibelor has always been a sacred place for our people. The druids and shamans live there.
Everspring is the realm of the dead. It is a place of peace and harmony where those who boldly braved the challenges of life dwell for eternity and share stories at the campfires after a hunt ...
Every true barbarian that is properly brought into afterlife will join the great hunt in Everspring where the animals are fat and have the thickest furs.
I don't care what people who come here believe in. If they provoke father Chyll, he will take care of them on his own. If their gods prove to be more powerful than Chyll, they might deserve to live.
The jarl is a kind of chieftain of the local people here. If you haven't done yet, talk to him. If you want to be accepted by the people here, you will have to ask the jarl for the barbarian test.
A true barbarian is something special among our people. Everyone who wants to become a barbarian will have to pass the barbarian test.

All of our juveniles have to take the barbarian test to become a true member of our community. Foreigners who manage to master the test might become honorary barbarians and gain the respect of our people.
The people here seem to be a bit uncivilised on the first glance. Rest rest assured that they are hospitable and generous if you earn their respect in some way.
Those barbarian who did oppose the building of this settlements call themselves raiders. They consist of some major and minor clans. ...
It's said that they are lead by a shaman woman, who has celebrated her 100th birthday a long time ago, but I am not sure how believable such records are.
A long time ago when the trade with Carlin was flourishing, people actually worked in the mines. During the years of the serpents, the mines had been abandoned. ...
Later, the raiders took shelter there, although they blame us for living in a fortified city ...
Now, the traders of Carlin are back but some other foreigners seem to have claimed the mines from the raiders ...

It's neither our business nor would we have the manpower to help them to recapture the mines. Also, if they do not have the strength to get the mines back on their own, they don't deserve them anyway.
It was an astonishing phenomenon. For decades, sea serpents made it impossible to reach these northern isles by ship ...
The most puzzling part of this event is probably the fact that sea serpents usually prefer a southern climate ...
However, almost over night the sea serpents seemed to be gone and the contact between Carlin and the isles here could finally be reestablished.
It's a shame I still have not seen a living chakoya. I could examine some dead specimen though and I have seen some of their victims ...
It's hard to believe that such a small creature is such a terrible threat but for all I can tell they are indeed quite dangerous.

The yetis are mythical beasts. Only few that encountered those creatures lived to tell the tale. The chakoyas worship them as divine beings, although they have no real relations to them, as far as we can tell.
We are friends of the Carliners. Still we don't allow their politics to influence our way to handle things here.
We have heard only little about this far away place.
We did not allow them to stay here. This had nothing to do with our friendship with Carlin but for the way they handled things and their harmful approach to go hunting.
We understand that our friends from Carlin are wary with the realm ruled by Thais but this is not of our concern.
Good bye. Come back soon with exciting stories about your travels.
pages.title: Lurik

pages.name: Hawkyr
npc_lines: Hello fellow hunter. Are you looking for paladin spells? I'm your man.
I am Hawkyr the hunter.
I am a hunter and bowyer. If you need some training, I am the man you want to see.
Sorry, I don't have anything to do for you.
In our lands, the most successful hunter is the king. Be it beast or man.
In our lands, the most successful huntress is the queen. Be it beast or woman.
The gods of the south seem to have little influence here.
Sorry, I don't teach spells for your vocation.
They know the ways of spirits and nature. You can learn a lot from them just by listening. Still, you can always learn a lot if you're listening well to what nature tells you.
Better ask the Southerners about that one.
A weapon hardly useful for a hunter.
The wolves are very hungry lately.
I don't think I'd like that place and it's not only that this is not my marked territory.
Only foreigners talk about that place now and then.
I admire the safety of the burrow and the closeness of the pack. It's a good thing to have a lair to which you can withdraw to lick your wounds.
Thais is some far away city.
Carlin and Venore seem to live in some sort of rivalry.
Most dwarfs I've seen seem to lack the stealthiness to become a good hunter.
Elves are good hunters. Even I was able to learn something from the elves that came here. I am thinking about visiting their city some day.
The chakoya are ferocious hunters. They don't only kill out of hunger, they love the carnage they are causing.
Yetis are rare but they do exist. Everyone that has been hunting in the frozen wastes for some time can share stories of their sightings.
It's not easy to hunt dragons. Suddenly, a hunter might become the hunted in their lairs.
I don't know anything about it.
Being a barbarian means to be one with nature and its instincts.
Their packs are not of our kin anymore. They left our pack. We will see how they prosper. They have nothing to expect from us except for cold steel in their hearts.
As far as I have understood it, they are of some importance for the people of Carlin.
Father north wind knows best.
An isle on which the shamans live.
I wonder if even bigger hunter have driven them away.
I only feel alive when I'm on a hunt. But even I need some time to rest and regain strength.
Good hunting, Jogador.
pages.title: Hawkyr

pages.name: Romir
npc_lines: Greetings, traveller. I'm a magical trader and trainer for sorcerer spells. How may I help you?
I am known as Romir.

I guess one could call me a hermit. I am a bit new to this hermit business though and I have to admit I enjoy some company now and then. I also earn some money by teaching spells to those in search of knowledge.
Of course, just browse through my wares. Or do you want to look only at potions, wands or runes?
Have a look. You can also look at wands or runes.
Have a look. You can also look at potions or runes.
Have a look. You can also look at wands or potions.
Okay, then just browse through all of my wares.
If I cared about news, I hadn't chosen this remote spot to settle down.
The most yetis have been seen further south. Of course only because they are much more easily overlooked in the rugged mountains and huge snow plains here.
There something sinister going on and I am quite sure this cult you just mentioned is somehow connected to it.
Dwarfs are quite settled. Even if the mines were recaptured, I doubt that we would see more than a handful of dwarfs here..
Good bye.
pages.title: Romir

pages.name: Thorwulf
npc_lines: Hi Jogador.
I am Thorwulf, slayer of dragons, giants and yetis.
The dragons of these lands are fierce as a blizzard and lethal as the silent cold and the howling snow storm alike.
The yetis are powerful and cunning foes. It takes the right bait to lure them out of their hiding places.
I won't tell. Never ever. Find out on your own.
I am an expert fighter and I can teach a true warrior in the arts of war.
I don't have anything to do for you.
How can someone who never proved himself as a warrior lead people into a battle?
The people from Carlin seem to respect their queen. Though, I can't understand why. She is hardly a warrior.
I couldn't care less for gods. Every true warrior creates his own fortune.
Sorry, I don't teach spells for your vocation.
As far as I understood it, druids are like our shamans. I know enough magic to defeat my opponents on my own. So I have only little use for such spell casters
All they are doing is talking to the spirits the whole day. My enemies, however, are of flesh and blood and I can handle them on my own.
Bah, to know that he is a sorcerer means to know that he is a coward.
A true warrior will kill his opponents with a rusty knife. There is no need for a mighty weapon. Where is the honour if the weapon is more powerful than its wielder?
There are no news ... yet. But I can smell blood and steel in the air. I can feel it, there is going to be a battle soon.
I care little for the people from Carlin. All of them are so weak and timid. I could not care less for their concerns. If they want something to be done, they will have to do it on their own.
Some far away place the people of Carlin talk about now and then.
I hate it to wait here for our enemies to arrive. I'd rather go out and wage war in their camps and lairs.
Thais is not better than Carlin.
For all I know, they are schemers and liars. That means they are even worse than the other southerners.
I haven't seen many of them around here.
The elves that came here were quite skilled with a bow. I respect that in a way, still it takes little courage to shoot something from afar.
The chakoyas are small but their teeth can shred a man's arm into pieces. Their strength lies in their number as well as in ambushes on unwary or sleeping persons.
I don't care about cults.
Our jarl has grown old. I honour him for his deeds in the past but I wonder if a younger leader wouldn't be better now. He could lead us into glorious battles with the raiders.
Their cowardly tactics are a shame for every true barbarian, so is their obedience to a witch. They are not even worthy opponents.
Most people have forgotten that being a true barbarian means to be a fearless fighter.
Those Carliners seem to care about those mines, but they don't have the guts to recapture them. Pathetic.
The wind that has seen all battles and that puts an icy blanket over the battlefields.
A boring piece of ice and rock on which only shamans live.
Men are not supposed to travel the seas. So I don't care if these giant serpents ever existed or if they had only been an excuse for cowards.
As long as I am not fighting, I am bored.

A few years ago there was an arena fighter named Alrik. He managed to win the Warlord title three times in a row. He was Svargrond's greatest hero and all of a sudden he was gone and never seen again. ...
Even his sculpture disappeared. The people say Chyll took him directly to Everspring where he could live a king's life as a reward.
You talked to Robert, did you? I think I scared him pretty well! Hehehe!
Bye Jogador.
pages.title: Thorwulf

pages.name: Bertha
npc_lines: Greetings Jogador. Looking for a trade, I hope. Business is not going well.
These barbarians are still adapting to the city life but they do quite well I guess. They still lack interest in real trading and ... let's say they are a bit limited in their horizon.
I guess whole Thais is laughing at the failure of our operations.
Carlin expects wonders of me. However, as long as they don't send some considerable help, they can wait until moss is growing in their hair.
They promised me these frozen lands could become for Carlin what Edron is for Thais. What a cruel joke.
Sadly I could not win many dwarfs for our mining operations. They are probably afraid of Thais's reaction if it becomes known that they are helping us.
The elves are of no great help. They do little to convince the spiritual leaders of the barbarians to help me.
My inventory of general goods and paperware is large, ask me for a trade to take a look.
Ask a sorcerer or druid about that.
Another senseless tale of superstitious natives.
Well, we heard of some strangers that travelled through this city. Not exchanging many words with the people here. The locals claim they headed straight to our old mines ...
As far as I can tell though not much has changed at the mines. Our scouts are still attacked or even killed. So I assume the strangers were either killed or they are friends of the raiders ...
I have no clue what has happened and I don't have the resources to find out.
I think these chakoyas are only a tale to scare the local kids.
All this cold seems to have frozen the brains of those people to solid ice.
Robert sells that. Go and ask him about that.
You can buy general goods from me. For weapons and armor you rather see my assistant Robert at the arena in the mountains to the west.
My inventory of general goods and paperware is large, ask me for a trade to take a look.
The jarl here is of no great help. Our equipment and wood is welcome but we get little profit out of these deals.
Their presence is bad enough. The fact that they occupied the mines and that they hate us non-natives of this frozen rock makes things only worse.
The mines are actually Carlin's property. If only the queen were sending soldiers, to get them back from this rabble. Venore is probably planning to take over these mines just as we are talking.
That's how the local druids call themselves.
That seems to be a god that the locals worship.
Nibelor is an isle on which the local druids dwell.
What a horrible threat those beasts have been. But if they hadn't vanished all of a sudden, we would never have stranded here.
I'm Bertha from Carlin.
I'm a trader by profession but here you could also call me the ambassador of Carlin. However, there is little I can do about our problems, and support from Carlin is virtually non-existent.
Unless you can change the whole situation here, I don't have anything to do for you.
The pompous king of Thais might be involved in the take-over of our mines.
The gods seem to be far away in this corner of the world.
Ask a sorcerer or druid about that.
The druids of Carlin have quite good connections to the local druids here.
Well, HE would only be needed to make things worse over here.
I toyed with the idea to spread the rumour that Excalibug might be hidden in the mines. I think if enough adventurers were lured into the mines, they might drive out the ones that occupy them now ...
So do me a favour, when somebody asks about Excalibug, tell them it's down there in those mines.
I have confirmed information that Excalibug lies deep in the mines. If you manage to find it, you would be the biggest hero and everybody would know your name! ...
Imagine that: King Jogador, who found Excalibug and saved the world !!! Sounds good, huh??
News? Are you mocking me? Almost any news would be good news. As long as it concerns Carlin's affairs, nothing seems to change for the better.
My inventory of general goods and paperware is large, ask me for a trade to take a look.
It could definitely be better but thanks for asking. I hope you're fine yourself.
Bye Jogador.
pages.title: Bertha

pages.name: Jessica
npc_lines: Greetings stranger. Let me know if you want to trade gems or jewellery. I am also the local bank contact.
My name is Jessica.
I sell jewellery and serve as the local bank contact.
Currently you can purchase Wedding Rings, Golden Amulets, and Ruby Necklaces. We also buy Gold Ingots.
We can change money for you. You can also access your bank account.
Okay okay, no need to be rude! It seems you are already know everything.
We can change money for you. You can also access your bank account.
Renting a house has never been this easy. Simply make a bid for an auction. We will check immediately if you have enough money ...

Please keep in mind that the sum you have used to bid will be unavailable unless somebody places a higher bid. Once you have acquired a house the rent will be charged automatically from your bank account every month.
I don't have anything to do for you.
The king in Thais works for the Venorean trade barons. I can't imagine what sinister ideas they might implant into his mind right now.
The gods only help those who help themselves.
We had hardly any assistance from the druids here. I think that's more than suspicious ...
There might be some agent from Venore who has been infiltrated into their ranks. It is also possible that these treehuggers were bribed with a handful of acorns. Who knows!
There are enough heroes around to take care of those obvious threats.
All Thaian colonies are in the firm grip of the schemes of Venorean trade barons.
This wannabe city full of hardly civilised barbarians is a dangerous mixture. It takes little for the Venorean agents to cause havoc here.
The trade barons are the worst enemies one can have. They have their hidden agents everywhere and murder and treachery are natural to them.
There is a mine but no dwarfs. What do they know what we don't, I ask you? I am convinced they know that Venore will make anyone suffer that is trying to claim these mines.
The elves are not interested in our problems at all.
We have never ever seen one here. Instead of talking about far-off chakoyas, they should concentrate on REAL threats like the Venoreans.
There are no yetis. That's just another story to draw off our attention from what is really happening.
Spare me with that cult stories. This was no cult but some Venorean agents who were heading to their hired barbarians which had occupied our mines.
We don't trade with them.
The local chieftain does nothing to help us. It would be so easy for him to drive those other barbarians away from the mines. I suspect he was bribed to remain inactive by agents of Venore.
Those are simple people. Sadly, they have been influenced by others.
How convenient for Venore that we lost control over the mines. And isn't it also convenient for Venore that Carlin seems to lack interest to recapture the mines. I'd say that smells like conspiracy.
I can't say that I trust these fellows.
That belongs to some superstitious belief of the locals.
Some mysterious isle which was hardly seen by any outsider. I wonder what's happening there in all that secrecy.

The sea serpents were surely the work of Venore. They are the only ones that are unscrupulous enough to execute such a plan. Their disappearance was just part of some conspiracy to lure us here for some reason ...
I am only wondering how the Venoreans managed to lure that many serpents to the north.
I am fine. Odd that you ask though ... I hope you are not up to something.
There are no news. I think that's quite suspicious.
I heard the jarl opened a head hunt on the Venorans. As this is a secret, you have to use the keyword “blubber” to gain his trust in that case. He promised 1000 gold for every dead Venorean hunter.
Good bye.
pages.title: Jessica

pages.name: Robert
npc_lines: Hello, Jogador! Nice to see you, welcome to my weapon shop.
My name is Robert.

I am responsible for the trade with weapons and armor here in the arena. I constantly beg my superior Bertha to give me some other job or, even better, to send me back to Carlin but the cold seems to have frozen her heart.
I have many weapons to offer, including bows, crossbows and ammunition. If you'd like to see my offers, ask me for a trade.
I am selling leather, chain, and brass armor. If you'd like to see my offers, ask me for a trade.
I am selling chain legs. If you'd like to see my offers, ask me for a trade.
No, I don't have anything to do for you.
I heard they have a king in Thais.
If only our beloved queen would know what dangers we have to face here. I am sure she would call us back to the safety of Carlin.
I daily pray to the gods to protect me from harm. I still believe in a wonder to come which will get me back to Carlin.
If there were some more druids around with all their awesome healing powers, I'd feel more comfortable.
They are the local witch doctors. I'd rather wait for the rare visit of a druid from Carlin than to put my life in the hands of one of those people.
Shush! Don't speak that name aloud. It might call him here.
Sorry, I think we are out of stock.
The good news are: I got not killed by some drunken barbarian or unskilled axe thrower. The bad news are: I am still stranded here.
My offers are weapons, ammunition, armors, helmets, legs, and shields. If you'd like to see my offers, ask me for a {trade}.
Oh sweet Carlin, when will I see you again?
Edron is in the other end of the world. I wish I were there.
Port Hope and its cannibal orcs is almost as bad as Svargrond.
Even Thais could not be worse than this frozen hell hole here.
Jessica says they have agents everywhere. I wonder if they try to kill me to hinder our trade here ...
Since the day I spoke with Jessica, I sleep under my bed, just to be on the safe side.
Sure it looks peaceful, but to be honest, those wild barbarians are scary.
You know, I thought dwarfs were rude drunkards. However, that was before I met the people here.
Elves are strange creatures. I heard each of them can cast spells and curses. Every time an elf is looking in my direction, it gives me shivers.
For all I heard, the palisades won't stop them when they come at night to kidnap sleeping people and to eat them alive.
Yetis are huge, but perfectly camouflaged in the snow. They attack out of nowhere and before you can scream you are dead.
I don't know what you mean.
The local jarl is a fine man, measured by local standards that is. Still he can't bring me back from the dead when some of the barbarians go berserk and kill me.
The raiders are even wilder and, well ... more barbaric than the local barbarians. Can you imagine?!
The mines are lost. If only the people in Carlin were to accept that and call us back.
That is some spirit the barbarians seem to fear.
It's a haunted isle where the shamans call spirits and such to our world.
If those sea serpents had not vanished, I could still sit in the warm and safe Carlin. Cursed serpents.
Oh, don't even ask.

Have you talked to Thorwulf yet?? Be careful, I heard that he killed an experienced fighter in one hit just because he was called a coward after rejecting a challenge. I myself don't even dare to look in his eyes.
Good bye, Jogador.
pages.title: Robert

pages.name: Nelly
npc_lines: Hello Jogador, What can I do for you? I'm working for the post office, but I also trade with important potions, runes and other magical equipment.
I am Nelly ... Any special reason you ask?
I am working for the local post office. I also happen to have some recently imported potions and runes to sell for a very special price.
I don't have anything to do for you. Not even for me. What a boring place!
I wonder if the king in Thais even knows that this post office exists.
Druids of Carlin come here now and then to meet with the local shaman.
Just another name for the same magic users as usual. Probably spying on unsuspecting people like all those magic guys do.
This place is godforsaken.
The depots you can send parcels or letters to are in the following cities: Ab'Dendriel, Ankrahmun, Carlin, Darashia, Edron, Kazordoon, Liberty Bay, Port Hope, Svargrond, Thais and Venore.
May his name be cursed.
A myth the locals probably enjoy.
As if anything you'd get to hear, could be considered new.
Carlin lost interest in this place quite fast.
What are you suggesting? What do you know ... No, you can't know anything at all. Just forget it.
Yes, that's Svargrond. Welcome to the end of the world.
Thais has no affairs here.
I wonder if things were better if Venore ran the mining operations.
It seems even the dwarfs know better than to try their luck here.
The elves are of no great help here. They prefer to stay in warmer climates.
We offer health, spirit and mana potions in up to four sizes: normal, strong, great and ultimate. Ask me for a {trade} to see my offers.
The locals have so many superstitions, who can tell what's the truth and what is a myth.
Those chakoyas are hopefully just a local myth.
There were several strange people passing through the city some months ago. As far as I heard, they headed to the west and probably died in the cold.
The local authority and the first man here. He seems quite reasonable for a northman to me.
Those barbarians are just ruffians with no manners.
Who cares, I would not be that stupid to leave this frozen town anyway.
The loss of the mines doomed this place to complete insignificance.
I think that's how the natives call the wind.
I am not sure if it's a real place. Perhaps it's only some myth. Who knows or cares?
If only these sea serpents had never disappeared.
What do you know that makes you asking??
That guy from the Carlin Trading Syndicate told me that he knows a guy in Carlin who heard that the postman was talking to a customer about Svargrond and that he would like to work here! ...
Do you know what that means ??? I could finally leave this cursed ice block for good!!
Good bye, Jogador.
I sell parcels, letters, health potions, mana potions and runes.
With our mail system you can send letters and parcels to other Tibians. I can give you detailed information or sell letters and parcels to you if you ask me for a trade.
If you want to buy a letter, ask me for a trade. Or do you want me to explain how letters work?

With a letter you can send a message to another Tibian's depot. If you want to send it to 'Ben' in 'Thais', use the letter - so that a form opens - and write 'Ben' in the first line and 'Thais' in the second line. Write your message below that. ...
I can explain the mail system to you, or how parcels and letters work. If you want to buy something, ask me for a trade.
pages.title: Nelly

pages.name: A Grumpy Cyclops
npc_lines: Humi nykts! Ba wapa!
Ulyachhrhhhrp.
Moorrpa! Chlyn app!
pages.title: A Grumpy Cyclops

pages.name: Armenius
npc_lines: Ah, an adventurer. Be greeted and have a seat. How may I serve you?
That’s not a serious question, is it? I’m running a bar. Duh. Are you interested in my offers?
Don’t you know that when you know a person’s name, you hold some power over that person?
Uh huh. Scary, you can read the name on my bar.
We offer bread, cheese, ham, and meat, as well as eggs and tomatoes. Ask for a trade if you want to have a look.
I got beer, wine and some imported rum.
Didn’t your mama teach you? Ask for a trade if you want to see what my bar has to offer.
Sure.
If you want blood, go kill a pig.
Why would you ask that? I give you a hint – don’t meddle in affairs you haven’t the slightest idea about.
Fine place for me right now. Lots of… supplies.
Go away, little fly.
It’d be better for you to leave now.
This quarter might look a little run-down, but I prefer that to the shallow golden glory of the inner city.
Oh, don’t talk about him. Little Mr. Know-it-all, he is.
Isn’t that the fruit guy? Yes, I’ve seen him.
Don’t see him often. He basically lives on the opposite side of the city.
He prefers to visit a nobler tavern than mine. Pff.
A former pirate I think.
Unimportant gofers.
He's not a bad person, even from my point of view. Lots of criminals find shelter in this quarter, which means more people who come and visit my bar.
You know, actually I don’t feel like chatting with you much. Sorry, kid.
Good bye.
pages.title: Armenius

pages.name: Barry
npc_lines: I wish my shift would end.
Hello. Unless you have official business here or want to pass the gate, please move on.
I'm a sergeant of the Yalaharian Guard Force.
I'm called Barry.
They were appointed by the Yalahari to execute supervising and controlling tasks.
Excuse me? I'm not sure which mission you are talking about, just tell me what you want from me.
Do you want to pass the gate? Are you going to the magician or the sunken quarter?
We have eight quarters plus the centre, and each of them is like an own microcosm.
I actually like the city. There's so much going on in all those small streets and corners, it's really entertaining.
Neither Captain Karith nor Captain Cookie are sailing to the outer islands. I haven't found anyone yet to bring me there.
Mistrock? Yes, maybe that's the name. I'm not sure.
Yes, you're right. People are calling that snowy island Fenrock.
I heard about Vengoth, but not much.
I'd be careful if I went there. Some people have never come back, and those who did are ill in one or the other way.
A lot of trouble has been coming from that quarter lately. It seems that the former fighters and gladiators have changed in most unexpected ways.
You know, I was guarding this gate here at the time the southern quarter collapsed. It's something I'll never be able to erase from my mind.
You will not be able to attend any religious ceremonies in that quarter, that's a fact. Better stay away.
The old factory is just south of here. The machines and worker golems are not really functioning anymore, but you still hear their operating sounds.
I'm glad I don't have to do shifts there. It's interesting, but there are constantly fights going on.
A quarter full of talented magicians, illustrious figures and dangerous magical creatures. The latter cause most of the problems in this quarter.
Mr. West is not as bad as some people make him look like. He's a bit like 'steal from the rich to give it to the poor', in my opinion.
This is of no importance to me right now.
Goodbye citizen!
pages.title: Barry

pages.name: Bruce
npc_lines: I wish my shift would end.
Hello. Unless you have official business here or want to pass the gate, please move on.
Master Sergeant of the Yalaharian Guard Force, sir.
My name is Bruce.
They are our supervisors.
What is that mission you are talking about?
Should I let you pass the gate? Are you headed for the alchemist or the cemetery quarter?
Our guards protect the gates between all eight quarters.
I will protect this city with my life.
Which island are you talking about? Mistrock, Fenrock or Vengoth?
No one knows what this island is really called, but the people stick with 'mistrock' due to it being covered in mist.
It's a snowy island to the west.
One day the vampires on Vengoth will become a big threat. We should expect the worst from that place.
There has been a huge explosion due to some unknown experiments. Ever since then, the quarter is contaminated.
This used to be a great recreation area with a zoo and a lively arena.
The quarter collapsed into the ocean.
This is the quarter to the east. Don't expect any worshippers of our Tibian gods though.
Those old and malfunctioning machines could pose a threat to civilians.
New inhabitants are arriving daily, and most will be stuck in the foreigners' quarter forever.
I have huge respect for those highly educated magicians living there and dealing with the other magical creatures each day.
I think it's an outrage that this quarter is controlled by criminals.
I have nothing to say about that topic.
Goodbye citizen!
pages.title: Bruce

pages.name: Captain Cookie
npc_lines: Greetings, daring adventurer. If you need a passage, let me know.
Until I finally discover the cockaigne, I'll work as a captain of this ship for the explorer's society.
Well, if I was a vampire I guess I'd want all the blood I could get too. So I can't really blame them. Guess they have found their land of blood and honey already.
There is little in the world that cannot be improved with honey! I even use honey to style my hair!
Sweets are the greatest creation of the gods ever!
Isn't it obvious? They are explorers! If someone else but me should ever discover the cockaigne, it will be them! So I'm staying with them!
I just love chocolate! And honeyed chocolate I like the most!
That doesn't sound really tasty.
When I heard the story about the cockaigne as a kid, I just knew it must be the truth. A land of milk and honey must exist, and one day I'll find it!
I can't help it, I love sweets of any kind!
I don't know much about him. He welcomed me to the city and was quite polite.
I always dreamt about a ship made of sweets. But honestly I think I could not resist to taste it and would probably shipwreck it.
Yummy, the mother of all sweets!
I sometimes wonder why the gods did not make the ocean taste like lemonade. I guess if they did, it would have been drunken dry already.
Get off my raft!
I travelled here, hoping to find the cockaigne. Imagine my disappointment when I discovered I was wrong.
I wonder what kind of sweets they might prefer.
I can bring you to our base in Liberty Bay for 400 gold. Is that what you want?
Well, this is a strange region of Tibia. All that green slime there ... That's not to my taste.
Go away. Everything there tastes salty or oily. They use all their honey to produce mead. What a waste!
That's an island east of Darashia. Full of old ruins and unholy, demonic creatures. Brrr.
Darama is a strange continent. I traveled there a long time ago in search of the cockaigne.
Hmm, cookies with sweetened bug milk are so delicious.
Venore's sweets are exclusive and incredibly expensive. Once, I spent my whole wage on a night full of cookies and candies.
They have a decent assortment of sweets there.
Thais is rather dull and uninteresting when it comes to sweets.
Dwarfish sweets taste oddly. And most sorts contain alcohol.
A horrible place. You have no idea how fast chocolate is melting there!
The heat there lets chocolate melt quickly, but their candies made of sand wasp honey are something I could die for!
The dwarves and their odd cave systems ...
Zao is a continent south-east of Yalahar. Many lizards live there ... Creepy, I tell you!
Krailos is a faraway grassland, inhabited by savage ogres.
A really big city on the continent Kilmaresh. Its architecture is almost as impressive as Yalahar's. The creatures there, even more so.
Good bye.
pages.title: Captain Cookie

pages.name: Chuckles
npc_lines: <chuckles>!
If they only knew. <chuckles>
My old bones feel a storm approaching. <chuckles>
Come in if you are not here to burn me. I am just doing my job. <chuckles>
Let’s get over with it. Just ask for my offers!
I’m selling spirit, health and mana potions, runes, wands, rods and spellbooks. If you’d like to see my offers, ask me for a trade.
My potions are powerful, but please excuse if they taste a bit odd. My seasoning abilities are somewhat limited. <chuckles>
Of course, just browse through my wares. Or do you want to look only at potions, wands or runes?
Ah, come on, our bad reputation results only from a few black sheep among us liches. Honestly! <chuckles>!
The city is impressive. In its current state it even has an aura of undeath. <chuckles>
I wonder if they are as powerful as they pretend to be. Who knows, perhaps one day we’ll find out. <chuckles>
One of my best customers happens to be one. Just kidding. <chuckles>
Oooh, you’re playing with fire. <chuckles>
Excuse me? <chuckles>
Oh my, something must have gone really wrong. <chuckles>
I wouldn’t worry about them. Sooner or later, they’ve all killed each other.
I wonder what they’re all worried about. There is still a lot of slaughter and roaming beasts and such. The only thing that has changed is the entry fee. <chuckles>
It must have been affected by a significant case of bad luck. <chuckles>
<chuckles> Oh come on! They’re just kids. All they want to do is play. <chuckles>
I just hope these factories will not drive me out of business one day. <chuckles>
Looks like every other Tibian city. <chuckles>
Rods can be wielded by druids only and have a certain level requirement. There are eight different rods, would you like to hear about them?
Wands can be wielded by sorcerers only and have a certain level requirement. There are eight different wands, would you like to hear about them?
I’m selling spirit, health and mana potions, runes, wands, rods and spellbooks. If you’d like to see my offers, ask me for a trade.
Magic is nothing but a tool that comes in different shapes. <chuckles>
Well, you could ask me for a trade to deposit your flasks, but you can also do it old style. I will pay you 5 gold for every empty vial and potion flask. Ok?
Sorry, we removed the old life and mana fluids from our assortment. However, we offer health, spirit and mana potions in up to four sizes, just ask me for a trade.
I prefer to refer to this state as biologically challenged.
Feel free to return – alive or as an ingredient. <chuckles>
pages.title: Chuckles

pages.name: Dorbin
npc_lines: Hey, need some furniture for your house? Come to my shop!
Hello, Jogador! Welcome to my furniture store. I hope you are interested in a trade!
I’m Dorbin.
I sell furniture. We own this store in the third generation.
The city looks like a mess but new furniture here and there would work wonders, believe me.
Have a look. Most furniture comes in handy kits. Just use them in your house to assemble the furniture. Do you want to see only a certain type of furniture?
I have beds, chairs, containers, decoration, flowers, instruments, pillows, pottery, statues, tapestries and tables. Which of those would you like to see?
Well, sigh. It’s not funny to live in a city that is under frequent attack by vampires.
They are too elitist to buy my wares. I doubt they find any better quality, though.
Well, as you can see, we sell furniture. Ask me for a trade if you’re interested.
Ah you noticed my little helper? Well, if you train them at a young age, they are quite helpful. Still, I have to keep an eye on him. Until now his use outweighed the stuff he has smashed.
It was probably just luck that those mad alchemists did not blow up the whole city.
As if it had not been bad enough that this quarter was run over by madmen, these madmen were armed to the teeth.
One day, these monsters will unite and attack us.
For a while flotsam was quite popular as decor, but by now there are only a few pieces left.
I don’t want to deal with these strange guys wearing robes.
I doubt that any factory could replace the carpentry skill me and my assistants have acquired.
I agree, that would be a nice decoration object. Unfortunately I don’t sell them.
You can toss some cookies to my little helper over there. But don’t stick your finger in.
I just reduced all prices drastically.
He seems to be quite nice and reasonable.
It is horas.
Good bye, Jogador.
pages.title: Dorbin

pages.name: Ethan
npc_lines: Welcome to the paladin guild, Jogador! How can I help you?
I train young paladins the art of our vocation, and an art it is without doubt. I was already teaching paladins before you were even born.
I'm Ethan.
Of course it is also the knowledge of spells.
Sorry, I don't teach spells for your vocation.
Your vocation is your profession. There are four vocations in Tibia: paladins, knights, sorcerers, and druids.
Their tranquil ways have preserved much of their ancient philosophy. I appreciate that.
Sorcerers have always been power-hungry maniacs, and that hasn't changed much over the years.
The decline in knighthood seems even worse than the decline in our vocation.
What you call a paladin these days is a pale shadow of the paladins of old times. I expect my pupils to become role models and heroes, not selfish cowards.
For an old man like me everything sounds like old news.
This city has seen better days.
Tamara mentioned it sometime ago.
I hardly see any of them at all. I doubt that they care much about the things going on here. Else the city wouldn't be the mess it is.
Every paladin profits from his vocation. It has many advantages to be a paladin.
It might be a myth, but as long as it inspires people to great deeds, it should be retold.
If you are as old as I am, you don't care about time anymore.
Magic is a weapon like any other. If it is wielded by a fool, it can be disastrous.
I've just had dinner, but thanks.
A paladin has to be true like his aim. A good bow and a sure hand is not enough to bring down an enemy. It also takes a pure heart and an iron will.
The stories of vampires are always filled with romance and drama. I hope I live long enough to see then end of Yalahar's vampire story.
We will help you to improve your skills. Besides, I offer spells for paladins.
I'm 101 years old, but I don't consider myself as too old.
I don't even remember who was king at the time I left Thais.
Paladins are the best missile fighters in Tibia!
He seems like a fine man to me. A man that cares about his city and his people. This is something quite rare these days.
We will help you to improve your skills. Besides, I offer spells for paladins.
Paladins are great warriors and magicians. Moreover, we are excellent missile fighters. Many people in Tibia want to join us.
In a spellbook, your spells are listed. You will find the pronunciation of each spell in there. If you want to buy one, visit Xodet in the magic shop.
Of course, we aren't as strong as knights, but no druid or sorcerer will ever defeat a paladin with a sword.
Bye, Jogador.
pages.title: Ethan

pages.name: Golem Guardian
npc_lines: Monitoring interaction for hostilities.
Danger: Overheating.
Target locked.
Scanning human life form.
Prime Mission: protect Yalahari master.
N.O.O.B. termination initiated.
pages.title: Golem Guardian

pages.name: Gree Dee
npc_lines: Come and buy at a cheap rate!
Prepare well for your next adventure! Buy my wares!
Buy my wares!
FEEL FREE TO BUY MY ITEMS!
Be greeted esteemed customer with a full purse!
I sell general equipment. Just ask me for a trade.
You will not believe how cheap my items are.
My foolish brother thinks he'll get rich by selling equipment to some inexperienced paupers, but I know better!
Just ask me for a trade.
It's almost as if I were handing them out for free. Just ask me for a trade.
Uhm, unfortunately I just ran out of garlic necklaces. But I heard they help.
I'm not interested in trading my wares for cookies.
If I had one, I could charge a fortune for it... <gets a dreamy look>
My shop will be famous soon enough. With all the dangers that are around this city, adventurers have to resupply constantly!
The city is a virtual gold mine. People from all over the world come here to explore and to get rich ...
So they have much money to spend on supplies!
They aren't worse than other nobles or officials. To be precise, they are so uninterested in our affairs that I prefer them to other city officials.
Mr. West is a honest man, that's for sure. You'll never hear me saying something bad about Mr. West.
The surviving magicians there seem to rely on resources they get by themselves. What a shame!
If they ever rebuild that city, I really hope to participate in this venture in some way.
If you find some treasures down there, I might be interested in doing business with you.
I tried to convince them of the quality of human wares, but without success.
I think the Yalahari should leave the factories inactive. They'd only ruin honest people's profit.
I wonder where these gladiators get their supplies from? I wouldn't mind to sell them some decent equipment.
You really should have bought some extra stuff, just in case.
pages.title: Gree Dee

pages.name: Hal
npc_lines: Just a... small... really tiny... sip from that bottle...
He.. hello. Unless you have official business here or want to pass the gate, please m... move on. <clears throat>
Corporal of the Yalaharian G... Guard Force.
I'm Hal... but please don't snitch on me.
My b... boss is an Augur.
Please don't tell anyone! Really... I... I need that, else I couldn't do this job.
Mission? I don't know anything about a m... mission. What do you want from me?
Do you want to p... pass the gate? Are you headed for the arena or the alchemist quarter?
There's too much going on here... too many people... too many problems.
Oh god... I hate this city. And my j... job.
There's too much going on here... too many people... too many problems.
I d... don't know what you're talking about. Ask someone e... else.
Uhm... I... forgot.
It's an i... island east of here. N... no, I mean west!
I heard there are v... vampires.
That's north of m... me. Sometimes there are... yellow clouds... and g... green clouds. It's p... pretty.
I d... don't like the shouting coming from that quarter.
Bah! Quara! That should be called a... quarater, not a ... quarter.
I once saw the g... ghost of a woman strolling around the g... graves.
They should shut a... all of that d... down. Or have they?
D... did you see those lizards?? And other beasts? I wonder where they come f... from.
Ah, w... witches and w... warlocks!
I don't want to t... trade.
What the h... heck are you talking about?
Goodbye citizen!
pages.title: Hal

pages.name: Harlow
npc_lines: What do you want, Jogador? I'm a busy man.
Well, I'm kind of a delivery man I guess. I take on small transportation jobs with my boat.
I'm Harlow.
I have a job, you know?
I can take care of them myself. Don't need anyone to babysit me at night.
I think I saw that guy lurking around in Yalahar. He's fighting vampires and all that crazy stuff.
Bye, Jogador.
Yes, this is where we are, genius.
Want me to bring you to Vengoth again for 100 gold?
What the heck, stop bothering me with your questions.
Yes, this is where we are, genius.
Do you want me to bring you back to Yalahar for 50 gold?
Listen, just because we're business partners doesn't mean we're friends. Leave me alone unless you need a passage.
pages.title: Harlow

pages.name: A Restless Soul
npc_lines: Ahhhh! At last someone that can listen to my story!
I was captured and tortured to death by the cultists here. They worship a being that they call Ghazbaran …
In his name they have claimed the mines and started to melt the ice to free an army of vile demons that have been frozen here for ages …
Their plan is to create a new demon army for their master to conquer the world. Hjaern and the other shamans must learn about it! Hurry before it’s too late.
(O NPC não responde mas encerra o diálogo.)
pages.title: A Restless Soul

pages.name: Captain Breezelda
npc_lines: Hello Jogador. Where do you want to sail?
I'm the captain of this ship.
My name is Breezelda.
I don't care much about politics.
If you are looking for a druid, try your luck in Carlin.
The gods help those who take care of their own fate.
I heard he reappeared somewhere in the South.
The locals claim that it exists.
I've never seen one.
I don't spy on my passengers.
At least they usually don't talk too much.
They are no sailors so the ship is safe.
I believe that's how the locals call the north wind.
Last week a ship sunk between Svargrond and Carlin. Rumour has it that a ship's kobold was the reason for it.
Bye.
pages.title: Captain Breezelda

pages.name: Eirik
npc_lines: LONG LIVE JARL SVEN, THE YOUNGER!
I AM A BARBARIAN! Names are of no concern during work!! If somebody is calling for help, I will come.
It's my duty to protect Svargrond and its citizens.
The shamans still have something to do for you. You should go to Nibelor and talk to them if you haven't been there for a while.
It's a sacred place for us! Our shamans live there. Ask Iskan if you want to go there.
He is the leader of the dog sled. Last time I saw him he was with his dogs on the shelf ice north of the harbour.
West of Svargrond is the Fimbul Ice Shelf, Nibelor and Grimlund are embedded in shelf ice, and in the north of Hrodmir are several small shelf ice fields.
Fimbul Shelf is the name of the big shelf ice west of Svargrond. A good spot to go ice fishing.
Stay away from there! It's the home of the chakoyas.
This big, icy rock you're standing at right now. The raiders live in the middle and south of the big Formorgar Glacier.
You can ask Iskan to bring you with his dog sled to Nibelor.
I heard Nelly talking about runes and fluids. Ask her.
That is a little too general. For what kind of profession do you need spells?
You have to look for Hjaern.
You have to look for Romir.
You have to look for Thorwulf.
You have to look for Hawkyr.
Svargrond is the only city here. Do you want to know where to find a shop,a trainer for a profession or a guildhall?
Near the harbour you find the equipment shop, the branch of the explorer's society as well as the post office and the bank. ...
Right-hand of the depot, which is in the centre of Svargrond, you find the furniture store ...
All weapon and armor traders linger at the arena in the North and the tavern is to the west.
Wait, wait! Don't say a word, it's, it's ...
that very small guy with the hairy feet? No?
I would love to have that legendary weapon. If you find it, bring it to me!

pages.name: Halvar
npc_lines: Hello competitor! Do you want to fight in the arena or shall I explain the rules first?
My job is to explain about the rules and to get the fee from the competitors.
Well I would rather call it an 'Ultimate Challenge' than a mission.
I have no time to talk and you should FIGHT instead of wasting your time here!
Bye.
It would be better not to die! In every pit there is an emergency exit to the south. If you die in a pit... well... your corpse and backpack are gone, so enter at your own risk.
Like I said: Everything is allowed. Go in, kill monsters and try not to get killed by your own.
You can use whatever you want but be aware that you might lose items and your backpack if you die.
What do you want to know? Something about the three different difficulties, the general rules or the prices? Maybe you also want to know what happens when you die?
The fee depends on the difficulty you choose. If you are a Greenhorn you have to pay 1000 gold, as a Scrapper you have to pay 5000 gold and as a Warlord the participation fee is 10000 gold. ...
Each competitor who manages to win all ten pits will win the arena goblet and an unique item appropriate to your difficulty level.
First you pay me the participation fee according to the difficulty you choose. This will grant you access to the door near me. ...
In the next room there you will find three teleporters. They all lead to the first pit, which you can enter as soon as there is no battle going on there anymore. ...
Beware though - when you enter the pit there is no turning back and the fight will start immediately! ...
Should you notice that you have overestimated your abilities, you can run for your life and flee through the teleporter to the south of the pit. ...
However, no real barbarian would run from a fight, right? When you successfully killed your opponent, a teleporter will appear to the west that brings you to the next pit. ...
If there is still a fight going on in the pit you would proceed to, there will be a red shrine stone placed instead. ...
As soon as the warrior in the next pit leaves the area, the red shrine stone will change into a teleporter. ...
However if that warrior died, you have to walk in front of the red shrine stone to create a teleporter. ...

There is a time limit of six to seven minutes to finish each pit. When the flame of life in the upper left corner is starting to wane, you have exactly one minute left to proceed to the next room. ...
If you take longer to kill the monster and leave the room you will be kicked out dishonourably.
There are three difficulties: Greenhorn, Scrapper and Warlord. On each challenge you will be confronted with ten monsters increasing in strength. ...
Besides the glory and honour you will earn we have unique awards for those who manage to pass the arena completely.
Only the strongest among us will take this challenge. The fee is 10000 gold. If you pass that I promise you the respect of all citizens here. You will be a hero!
The most common difficulty for us. The fee is 5000 gold. So if you are experienced in fighting middle class monsters this is your challenge!
That is the easiest way in our arena. The fee is 1000 gold. We were setting this up for of our children to challenge some easy monsters and train them for the future.
So you agree to the rules and want to participate in the challenge? Which difficulty do you choose, Greenhorn, Scrapper or Warlord?
Then not. Get away and don't waste my time!
pages.title: Halvar

pages.name: Iskan
npc_lines: HAIL to the Warlord of the arena! Jogador, Hero of Svargrond! What can I do for you?
I am Iskan.
I run the dog sled service from this city to Nibelor.
I can bring you to Nibelor with the sled if you want to. Just ask for a passage.
So, do you want a passage to Nibelor my friend?
In my whole long life, I've not seen any sign of those gods the people of the south are constantly talking about.
We don't need any kings or queens. Am I right, boys? Yeah, I am.
Nasty little beasts. Me and the boys had quite some bloody encounters with them on the ice.
The yeti is real and dangerous.
Easy, boys! Don't mention that name again. Makes the boys nuts, ye know?
This city seems to be growing every day. First, there have been only a few huts and now ... look around, houses everywhere.
Yeah, where could it be. That's the question.
The icy father. We know him all too well, am I right boys? He has claimed so many old friends in all those years. So many.
I heard something about a ship crashing in the shelf ice between Nibelor and Grimlund. If I were you, I wouldn't go to chakoya terrain. It's pretty dangerous.
Farewell, Warlord of the arena, Jogador, Hero of Svargrond!

He is the paladin trainer. You find him near the arena.
You have to look for Thorwulf.
He is the trainer for knights. You find him near the arena.
You have to look for Romir.
He is an old hermit who lives in a hut on the elevated plain north of Svargrond . He is some kind of male witch, you know what I mean? ...
He knows magic and all that. Maybe he teaches his knowledge to others.
Mhmmm, Nor? Nobody with that name lives here in Svargrond. Maybe he is one of the southerners that came here.
You have to look for Hjaern.
He is one of our shamans and trainer for druids. He lives on Nibelor.
The guild masters for paladins and knights are at the arena, the shamans on Nibelor surely can teach druids new things ...
and Romir the old hermit who lives in a cave north of Svargrond may have some knowledge concerning magic.

In the city you will find three guildhalls. Frost Manor is on top of the cliff ...
Crystal Glance is north of the depot at the street which leads to the arena and Mammoth Belly is to the south, near the furrier quarter.
If you think you are strong enough, then try to fight there. You have to challenge waves of monsters that get stronger and stronger. ...
The entrance to the arena is a stairway north of the town, left of the town gate.

pages.name: Sven
npc_lines: Be greeted, Jogador!

I am Sven the Younger. My father, Sven the Elder has been missing in the ice waste since I was young. But unless one of our people is buried properly, we assume that he is still in the realm of the living ...
Therefore, I am still known as 'the Younger', even though I have grown old.
I am the jarl of my people. It's an honour and I am very proud of it.
Our people are simple and honest. We don't like the scheming ways of the city dwellers that live on the main continent.
I am more than just the spokesman and highest judge among my people. I don't raise taxes, and when the clans feel that it is necessary, I will be replaced by another jarl.
We don't need any kings and queens here. Being the jarl of my people, I see that the laws are followed.
Even here we heard about this powerful man. Travellers from the south only dare to whisper his name.
On the campfire, there are numerous tales about this weapon. It's told that it has been missing since ages ...
In my opinion, the power and fame of a weapon shouldn't exceed the power and fame of it's wielder. And I have not heard of any hero whose fame would surpass that of excalibug.
A true barbarian is something special among our people. Everyone who wants to become a barbarian will have to pass the barbarian test.
You might become an honorary barbarian if you manage to pass the barbarian test.
You have braved all three tests and are now an honorary barbarian.
There is something evil going on. I have it in my bones.
There is something in the air that worries me. A great evil is threatening all of us ...
I might not have the gift of dreams that foresee the future like my mother did, but I seem to have inherited some of her gift nonetheless. Sometimes I just feel that something is about to happen ...
And this time it's something sinister and evil that threatens us all.
We heard that this mythical dwarf lives somewhere on the southern Ice Islands.
Our people lived as nomads some generations ago. The contact with Carlin taught us another way of living ...
We did not like everything about it but we are not stupid. We have seen the many advantages ...
If you cannot adapt to this land, you are dead and so we adapted to it and built this city. When the contact to Carlin got lost during the years of the serpents, we kept this city alive ...
And we survived, even though the raiders did their best to make us fail.
For more than two generations no ship had reached our shores because the giant sea serpents attacked and sank most ships that tried to travel here ...
Not long ago the sea serpents disappeared as suddenly as they had come. Now ships visit us again on a regular base.
In the past, all barbarian tribes roamed the lands of Chyll as nomads. When the Carliners came here and the trade flourished, we used the resources to build this permanent settlement ...
Some of our people claimed that it was wrong to settle down and to abandon the ancient ways. A female shaman rose in the ranks of those who opposed the erection of a settlement ...
She gathered all those who were not content, who did not want any foreign influence and who refused to learn ...
They tried to destroy everything our ancestors had built, but with the help of the Carliners they were stopped and driven away. Now they still roam the land and attack everyone they see ...
They became the raiders, our worst enemy. Nowadays, there are three larger tribes that often build camps in the South of our land ...
And after all those years, surviving several generations, this female shaman is still their leader.
A long time ago when the trade with Carlin was flourishing, people actually worked in the mines. ...
During the years of the serpents, the mines had been abandoned. Later, the raiders took shelter there, although they blame us for living in a fortified city ...
Now, the traders of Carlin are back but some other foreigners seem to have claimed the mines from the raiders ...

It's neither our business nor would we have the manpower to help them to recapture the mines. Also, if they do not have the strength to get the mines back on their own, they don't deserve them anyway.
We know of father Chyll and his freezing breath. We care little for other gods. It is foolish to meddle with beings that are so powerful ...
We leave it to the druids and shamans to handle such affairs.
Father north wind is called Chyll by our people. He is an unforgiving hunter. He knows no mercy with the weak ...
Chyll is a harsh god and the best you can do is to avoid his attention. Only the shamans and druids deal with him.

Most shaman and druids of our people live on the sacred isle Nibelor. There, they divine the future, calm the wrath of father Chyll and prepare the dead for their last travel to the lands of Everspring.
Nibelor has always been a sacred place for our people. The druids and shamans live there.
Everspring is the realm of the dead. It is a place of peace and harmony where those who boldly braved the challenges of life dwell for eternity and share stories at the campfires after a hunt ...
Every true barbarian that is properly brought into afterlife will join the great hunt in Everspring where the animals are fat and have the thickest furs.
I don't care what people who come here believe in. If they provoke father Chyll, he will take care of them on his own. If their gods prove to be more powerful than Chyll, they might deserve to live.
We are friends of the Carliners. Still we don't allow their politics to influence our way to handle things here.
We have heard only little about this far away place.
We understand that our friends from Carlin are wary with the realm ruled by Thais but this is not of our concern.
We did not allow them to stay here. This had nothing to do with our friendship with Carlin but for the way they handled things and their harmful approach to go hunting.
The chakoyas are neither beast nor man. Yet, they share the worst and more dangerous traits of both of them. Their small and furry appearance can be very misleading at first glance ...
But as soon as you've seen a pack of chakoyas literally shredding a mammoth into pieces with their claws and teeth, all misconceptions will be gone.

The yetis are mythical beasts. Only few that encountered those creatures lived to tell the tale. The chakoyas worship them as divine beings, although they have no real relations to them as far as we can tell.

I met some of those little people in the past. Considering our experience with the chakoyas, we don't underestimate someone just for its look. And those dwarfs proved indeed to be powerful, courageous and enduring.
Some time ago, a few elves came here but they could not stand the cold and so they left pretty soon. Most likely it was Nibelor in which they have been interested.
May wind and weather be with you, Jogador.
pages.title: Sven

pages.name: Iriana
npc_lines: Pilferer! Thief!!
Help! Stop that thief!
Are you here to help me? That masked guy has stolen my complete daily earnings! Ask me for a quest if you are willing to help me.
My name is Iriana and my family lives here in Yalahar since the early days.
I'm selling fishing equipment. You know, this isn't only the trade quarter. Most people here earn their bread and butter on the sea with a fishing rod in their hands.
Take a look.
You can still see the brilliance of this city in its centre. It's a pity that the slow decay of the other quarters persists.
It's the domicile of the Yalahari who created this city after the God Wars. Today, the Yalahari try to let the city shine in its former brilliancy again.

The city once had 8 quarters excluding the centre. Right now you are in the former trade quarter, east of it you find the factory quarter. Further to the north-east you find the quarter known as the sunken quarter ...

followed by the magician quarter. Then you have the most northern quarter, known as the cemetery quarter, and west of that you find the former alchemist quarter. The most western quarter is the former zoo and arena quarter ...
and last but not least there is the foreigner quarter. If you want to know more about one of the single quarters, just ask me about it.
<whispers> It's all controlled by the trade baron. Stay out of his business, or you'll regret it, I promise.

Not much is known about the things going on there, or what has been produced in these factories. From time to time, the Yalahari 'appoint' inhabitants to work for them there but none of them was ever seen again.

It used to be a high society residential quarter, but as you probably realised, the city grew larger than the landmass on which it had been erected. So the quarter just broke off and sunk into the sea. That happened a very long time ago.

Nowadays, the magician quarter is the home of all magic using races. You find different races using various kinds of magic in this quarter. It can be quite dangerous there depending on which part of the quarter you enter.
Back in the days, the Yalahari caught all kinds of animals just for their own pleasure. After their disappearance, the animals escaped. They are on the loose in this quarter ever since.
In the centre of the Zoo quarter, you'll find a huge arena. Once gladiators have been battling each other to amuse the Yalahari. The most skilful of them survived and are still there.
The whole quarter is sealed up. Undead creatures took over a long time time ago. It's a mess!

I doubt that a single alchemist survived the catastrophe. There was a huge explosion which caused a chain reaction. Nowadays, it's an infested and burnt down quarter in which it is more likely to meet a mutant than a human.

The quarter west of the waterway is nowadays inhabited by various races. It used to be a residential area, but almost got completely destroyed after the downfall of Yalahar. Only the harbour promenade still contains the original buildings. ...
The other parts of the quarter have been rebuilt by the newly arrived races. For this reason, you find all those different building styles there.
Bye bye Jogador.
pages.title: Iriana

pages.name: Soilance
npc_lines: Come in and buy my delicious meat!
Hi, Jogador. I assume you are here for a good old trade.
I supply this part of the city with meat.
Of course, take a look at the great food I sell.
They are .. uhm just there to get rid of the garbage. Don't pay them any attention.
I .. import that meat from several sources which I cannot reveal for the safety of my small profit.
He should care more about the city instead of harassing innocent traders like me.
I offer ham or meat. If you'd like to see my offers, ask me for a trade.
I offer ham or meat. If you'd like to see my offers, ask me for a trade.
They are rather scary. I wish those attacks would stop.
No, haven't heard about that.
No, I don't sell cookies. And I don't want to buy any either. This is a MEAT store!
The city has some severe problems. Thanks to me the supply of meat is a smaller problem, though.
I haven't even seen one in my life.
The people there are way too poor to buy anything, so they better stay away from my store.
They shouldn't allow anyone to go there at all. If they do, they risk the spreading of the plague in the rest of the city.
I have an agreement with Mr. West which provides that I supply his people with meat.
The creatures in the arena are lean and their meat tastes stale. Nothing like the meat I'm selling!
They used to fish there a lot, but fish seems to become quite rare lately. Luckily, I provide the city with delicious meat!
I heard nothing good about this quarter.
Those barbaric monsters have no taste at all.
I have an agreement with Mr. West which provides that I supply his people with meat.
You'll come back when you are hungry enough.
pages.title: Soilance

pages.name: Julius
npc_lines: Be greeted, adventurer Jogador. Please excuse me if I appear distracted!
I come from a family of vampire hunters, but to be honest, I'm more into the theoretic part and strategic planning.
My name is Julius.
Our nightly blood-sucking visitors put the inhabitants of Yalahar in constant danger.
A better name would be Gomorrah, if you ask me.
Storkus? Oh yes, I know him. A long time ago we used to hunt together... sometimes.
It's about time you showed the vampires that they should never bother the citizens again.
I'll reward you for every pair of vampire teeth you bring me.
Another vampire raid last night. But then again, that's nothing new.
Well, I should be the one to thank you I guess.
Good bye, Jogador. Never trust anyone.
pages.title: Julius

pages.name: Redward
npc_lines: Are you looking at me!?
Hi there. Welcome to my humble post office.
Believe it or not, I'm the local post officer. Don't give me that look. It's a long story how I ended up with this job.
You may call me Redward.
I guess I don't look really appetising to them. Being a big red monster and all that has its advantages I guess.
With our mail system you can send letters and parcels to other Tibians. I can either explain how letters and parcels work or sell them to you if you ask me for a trade.
Here. Don't forget that you need to buy a label too if you want to send a parcel. Always write the name of the receiver in the first line and make sure you entered it correctly.
Now, don't be nervous, I'm just your average next door imp.
Have you seen my belly?? I'm on a diet. But thanks, kid.
Ah well, sometimes I just can't help it. Then I must do something very evil, things like throwing around parcels who are labelled as fragile, and other stuff like that, you know?
Oh well. My master was a dark wizard, not like Ferumbras, more the wannabe type ...

He was rather ambitious than competent, and he tended to blame me for all of his failures. Well, I have to admit I made fun of his mistakes quite often, and I might have spilled some of his spell ingredients now and then .. accidentally of course ...
Still, that's no reason to lock me into a bottle and throw me into the sea.
To make a long story short: I left my master after a dispute, and after a long and perilous journey, I arrived at this city ...
I quit being evil and became a postman.
I sell parcels and letters. Ask me for a trade if you're interested. I can also explain how the mail system works.
The city is kind of a melting pot when it comes to civilisations and races. Such a mixture becomes quickly explosive, though. This will turn out very interesting.
Quite an arrogant bunch if you ask me. But at least they allow almost everyone to settle here.
It's really a shame that it's no longer possible to watch humans slaughter each other for the amusement of the masses.
Too wet for my taste.
Ahh, all that noise and the smoke and the smell and the whining of working humans - it must have been terrific.
Now those guys know how to party.
Humans that tamper with magic - that must end up in something funny.
Bye for now, Jogador.
pages.title: Redward

pages.name: Lucius
npc_lines: Bring some light to the world in these dark days!
It's the time of the year where we all need some light.
Meet me tomorrow and you shall learn more.
Greetings, Jogador.
My name is Lucius.
Well, I use to call myself a 'lightbearer'. I provide magical torches to light fires at places where hellish creatures are trying to enter our world, thus fending them off.
Let's not talk here. I prefer to meet you in the Temple of Light. Will you accompany me there now?
Come join me in my room. (Você será transportado ao Temple of Light)
Greetings, Jogador! We have no time to waste. Let's talk about an urgent mission.

This is the time of the year where demons try hardest to break through to our world. I try my best to keep them away by spiritually empowering those magical fire basins here in the Temple of Light. ...
However, I cannot be everywhere at the same time, and there are ten spots all over Tibia where the layer between our world and the hellish world is especially thin. ...
You need to travel to these places within a day after I gave you a magical torch. I summoned a lightbearer's basin there, similar to those here in the temple. ...
You have to use the torch on a basin to power its light. Then it will have regain enough energy to burn brightly for another two hours. ...
If you look at a basin, you can see how much energy there is still left. As long as all fire basins are burning, no creatures will be able to enter Tibia. ...
However, when only one fire basin turns dark and disappears, powerful demons will be unleashed onto this world. ...
You have to keep the fire burning for five days, and on the last day the demons will be so weakened that you can dispose of them easily when they come. ...
I can give you only one torch which lasts for a day and will then disappear. Also, you can only use your torch ONCE on each basin. ...
Thus you need to work together with your fellow Tibians, so that someone can always keep the fire basins burning, on each of the five days. ...
I can either give you the torch now - but remember it will only last for a day - or hold onto it for you until your time to be a lightbearer has come. Do you want that torch right now?
Good, then wait for a while. But don't wait too long.
Here is your torch, Jogador. Please try to keep all ten spots burning, and remember you can only use your torch ONCE on each spot. ...
And be careful - evil might send its minions there from time to time to keep you from lighting the basin.
There are ten of these fire basins all over Tibia. Ask me for any number between one and ten to learn more about the location where it can be found.

This is the time of the year where demons try hardest to break through to our world. I try my best to keep them away by spiritually empowering those magical fire basins here in the Temple of Light. ...
However, I cannot be everywhere at the same time, and there are ten spots all over Tibia where the layer between our world and the hellish world is especially thin. ...
You need to travel to these places after I gave you a magical torch. I summoned a lightbearer's basin there, similar to those here in the temple. ...
You have to use the torch on a basin to power its light. Then it will have regain enough energy to burn brightly for another two hours. ...
If you look at a basin, you can see how much energy there is still left. As long as all fire basins are burning, no creatures will be able to enter Tibia. ...
However, when only one fire basin turns dark and disappears, powerful demons will be unleashed onto this world. ...
You have to keep the fire burning for five days, and on the last day the demons will be so weakened that you can dispose of them easily when they come. ...
I can give you only one torch, and you can only use it ONCE on each basin. ...
Thus you need to work together with your fellow Tibians, so that someone can always keep the fire basins burning, on each of the five days, on each of the ten spots.
Those magical torches burn for much longer than normal torches. They will also protect you while you carry them. If you are willing to take on this mission, let me know.
There are ten of these fire basins all over Tibia. Ask me for any number between one and ten to learn more about the location where it can be found.
The first place might be somewhat hard to find... it is on the Formorgar Glacier on Svargrond.
The second place is in the Plains of Havoc near the Knightwatch Tower.
The third place is under the taboo area of Port Hope.
The fourth place is in the prison under Kazordoon.
The fifth place is on Ramoa, one of the Forbidden Islands close to Liberty Bay.
The sixth place is in the northern ruins of Edron, near the entrance to the demon lair.
The seventh place is deep under Drefia, at the top of the pentagram.
The eighth place is in the middle of Hellgate. It can be found close to a necromantic ritual place.
The ninth place is not very dangerous to reach. It is near Ankrahmun, in the tomb that's covered with tar pits.
The tenth place is quite close to here. Go to the area of the Magician Quarter where the earth is broken up and hellish creatures are crawling to the surface. ...
Go one level down through one of the holes and search for the fire basin in this area.
If you would like to trade any shards you might have for gold coins, just do so.
Farewell and safe journeys, Jogador.
pages.title: Lucius

pages.name: Tamara
npc_lines: Welcome to my little place, Jogador. How may I help you?
I'm a druid. I teach spells to other druids.
I'm known as Tamara, though my friends also nickname me Tamera.
Sorry, I don't teach spells for your vocation.
Your vocation is your profession. There are four vocations in Tibia: druids, paladins, knights, and sorcerers.
Druids are in close communion with nature. Some of them are also close to their inner beast.
Sorcerers are very aggressive. They use their power to fight and to kill.
Their animalistic rage and their passion for battles are somewhat impressive. If they only understood the animal in them, they could gain much more power.
They restrict themselves way too much. All this talk about holiness and divine will is pointless. Still, their devotion is admirable.
Eh, I haven't seen daylight for a long time. So, don't ask me, what time it is.
Another weapon of destruction. I hope nobody will ever find it.
