I came here to get away from evil creatures like him, but here I've found other curses.
Thank you honey, but I pass on that offer.
He is nothing than a puppy of its uncaring masters.
Fortunately they never come here.
Oh! That cursed stone! I know about it, but I can't tell you anything. Evil gems like that shouldn't be passed around, only a crazy fool would do that.
Everyone who becomes a druid has the opportunity to learn many magic spells.
Crunor, the father of all trees, is a symbol of life.
Our members use their magic power to protect their life and the life of other creatures.
News are of little value in a city that old.
The city is dying, I can feel it. Not only in a physical sense, but also in a spiritual one.
They have lost connection to their city, to their people, to the world. They are lost.
The breath of life is no longer blowing over this quarter. The beast of the plaque is lurking in every shady corner, and no hunter can bring it down.
A scorpion will always be a scorpion.
The pack is always looking for a leader.
They thought they could tame magic, but magic devoured them.
The gladiators are to some extent in touch with their inner beast. Still, sometimes they are the prey rather than the predator.
It is inevitable that mother nature will claim what was once hers.
They tried to cage the forces of nature to have them work for them. Now the factories are silent and covered with dust. Those who thought to have mastered nature are gone, while nature is still here.
Farewell.
pages.title: Tamara

pages.name: Tamoril
npc_lines: FCHHHHH!
GRRRRRRR!
Come a little closer mortal.
Another pesky mortal who believes his gold outweighs his nutrition value.
I share some of my eternal knowledge of spells with you humans ... for a price of course. You should be grateful.
My real name is not pronounceable for a human.
You puny mortals are an annoyance. However, the little magic your simple minds are able to comprehend earns me enough money not to kill you.
I share some of my eternal knowledge of spells with you humans ... for a price of course. You should be grateful.
Dragons are the most powerful creatures of the world. Every year, we gain more and more power. ...
Hardly anyone of us dies of old age. Instead we find death by diseases brought to our race by you mortal pests, and countless of my younger brethren and sisters have been slaughtered by humans. ...
Expect little from me mortal. And even for that little, you will have to pay dearly.
What you call magic is only a pale shadow of real magic. The more you try, the more magic will retreat from you. ...
To us dragons magic comes natural. It is a part of us, and not a tool we have to learn to control like you do.
I can teach you rune spells and instant spells. What kind of spell do you wish to learn? You can also tell me for which level you would like to learn a spell, if you prefer that.
Gods are of no use for us dragons. One day, a dragon will become old and powerful enough to destroy all gods. Fear that day mortal, from then on the age of the dragons will have begun.
If I had one, I'd surely add it to my treasure and not give it to you.
I usually prefer to plunder instead of a fair trade. However, I have enough gold and could use some more shiny valuables.

It is told that the First Dragon had four descendants, who became the ancestors of the four kinds of dragons we know in Tibia. They perhaps still have knowledge about the First Dragon's whereabouts - if one could find them.
The First Dragon? The first of all of us? The Son of Garsharak? I'm surprised you heard about him. It is such a long time that he wandered Tibia. Yet, there are some rumours.
Brog the Raging Titan once released as much of a painful flame into the world as he could. The searing fire mixed with his rage, and from it rose Garsharak, the progenitor of all dragons. ...
He sired the first dragon that wandered the world of Tibia and later a whole race of intelligent, giant lizards, a race that would eventually bring terror and chaos into the world.

The names of these four are Tazhadur, Kalyassa, Gelidrazah and Zorvorax. Not only were they the ancestors of all dragons after but also the primal representation of the draconic incitements. About whom do you want to learn more?

He was the firstborn among the four, the primal dragon, the kind so many of you know. He saw no advantage in choosing any special aspect or element. So he became the ancestor of all common dragons. These days he's hiding in a secret lair.
She was Tazhadur's younger sister, lofty and imperious. She declared herself a dragon empress and thus became the ancestress of all dragon lords. These days she's hiding in a secret lair

She was also called the Frozen because she chose to inhabit the icy wastes in the north of Tibia, today known as Svargrond. She is the ancestress of the frost dragons. These days she's hiding in a secret lair

He was once a dragon of air and storm. But he chose undeath and transformed himself into an undead dragon. And thus all his children became undead monstrosities, too. These days he's hiding in a secret lair
What didn't you understand about the word secret, little human? What do you want to do, if you know about these mighty dragons' abodes? Go there and look for a fight?

The names of these four are Tazhadur, Kalyassa, Gelidrazah and Zorvorax. Not only were they the ancestors of all dragons after but also the primal representation of the draconic incitements. About whom do you want to learn more?

Each kind of dragon has its own incitement, an important aspect that impels them and occupies their mind. For the common dragons this is the lust for power, for the dragon lords the greed for treasures. ...
The frost dragons' incitement is the thirst for knowledge and for the undead dragons it's the desire for life, as they regret their ancestor's mistake. ...
These incitements are also a kind of trial that has to be undergone if one wants to find the First Dragon's four descendants.
The lust for power is connected to the urge to kill and the delight in bloodshed. This trial means to kill two hundred dragons. Only if you do this you will be able to enter Tazhadur's secret lair.

The greed for treasures is connected to the hoarding of gold and the seeking for gems. This trial means to find at least five ancient dragon hoards spread all over this world. Only if you do this you will be able to enter Kalyassa's secret lair.

If I knew where they are any efforts to find them would be futile. In this case the treasures would be here in my hoard. But no, unfortunately I don't know. I guess an old book about dragon hoards exists in some library. But I don't remember the place.
The thirst for knowledge is connected to learning and the love for ancient myths. This trial means to answer some questions. I don't know anything about these questions. ...
I assume you will learn more about them when you find the portal to the secret lair. Only if you can answer the questions you will be able to enter Gelidrazah's lair.

The desire for life is connected to the restlessness of undeath and the longing for days long lost. This trial means to visit three places connected to the power of living. Only if you do this you will be able to enter Zorvorax' secret lair.

I never thought about it, little human. Perhaps it could be something connected to the elves. Or a druidic site. Or maybe it is something symbolic. Like water in the desert, that kind of romantic stuff.
What do you want to do, if you know about these mighty dragons' abodes? Go there and look for a fight?
The city is dying. It is mortal just like you and for this reason, it is insignificant. I will still be around when this city is long forgotten.
They are strange beings at best. If I had any interest in mortals, I might be curious. Regardless of what they claim, they smell of mortality.
I'm not surprised about the things that happened there. Humans are unable to handle the higher forces.
Another bunch of humans who dabbles in the arcane arts to become godlike beings.
I'm not surprised about the things that happened there. Humans are unable to handle the higher forces.
You humans are unable to live on your own. You rely on your little tools and protection. Your sheer inferiority makes me sick.
That was only the beginning. I will be there when everything comes to an end.
A museum of races who will sooner or later be wiped out.
Sometimes I fly there for some exercise.
I'm not interested in your human quarrels.
Come back if you dare, Jogador.
pages.title: Tamoril

pages.name: Zarak
npc_lines: I sssmell humansss!
Greetingsss, Jogador. What do you want?
I teach the artsss of the warrior. I know ssseveral ssspellsss I might ssshare with a worthy knight.
Your vocation isss your professsion. There are four vocationsss in Tibia: knightsss, paladinsss, sssorcerersss, and druidsss.
What you clumsssy humannsss call fighting looksss asss akwardly asss a bear trying to catch a fly. True warriorsss fight with ssskill rather than with power.
They try to massster the powersss of nature, but they fail to sssee the sssnake in the grasss.
They dabble with powersss far older than their art. One day thisss power will ssswallow them all.
The great ssserpent wouldn't allow that sssuch a weapon exisssted.
Magic isss a tool of the godsss. Only holy men are allowed to wield sssuch power. You humansss play way too freely with magic.
A wind of change isss blowing in Yalahar.
Sssoft and without pride. The choice of a ssservant tellsss much about itsss massster.
A true warrior doesssn't need jewellery.
Your warm-blooded brain can't comprehend the waysss of the great ssserpent.
Sorry, I don't teach spells for your vocation.
In a ssspellbook, your ssspells are lisssted. You will find the pronunciation of each ssspell in there.
The world is nothing but an egg of the great ssserpent.
You sssoft ssskinsss rely too much on armor and weaponsss. A true warrior usssesss hisss whole body asss a weapon.
My people know a lot about lossst greatnesss. Ssstill, don't expect to sssee me mourning.
They can't hide under their rock forever. Asss sssoon asss they leave their shelter, the predatorsss will ssstrike.
If you want to die by a plague, jussst go there!
I don't mind that thisss ssstinking factoriesss are out of busssinesss.
What a foolish idea to open the city for the enemy!
Sssoft ssskinned humansss are to obsssessed with magic.
Now the quara rule at a place which once belonged to the city.
The gladiatorsss know to fight, but they don't know how to battle.
We'll meet again.
pages.title: Zarak

pages.name: Morpel
npc_lines: Buy a weapon before your enemy does!
<whispers> Morpel clean the shop, Morpel wash your hand .. stupid cyclops, jawoll!
WEAPONS! ARMOR! HIGHEST QUALITY, JAWOLL!
Hello! Welcome to my shop!
I have an incredible assortment of weapons and armor for sale. Just ask me for a trade.
No, I don't sell that, sorry.
I'm only allowed to eat during my break.
Uhm <whispers> just between you and me. That cyclops with this unpronounceable name is the owner of this store. I just do all the talking and trade ...
I get a decent share of the profit though. It seems he is more interested in this smithing stuff than in getting rich.
My offers are weapons, armors, helmets, legs, and shields. If you'd like to see my offers, ask me for a trade.
Of course, just browse through my wares.
I guess for a city that does not consist of caves, it's ok.
Can't say much about them. It's not like they would interact much with anyone from the outer city.
We can only hope that this catastrophe was a one-time occurrence. We dwarfs live long enough to make it likely that I'm around when another part of the city might sink, jawoll.
Mr. West often buys weapons and armor for his men. I think that proves the quality of my wares.
The people in that quarter are desperate enough to attack any strangers. So if you are planning on going there, be well armed and prepared.
I can't say I have the guts to pay this quarter a visit.
For me magic is just scary.
As a smith I know better than to underestimate the power of fire, jawoll. It seems the alchemists never learnt this lesson.
Now and then, one of the gladiators comes here to by some piece of equipment. Usually they simply use what they loot from slain visitors.
You really should have bought some extra stuff, just in case.
pages.title: Morpel

pages.name: Oiriz
npc_lines: Gems and precious jewellery for sale!
<mumbles> My poor old bones. This weather is killing me!
Hi! How nice of you to visit my gem shop!
I'm Oiriz Stonedigger.
Selling only the finest jewels!
Back home there was too much competition for an old dwarf like me. I prefer a peaceful life with enough time for my stuff.
It's a shame that I have to sell my precious gems to igno.. uhm customers who might not appreciate their value.
Well, I sell gems and goblets. If you'd like to see my offers, ask me for a trade.
Ah, our newest import! We have golden goblets, silver goblets and bronze goblets. All of them have space for a hand-written dedication.
I heard they appreciate beauty, even though they are beasts.
You can buy and sell small diamonds, sapphires, rubies, emeralds and amethysts or sell topazes.
There are white and black pearls you can buy or sell, as well as giant green and brown pearls which you can sell.
Haha, they are not meant to be owned by ordinary humans. Sorry, but no.
I'm not a fan of sweets.
Currently you can purchase wedding rings, golden amulets, and ruby necklaces. We also buy gold ingots.
We don't trade with them.
Here, take a look.
They are as rare as the most valuable gems. Yet, I can't say they are as much in demand as jewels.
This city has turned into an uncut diamond over the centuries. Perhaps one day someone will come and cut it.
I guess the technomancers back in Kazordoon would love all those machines.
Plagues and destruction hold this quarter in a firm grip. Not many of the people who went there looking for treasures have ever returned.
Well, it seems those magicians really messed things up.
Humans come, humans go. Considering the shortness of a human's life span, I wouldn't bother much about a crime lord in this quarter.
They have quite rough attitudes in this quarter. You'll only earn respect if you fight for it...
This quarter is way too wet as that any dwarf with some self-esteem would care about.
Those gladiators have an even worse temper than a drunken dwarf. And a drunken dwarf has quite a bad temper, I tell you.
Good bye! Always remember where to buy the best gems and jewellery in the world!
pages.title: Oiriz

pages.name: Pugwah
npc_lines: Food! Food! Best food in world from best cook in world!
Uh, a brave customer! Me happy to serve you delicious food and drinks.
Me great cook! Only ingredients most rotten find way in my stews!
Me Pugwah.
Me came here with little canoe. Great storm making bshhhh bshhh! Trying to drown little Pugwah! But no no! Pugwah row row row and escape! Then long long only water. ...
But Pugwah have fishing rod. Many fish and drinking rain making Pugwah's stomach sick but then Pugwah seeing city! At first Pugwah wanting eat everyone in city but Pugwah small and lonely. ...

But Pugwah also smart very much! Hunting rats and selling stew Pugwah become rich! Soon buy old house and making tavern! Every one comes and eats! Stupid people selling rotten stuff so cheap, Pugwah making fortune by cooking it!
Me find him in box with exquisite stinky old meat I ordered!
Biiiiig city. Soooo many opportunity to find something rotten to make a stew or sausage!
Me bite back!! Pugwah swear!
No thanks. Me mummy says no take food from strangers.
Food has to be rotten to gain flavour! No need for expensive spices!
Me offer bread, cheese, ham, or meat. And drinks. If you like? Ask Pugwah for trade.
Good, good! Take look at yummy food good Pugwah sells.
Big red crystal. Some people talk about it in my tavern. But strange people those are!
I know people go there, come back green as dworc!
Big chieftain West there master is.
People there mean, I don't go there. Thinking they want to eat Pugwah.
Big bad voodoo they making. Stay away! Stay away!
Now fish there live.
Good area for hunt.
Lot of different people around in quarter.
Coming back soon to taste me special meat, Jogador.
pages.title: Pugwah

pages.name: Serafin
npc_lines: Welcome to my fruit and vegetable store, Jogador! Ask me for a trade if you'd like to see my wares.
Oh, I'm selling fruits and veggies as you can see. If you want to have a closer look, ask me for a trade.
I'm Serafin, pleased to meet you.
I think that poor guy has serious trust issues... must be hard if you are obsessed with the idea that everyone is your enemy or a monster.
I think he runs a bar in the former trade quarter.
Oh yes, I see him often. Nice guy.
A man of the seas.
I like him, but unfortunately I don't have much time to chat with him anymore.
Oh, sure, take a look!
I don't know what you're talking about.
This is a fruit store. No slaughterhouse.
It'd be better for you to leave now.
Oh, this lovely city is a great place to live and to do business.
Well, actually this is not a quarter but the city centre.
I'm so sorry, but I don't sell garlic.
There's something about these words which makes me feel awkward. Or maybe it's you who causes that feeling. You better get lost.
Sorry, but I already have a delivery boy.
Good bye, my dear customer.
pages.title: Serafin

pages.name: Vincent
npc_lines: Bows, crossbows and ammunition for sale.
Hello, Jogador. If you are interested in distance weapons or ammunition, ask me for a trade.
I sell things that make your life in the city safer. My bows, crossbows, and ammunition are the best you can get.
For you I'm Vincent. That will have to do.
My offers are bows, crossbows and ammunition. If you'd like to see my offers, ask me for a trade.
Of course, just browse through my wares.
I have normal arrows, sniper arrows, flaming arrows, shiver arrows, flash arrows, earth arrows and onyx arrows used with bows. Just ask me for a trade.
I have bolts, piercing bolts and power bolts used with crossbows.
What use does a sword, an axe, or a mace have when the guy you are fighting kills you with a few well-placed shots? Distance weapons are the better choice, I tell you!
Well, I sell spears, bows, crossbows and ammunition for distance fighting. Ask me for a trade if you're interested to see my wares.
I don't buy used bows. If you want to buy one, just ask me for a trade.
I don't buy used crossbows. If you want to buy one, just ask me for a trade.
What's that supposed to be? Anyway, I don't sell it.
I sell things that make your life in the city safer. My bows, crossbows, and ammunition are the best you can get.
I don't want others to talk about me, and I also don't talk about others. Easiest way to stay out of trouble.
I don't trust strangers enough to take food from them.
Yes, I sell spears. Ask me for a trade if you're interested to see my wares.
Why do you think I've built this defensive fortification?!
In its golden age, this city must have been a joy for Kurik's eye. Even today you can still see some of its former glory here and there.
They must have been great inventors in the past. Nowadays not much of that is left. I guess they were foolish enough to let things slide.
Good bye.
pages.title: Vincent

pages.name: Jimmy
npc_lines: Get him!!
Not bad, not bad... why did you follow me?
Hello my friend. What's up?
Guess what? I'm a thief!
People call me Jimmy Swiftfinger.
What's that? Never heard of it.
This city is a huge jail with its keepers in the middle. I've never seen its former brilliance so I rather see it in a negative light.
I don't like them and I can't see how they should ever have managed to build a city like this. I mean, they were never able to organise that many people.
Some dwarfs live in Yalahar but they are not very talkative. I have no clue where they came from.
Never heard of that.
This island is weird. It's definitely no ordinary mist that covers the island most of the days. To me it looks more like....steam from a chimney.
I've never been there because there is no reason to go. It is cold and the island is small and meagre.
We had a deal and I kept my word, so what do you want? You'd better leave now.
I don't kill people.
I was a little boy when the quarter blew up. It was a huge explosion and the stench was evil. No one made it out there alive. Every living being mutated into some monster.
What are they producing there anyway? Tell me if you find out.
I sneaked in once. You have to know that it is not allowed for 'normal' citizens like me to enter. They carry out dark experiments there, that's for sure.
No one knows what really happened there. The whole quarter is overrun with undead and demonic creatures. It's the work of the mages if you ask me.
A smart person like you has surely seen that most of the city has grown larger than the island it was built on. The Yalahari built metal construction to enlarge the city. ...
Well, in the case of the sunken quarter, it didn't work out. The whole quarter broke away and sunk into the sea.
The foreigner quarter is almost as shabby as the trade quarter. Be careful there or you might get in trouble.

I like the zoo quarter. I often go there and watch the animals. One advice, though: Stay away from the arena! The gladiators there are always up for a fight and there are rumours about some very strong undead gladiators deep down under the arena.
Watch your back, Jogador.
pages.title: Jimmy

pages.name: Karith
npc_lines: This weather is killing me. If I only had enough money to retire.
Hello! Tell me what's on your mind. Time is money.
I'm the captain of this ship. Now and then a Yalahari wants to make a trip around the isle. ...
It's a special privilege, although a rare one.
I'm Karith. I don't belong to a caste any longer, and only serve the Yalahari.
For the sake of profit, we established ship routes to Ab'Dendriel, Darashia, Venore, Ankrahmun, Port Hope, Thais, Liberty Bay and Carlin. I can also sail you to Travora, if you want.
I guess as soon as you are leaving, I'll be fine.
I'm sure the Yalahari possess more powerful weapons than that.
I leave them in peace, they leave me in peace. Whatever.
I'm not interested in stuff like that.
The power of the Yalahari will ward off all monsters.
I bet his power is nothing compared to the awesome might of the Yalahari.
I've got no contact to other elves, my family came here a generation ago.
Luckily, those little diggers are a rare sight here.
Gods are useless at best and a danger at worst.
I'm too busy to bother about rumours.
I doubt that you can do anything that would be useful for me!
The Yalahari are wiser and more powerful than you could ever imagine. You won't be able to understand the extent of their power. It's a pity there are only so few left.
The city was a marvel to behold. It is certain that its ruin was caused by too many foreigners.
I must admit this bug milk is something special. The rich Yalahari might be quite fond of it. Do you want a passage to Ab'Dendriel for 150 gold?
The Yalahari seem to be obsessed with conserving their dead, so I guess the embalming fluid will be a great success in Yalahar. Do you want a passage to Ankrahmun for 220 gold?
The evergreen flower pots are an amusing item that might find some customers here. Do you want a passage to Carlin for 175 gold?

Of course it is merely superstition that the darashian sand wasp honey brings back youth and vitality, but as long people pay a decent price, I couldn't care less. Do you want a passage to Darashia for 200 gold?
Astonishing enough the royal satin seems to suit the exquisite taste of the Yalahari. Do you want a passage to Thais for 190 gold?
The rum of this city seems .. adequate for the taste of some inhabitants. Do you want a passage to Liberty Bay for 265 gold?
The swamp spice will turn out very lucrative considering that it helps to make even the most disgusting dish taste good. Do you want a passage to Venore for 175 gold?
Ivory is highly prized by the artisans of the Yalahari. Do you want a passage to Port Hope for 250 gold?
Travora is the place for the character world transfer, so if you travel there make sure you actually do want to change worlds. Do you want to purchase a new daily ticket for 1000 gold?
I deny going there. It is way too cold there.
Even if they had a harbour, I can do without the company of dwarfs.
This city is of no interest to us.
That's a faraway grassland, inhabited by savage ogres, as the word is. I won't sail there.
A beautiful city in a strange but fascinating land. I don't sail there, though.
Darama is a continent, not a city! <sigh> I guess that is what happens when someone has never seen a school from the inside.
Good bye.
pages.title: Karith

pages.name: Lisander
npc_lines: I'd rather be left in peace. Keep it short.
Listen, I'm not a big small talker. Why don't you do us both a favour and leave me alone?
Lisander. Couldn't say 'nice to meet you' though. Are you done?
They can be a pain in the neck.
Hold your tongue.
No, that's wine I'm drinking.
Ooooh. <makes a dramatic gesture> Daaaaaaaangerous creatures of the night! If that's what you wanted to hear.
It'd be better for you to leave now.
Yes, I have one. Mission 1: Try to keep your mouth shut for at least two hours!
This city has a lot more to offer than other cities.
I like it here, though that's obviously not a quarter.
His bar is a little too dirty for my taste.
He's not the type to hang out in taverns, so I rarely see him.
That guy should become a bit tougher. He's a little too mellow.
Nosy little wannabe.
Good man.
Finally.
pages.title: Lisander

pages.name: Lorietta
npc_lines: Lalalaaalalaa.
Hi there, Jogador! What do you need?
I guess I'm the local priest! They said only a priest of Kurik would be crazy enough to try spreading the faith in this town. And I tell you what: They have been soooo right!
My name is Lorietta. But why do you ask? I knew your name without asking. Guess how!
Oh, we heal people and ... and ... do other nice stuff. You know?!
You do not need any healing right now.

Kurik is the patron saint of jesters, fools, and inventors. This might sound strange, but do you know any inventor that isn't also a fool to some extent, and don't you think jesters are quite inventive?
In its golden age, this city must have been a joy for Kurik's eye. Even today you can still see some of its former glory here and there.
They must have been great inventors in the past. Nowadays not much of that is left. I guess they were foolish enough to let things slide.
As long as I don't invite them into my temple I'll be fine.
He's a bit too boring for my taste.
Tibia is quite big, isn't it?
Keep your adventurer's stone well.
Ehehehe! A blood crystal? You must be a fool looking for one. I like fools. Why don't you check the cultist hideout in the magician quarter?
The gods created all.
Life can be a cruel joke sometimes.
People come, people go.

Whenever you receive a lethal wound, your vital force is damaged and there is a chance that you lose some of your equipment. With every single of the five blessings you have, this damage and chance of loss will be reduced.

There are five blessings available in five sacred places: the spiritual shielding, the spark of the phoenix, the embrace of Tibia, the fire of the suns and the wisdom of solitude. Additionally, you can receive the twist of fate here. ...
There are also two enhanced blessings for further reduction of experience loss.
Oh, nonono, but thank you!
If I were a hero, I'd rather search for the screwdriver of Kurik.
My preferred plant is salad.
Hey! You are not a beauty yourself!
I'm only interested in new jokes, but I haven't heard any lately.
Just ask in which of the five blessings you are interested in.
Bye bye, Jogador!
pages.title: Lorietta

pages.name: Maris
npc_lines: I hope you have a good reason to step near my ship, Jogador.
I once sailed all seas of Tibia. No storm was too powerful and no sea too troubled for me and my ship.
I'm Maris Sharktooth. Arrr! - Well, I used to be.
Stop mumbling and don't bug me.
I don't know what you're talking about.
He sometimes sneaks around here. I have no idea what he's up to.
Such a polite little angel. Hahaha.
Good guy to have a drink with, if you know what I mean.
He seems like a crazy old magician or something like that. Don't have much to do with him.
He used to hang out with Armenius and me, but nowadays he prefers to stay in the centre.
They don't let me anchor my ship in the central harbour, so of course I'm not exactly fond of them.
Oh well, I stick with what I got.
No, thanks.
Those days are over, kid. I don't hire for my crew anymore.
Get off!
Good bye.
I don't mind having ended up here. There are worse places.
There are two small islands west of Yalahar. I'm not sure if they have an official name but the people call the bigger one 'Mistrock' and the other one 'Fenrock'.
Do I look like a ferryman?! Well... if I think about it, I could use some sailing practice. I can bring you to Fenrock for 100 gold. Agreed?
Do I look like a ferryman?! Well... if I think about it, I could use some sailing practice. I can bring you to Mistrock for 100 gold. Agreed?
This island bears a secret. I can feel it.
Well, we haven't got many options here. It's either Mistrock or back to Yalahar.
Back to Yalahar for 100 gold?
To Mistrock for 100 gold?
Do you smell this? It's the smell of fire... the fire of a forge. Many people searched this rock here for a hidden path, but they haven't found anything. ...
I'd search on Fenrock if I were you. Even though there's snow on the surface, it's still warm underground. There are often caves under fresh lava streams.
Well, we haven't got many options here. It's either Fenrock or back to Yalahar.
Back to Yalahar for 100 gold?
To Fenrock for 50 gold?
pages.title: Maris

pages.name: Menacing Mummy
npc_lines: Grrrr.
pages.title: Menacing Mummy

pages.name: Mr. West
npc_lines: I'll make them an offer they can't refuse.
Wh .. What? How did you get here? Where are all the guards? You .. you could have killed me but yet you chose to talk? What a relief! ...
So what brings you here my friend, if I might call you like that?
Hello. What brings you here?
I guess you are here on a mission.
He seems astonishingly determined and focused for a Yalahari. Perhaps he is the first sign of a change of wind blowing in our city. Who knows if it will be for the better.
Uhm. That cookie smells kinda strange. Don't take it as an offence, but no.
I wouldn't trust a single elf, let alone a whole city of them.
The word is that Thais is a dangerous place which you better do not visit unprepared.
The trade barons know how to run a city, that's for sure. Unfortunately, they are greedier than it is good for them. I'm prepared to deal with their intrusion into my territory.
Those dwarfs know how to fortify a city. Perhaps one day, when I've earned enough money and have grown too old for the trouble in Yalahar, I will retire there.
The illusion of peace that this city is offering often distracts the attention from the dangers lurking there.
He is a typical Yalahar official - always occupied with trying to stop the dam from breaking. After all these years, he still has not given up. That qualifies him either as an idealist or a fool.
All those royal bloodlines started with some kind of bandit anyhow.
Never heard of it.
The city offers great possibilities as long as order is maintained in some way. ...
It's easy to maintain order by using brute force but I see that as a necessary evil. My little empire developed out of my need for security in these times of turmoil. ...
To establish some security, I had to establish a base of power first. To maintain this power, I had to gain money somehow. ...
At this point I used my power to secure resources and to encourage trade. ...
In fact I do nothing else than the kings. I collect taxes and use them to hire men that ensure the safety of the people.
The people do their best to earn their living. Still, they are desperate. If it were not for me, they'd rob and murder each other.
Yalahar is an oyster. Its treasure is waiting to be excavated by someone with the necessary determination.
I don't care much about what has happened there. All that matters to me is that the quarter is lost and poses a danger.
In fact the arena quarter is still useful for the city. It's a good food source, and I recruit some of my best men from the descendants of the gladiators.
There are still many people living there. Of course, I provide them with some of my services as well.
It's a shame. I'm convinced there are countless treasures hidden in those ruins. However, neither bribe nor threats get my men even close to this quarter.
Good bye.
pages.title: Mr. West

pages.name: Oliver
npc_lines: I wish my shift would end.
Hello. Unless you have official business here or want to pass the gate, please move on.
I'm a proud sergeant of the Yalaharian Guard Force and at your service.
I'm called Oliver.

Of all the Augur, I only know Palimuth in person. If I were you, I'd trust him. He's a good man and really cares about the citizens of Yalahar, not only about his own profit or status. People like him are rare.
I'd love to help you with your mission, but I'm not sure what you expect from me? Anything in particular?
Do you want to pass the gate? Are you headed for the sunken or the factory quarter?

Now that's an interesting topic. Each quarter has its own stories and problems, and I could probably go on for hours and hours telling about my shifts there... ehmm... sorry, I tend to get carried away.

I could tell so many stories about what I experienced here in Yalahar ever since I arrived here around ten years ago. Still a young and eager soldier, fresh from the... ah no, that would lead too far.
Yes, we have a few islands surrounding Yalahar. They are called Mistrock, Fenrock and Vengoth.

I heard the weirdest stories about Mistrock from all kind of people. I don't think it's an 'evil' island, even though it's shrouded in mist. Actually I heard something about dwarfs living there somewhere.
Fenrock is close to the western Ice Islands. That's why it's also rather cold there. I'm not sure if any captain sails there, but you might ask in the foreign quarter.
To be honest, nobody actually knows whether Vengoth is an 'island' as in 'small island'. I think people have only travelled to the western shore so far, and also came back rather fast.

Oh dear, the poor alchemists who were working in that quarter when the big explosion happened! But well - some people say that it was caused by their very dangerous experiments... I wonder what they were playing with.
When I was still a young boy I dreamt of fighting in the arena and facing huge beasts and powerful gladiators. But ever since the gladiators behave strangely, my dream has become unrealisable.
I think almost everyone in this city lost someone when the quarter collapsed into the ocean. I could tell you the full story, but then again that's Tarak's job. He's a ferryman in the sunken quarter.

The ironic thing is that my mother is buried there. Well, she was buried there, that is. You might imagine my surprise and pain when I saw her... or rather her remains strolling around the city some night...

One of my buddies used to work in the factory before the normal production of food, weapons and such was shut down. I don't know what keeps the machines and golems running - it must be a magical power source.

Once during one of my shifts in the foreign quarter, I had a really interesting conversation with a lizard about the differences between human and lizard fighting skills... I should write that down sometime.
A long time ago, there was an incident with an old witch who was absolutely convinced that she was a cat. It was still funny when she was chasing rats... but then she almost fell off a roof.

I've known Mr. West for a long time now and witnessed him establishing his small empire of bandits and criminals. It's quite impressive considering that this is all the work of one man, as crazy as he might be.
I'll tell you that story another time, but not now. Sorry.
Goodbye citizen!
pages.title: Oliver

pages.name: Orc Berserker (NPC)
npc_lines: KRAK ORRRRRRK!
pages.title: Orc Berserker (NPC)

pages.name: Palimuth
npc_lines: Greetings.
I'm an Augur of the city of Yalahar. My special duty consists of coordinating the efforts to keep the city and its services running.
I'm Palimuth. Nice to meet you.
It is a somewhat futile mission but I won't give up.
I'm afraid we have not seen the last chapter of Yalahar's drama but I don't have any more missions for you.
Yes, that is indeed a threat. Those raids, not knowing who to trust... unfortunately that matter lies not in my hands.
There are no more addons available for you at this time.
Well, Azerus Vilus wasn't a high-ranking Yalahari in the past. Something must have happened which gained him so much power. ...
Still, I can't imagine anybody that would entrust someone like Azerus with a position of power and responsibility. He was known as self-centred, greedy, and cruel towards his underlings. ...
Not by chance people called him Azerus Vile behind his back.
What would you need a blood crystal for? Maybe a magician knows where to find one.
Uhm, no thanks.
I have to admit I'm a bit worried about the current state of our city.
I'm a bit worried about our city's current state!
The Yalahari are up to something strange and it does not bode well for the city of Yalahar!
As if Yalahar had not already endured enough hardship, also nature seemed to have conspired to ruin the city. It was a great disaster when a large part of the city simply broke away.
The people there are rather desperate than evil. Still the quarter poses a danger, especially for strangers.
Once, the Yalahari had the policy that their city is open for everyone who comes here in peace. Considering the situation in the foreign quarter today, they seem to have changed this policy. ...
I can't blame them. Still, I wonder if there is no hope for a peaceful coexistence.
As annoying it might be for my superiors, the presence of Mr. West and his private army of bullies brings at least some sort of order for a great part of our townspeople.
The Yalahari seem to be quite interested in retaking this quarter. But all efforts ended in the loss of men, they could not even nearly replace.
We did little to retake the arena quarter. On the one hand, we lack the manpower, on the other hand, it turned into some sort of food resource for the city.
It's hard to tell what actually has happened there. ...
According to the most prominent big bang theory, a devastating explosion laid waste most of the quarter and unleashed all kind of vile forces that made the quarter uninhabitable. ...

Others claim that numerous experiments had gone wrong and that parts of the quarter had already been polluted. The great explosion was only a result of the previous disasters that had accumulated over time. ...
This theory also claims that the explosion might actually have prevented the spreading of the plague to other parts of the city.
Good bye, Jogador.
pages.title: Palimuth

pages.name: Peter
npc_lines: I wish my shift would end.
Hello. Unless you have official business here or want to pass the gate, please move on.
Sergeant first class of the Yalaharian Guard Force. But I don't care about ranks and titles.
Peter.
One day I will walk into the office of my superior and announce my resignment. Probably not long from now.
Leave me alone with your 'mission' unless you have precise orders from my superiors.
Pass the gate? If it must be. Are you headed for the factory or the former trade quarter?
Count them yourself.
You're here. So what?
There it's even more smelly than in the factory quarter. Smells a bit like rotten eggs.
You don't look as if you would last one second there.
That quara brood should be extinguished.
Good idea. Go for a walk there. Preferably six feet down.
It's too noisy and smelly.
Go there if you wanna get beaten up.
I can't stand those arrogant fools.
The leader of their pack is the biggest criminal among them all.
Listen, I don't get paid enough to chat with citizens. Move on.
Goodbye citizen!
pages.title: Peter

pages.name: Reed
npc_lines: I wish my shift would end.
Hello. Unless you have official business here or want to pass the gate, please move on.
I'm a corporal of the Yalaharian Guard Force.
My name is Reed.
<whispers> I'm actually not allowed to talk about my superiors, but... something is fishy about them, too.
Mission? I will not go on any mission for you. Or what do you want from me?
You want to pass the gate? Are you headed for the cemetery or the magician quarter?
I really can't tell which quarter is the worst.
This city contains so much evil that I fear one day it will explode and end up in chaos and darkness.
The outer islands are called Mistrock, Fenrock and Vengoth.
I think some sinister and old force is hidden under all that mist.
One day I went there and broke my arm by slipping on ice.
I will never ever go there, and if I were sent there, I'd resign from the Guard Force.
If you stick your nose into that quarter, you will catch the disease and carry it with you for the rest of your life. I'm sure of that.
My little son was attacked by a mutated tiger in this quarter. He changed in a horrible way afterwards and I don't want to talk about it.
It's a catastrophe. I used to live there and barely got away with my life when the quarter crashed into the ocean.
Nothing holy is coming out of this... strange church. At night the living dead come to me and cling to the iron bars. One day they will probably get me.
Did you see those giant... creatures walking in the factory quarter?? They could kill a human just by squeezing it between their claws! Arr!
One day there will be a gigantic war between all the races in this quarter and it will devour the city.
Can you imagine how it feels for me to keep guard so close to all those insane mages, cultists and demonic creatures? Can you?! No, of course you can't!
I think Mr. West is planning to take over the whole city, if it hasn't been destroyed by war, contamination, monsters or greater evil by then.
It's nice talking to you, but honestly, you give me the creeps. So please decide what you want and move on.
Goodbye citizen!
pages.title: Reed

pages.name: Tamerin
npc_lines: Come here, kitty, kitty!
Hello, what brings you here?
I'm a humble druid, tending the animals.
I'm known as Tamerin.
Animals don't lie and know no cruelty.
The city is in its death throes.
I'm not interested in city politics.
I have no use for a watch.
Gladiators are merciless killers.
It was an atrocity, and it's a good thing that it doesn't exist any longer.
Good bye!
pages.title: Tamerin

pages.name: Tarak
npc_lines: Boat trips to the monument tower!
Listen to my story about the sunken quarter!
Want to explore the sunken quarter of Yalahar? I'm your man!
Hi, Jogador. Can I interest you in a trip to the monument tower?
Well, actually I'm unemployed. But I make a little money by bringing tourists to the monument tower.
I'm Tarak. I may look like a beggar, but I'd never ask for free stuff - I work for my money! At your service.
This tower is the most intact remaining part of the sunken quarter of Yalahar. From there, you can dive down to the sunken city. Want to travel there, just ask me for a passage.
I can row you to the monument tower for 50 gold. Return trip included! You can only dive down with a helmet of the deep, though. Wanna go?
No, I wouldn't consider myself a true sailor. But I know enough to bring you to the tower and back again safely.
Now that's some story. I've told it numerous times to tourists - <coughs>, I mean, adventurers - but it still makes me shiver each time. ...
As you might have already noticed, Yalahar is huge. HUGE. The city has grown so much over the past centuries that eventually there was no space left for new buildings. ...

However, due to the constant flow of immigrants, the citizens just kept on building and building - either placing buildings on top of each other or trying to enhance the space with platforms on the water. ...
Then, a few decades ago, there was a day which I still remember vividly, because I was right in the middle of the whole disaster happening. ...
I just came back from the centre and was on the way to my house located in the east quarter - today situated several feet below us under the ocean surface. ...
Suddenly the earth was shaking and I heard a loud rumbling. I was still wondering what on earth was going on, or if we were under attack, when I saw the houses closest to the ocean collapse. ...
Just like that! The ground under them broke away and fell into the ocean, and then - imagine that - like a wave of destruction, terror rushed through the whole quarter. ...

I heard people screaming and more houses tumbling down, and immediately I rushed back to the centre, behind the solid city walls - even though they didn't seem so solid at that time, but it was the safest place I could get to. ...
From there I had to helplessly watch how the whole quarter fell apart. Large chunks of stone and earth collapsed into the ocean, and with them all of my belongings. ...
When the wave of destruction reached the wall separating the quarter from the other parts of the city, that wall also sunk into the ocean and must have worked as a barrier down there. ...
You can still see the top of the old wall sticking out of the water. After that last collapse, the destruction stopped all of a sudden. ...
Only a few people, among them myself as you can see, were able to survive the great downfall. The rest was buried under their houses, or drowned in the ocean. Such cruel fate... ...

Well, <clears throat> it took a while for me to recover from that incident, and afterwards I decided to show to adventurers what can happen when you foolishly overestimate your power. So let that be a lesson to you. ...
Now, it's up to you if you want to dive down to the remains of the sunken part of Yalahar. You need a Helmet of the Deep, though. And beware, quara have infested the area. ...
Maybe they were also involved into the great downfall. We will never know for sure, but I truly hope an incident like that won't repeat itself in Yalahar.
Well, a nicer expression would be 'adventurers' I guess.
You know, the people back in the old days, those were real adventurers.
My watch was stolen, unfortunately.
How strange a city you are... Yalahar. I guess I'll make a song out of that someday. I'm quite a talented musician, you know!
Oh yes, I saw the king once, when I was still a youngster living in Thais. I think the nobles don't care about the common people.
I've lived there for a short time before moving on to Yalahar. I never really got along with the elves, though. Can't stand people who think they are better than me.
Carlin isn't as bad as people say, as long as you bring your own alcohol and can handle the women there.
I guess it would be hard to earn money there as a ferryman - the swamp is not passable by boat.
I grew up there, so I still have pleasant memories of it.
Edron is actually close by here. One day, I'll row there with my own hands. That's my goal.
I know some people down there. Old Adall used to be a close friend of mine, but we lost contact over the years. Don't know if he even remembers me.
One day, I'd like to see the pyramids. The real, big pyramids I mean, not the small one we have in Yalahar.
I've never been there, and to be honest, I'm not planning to. Nothing exciting about it.
I like the dwarfs. They usually don't talk much, but still they are great drinking companions.
Yes, the barbarian settlement west of here. I went there once, but honestly, my old bones can't stand the cold.
Vengoth?? No, heck, I don't go near that cursed island. Maybe someone in the south quarters is brave enough, they have boats too, you know.
Those stories don't scare me. Ferumbras' tower is said to be on an island to the far south-west. That's far away enough for me.
Over the years, I've seen many things happening in Tibia, especially a lot of bad stuff. Somehow I managed not to get disillusioned, though, just seasoned.
An old love of mine used to live there. I wonder how she's doing today.
Yes, in fact that's the name of my old love. You must be a good guesser.
Bye, Jogador. Come back whenever you want to see the monument tower.
pages.title: Tarak

pages.name: Timothy
npc_lines: So many discoveries to be made .. I hardly know where to start.
Oh, hello! It's a pleasure to see a visitor from the continent.
I work for the explorer's society as an information gatherer here in this newly discovered city.
I'm Timothy of the explorer's society.
As we are interested in many fields, it's no wonder that we are here. There are so many marvels to observe and so many things to discover. ...
It will take a lifetime to compile all that knowledge. If you are interested, you can assist me in this matter.
If you stumble upon an artefact from Yalahar's past, I'd certainly be interested in buying it from you. ...
These artefacts come in different shapes and sizes, but I'm sure you will recognise their importance.
Do you have a real Yalahari artefact with you?
The city is still a marvel to behold. I can only slightly imagine how it must have looked in its prime. ...
It's a shame that all its glory vanished through the centuries.
He works as an Augur - a high ranking official of the city. He's responsible for assigning all available helpers to different tasks. ...
An ungrateful job considering what kind of helpers are at his disposal. There are many problems and the number of the hired helpers is small.
Look, my friend, I'm only interested in ancient artefacts. Ancient cookies are not what I'm looking for.
I've just started to research why the vampires attack Yalahar, but unfortunately I've not gotten very far yet.
Oh, didn't I mention it? A friend of mine, a local officer named Palimuth, needs some assistance. Maybe you are interested in this job!
Oh yes, I heard about a gem like that. Nowadays they seem incredibly hard to acquire. The explorer's society doesn't own one, else I'd help you.
Good bye.
pages.title: Timothy

pages.name: Tony
npc_lines: Please move on, nothing to see here.
Hello. Unless you have official business here or want to pass the gate, please move on.
Uhm, private first class of the Yalaharian Guard Force. <salutes clumsily>
I'm Tony.
They are also our superiors... but lower in rank than the Yalahari.
Mission? Eh? I don't know anything about any mission. What do you want from me?
Uh, you want to pass the gate? Are you headed for the arena or the foreign quarter?
Uhm, there are many quarters. I think... about eight. My duty is to guard the gate between the arena quarter and the... err... foreign quarter.
This city has a lot of problems... <scratches head> ... and a few surrounding islands.
This city has a few surrounding islands... but no official ship route is going there. Mistrock... Fenrock... and err... Vengoth, as far as I know.
That island is covered in mist. I've never been there. Someone in the foreign quarter told me something about it once... but I forgot what he said.
I heard there's some snow there... I would love to go there some day.
There are really bad rumours about this place. I don't want to find out if they are true.
Uhm... I'm glad I don't have to guard the gate between alchemist quarter and arena quarter. You know... all that acid and fume... can't be healthy.
That side of the gate can be a little scary... all those animal roaring at night... and the gladiators can be even worse.
Mh... a really tragic story... a whole quarter of the city broke down and fell into the ocean.
Now that's spooky... undead roaming around at nighttime and sometimes even at daytime... I don't set a foot there if I don't have to.
Err... I have a rust allergy. It makes my nose tickle to go there.
I think some people there are not bad at all. Sometimes they visit me at the gate and ask me how I am.
I don't like going there... and I think magicians consider themselves so wise and educated that they look down on normal people like you and me.
The former trade quarter is under the wing of Mr. West. He can be intimidating...
Sorry... but uhm... please move on, I actually shouldn't chat with you.
Goodbye citizen!
pages.title: Tony

pages.name: Yalahari (NPC)
npc_lines: Greetings.
I'm a member of the Yalahar. I'm obliged to assist our helpers in their efforts to improve the life within our city. So from time to time I assign a mission to our helpers.
My Name is Azerus.
I'm fine, thank you.
You shouldn't bother about such things.
Since you have proven yourself as worthy, there might be more important missions to accomplish if you are interested.
I don't care about them. They are outside these walls.
There are more important matters to take care of.
His lack of a vision for the city is typical for our helpers. Sadly all the responsibilities still rest solemnly on the shoulders of us - the Yalahari.
Soon enough our city will once again become a beacon of hope!
We are the masters of this city and see ourselves as benevolent caretakers of our citizens!
We welcomed many foreigners to our city to share in our wealth. They did not value our generosity. Instead they introduced their own barbaric ways here. ...
It was only a question of time until they waged war against each others and the city's officials. The only thing those creatures respect is power. ...
In time, we will regain our power and get them back into line.

With only a little more authority, those gladiators had never dared to affront us. It is only a matter of time until we re-establish the power needed to enforce law and order in this quarter once again.
A shroud of pestilence and decay lies over this quarter. It is one of the major failures of the past to let that quarter deteriorate so badly.
This quarter is a good example for the failure of the policy to allow people to mind their own business. What should have become a centre of knowledge and learning, became a cauldron of chaos. ...
Even now that several catastrophes have destroyed the quarter and the order there, scheming magicians plot to gain power at the expense of the city.
We have to consider this quarter as lost. There is no hope left that it could be rebuilt in some way. ...
On the peak of our power, we, the Yalahari, would have been able to re-establish this quarter. But much work has to be done until we ever reach such power again.
Most of the factories are no longer functional, and the unruly people living there don't make it easier to retake and repair them. ...
As soon as the order has been restored in other parts of the city, we will be able to spent more resources in the rebuilding of the factories.

It is an affront to our authority that someone claims dominance over one of our territories. If we allowed such a behaviour, others would follow. It would not take long until we had to deal with several petty kings that question our might.
Good bye, Jogador.
I'm Tirak, the replacement of the recently vanished Azerus
I'm quite busy getting accustomed to my new duties, so please excuse me.
pages.title: Yalahari (NPC)

pages.name: Znozel
npc_lines: Me take all gold! Good care! Give! Give!
Hi there. Welcome to me gold storage called bank.
Me Znozel the great goblin banker!
Me great good banker! Me smart and honey .. no wait I mean horrible .. no, no honest I am! Yes, yes! Money give, give to honest goblin! Uhhh so shiny coins!
Where? WHERE?! HELP! Protect my gold!
Taxes, taxes! Always government is harassing harmless little goblins!
Oooooooooh shiny shiny shiny shiny!! Give me!!
Me only take cookie if it's golden. Ehehehe.
Goblins not bankers usually. But great love everything shiny. Yes. Yes.
Me do good job! Me honest goblin for sure! Me that honest other goblin call me mad! Imagine!
Okay okay, no need to be rude! It seems you are already know everything.
Banker rule number one: Dragons are always served first!
Just give good goblin all your money. Me making us both rich. Trust! Trust!
We can change money for you. You can also access your bank account or your guild account options.
Me came here to plunder. Old banker hired me. When dragon eats banker for must waiting in line I taking over everything!
It gone BOOOM! Yes, yes! No good going there.
Big humans there are mean. Big beasts even worse!
Others there only bully little goblins around.
Me did not break it! Honest! Was broke as I came!
Spooky guys are not good for business.
Many humans there. Seldom come here to trade.
This West human not too bad is. He great trader, strong chieftain.
Bye, bye. You gold safe at here, Jogador. <snickers>!
pages.title: Znozel

pages.name: Awareness of the Emperor
npc_lines: I have to admit I figured out quite late what is happening. It seems we are both involved in a scheme of it who is known as the snake god rising to power. A process that could mean the end of the world as you know it.

I don't know what it is or was. But I heard that this thing tried to become a god in the past and was trapped in a state 'in between'. Its current plan seems to be to use my crystal matrix which I use to amplify my control over the dragon kings in a reverse way to steal the vital force of the dragons, those bound to them, and even from the land itself.

With this stolen power it hopes to become a true god. This would destroy the continent. Not only the continent's life would be drained, it would also damage its integrity and stability. The whole land would crumble and vanish in the sea. Such a destruction would probably lead to earthquakes and floods everywhere in the world, causing death and destruction beyond compare. And all this only because you fools let yourselves use by that priest just like he is used by his so-called god.

We came here from a distant land that is no longer. We took it upon us to become the rulers of this land. We brought order to the struggles and saved a dying empire. We deserve no less than to be accepted as leaders by the lesser beings. We allowed the lizards to exist and to serve us.

He is just a willing vessel. He seems to serve as some sort of anchor or even avatar for the snake's power. Fortunately, his body is too weak to channel much of the snake's power. He might become a formidable opponent but he will still be mortal. With a sizeable force of capable opponents he can be brought down.

Indeed, this will be your mission though. Since you cut off the way to control the dragon kings easily, I'll have to put some effort into holding them at bay. Another part of me tries to repair the damage you have caused, and yet another will try to interrupt the flow of power which this snake thing sends to its priest.
I am the emperor of Zao. Power and destiny made me the ruler over dragons and lizards.
They are more familiar to us than the brutish and stupid orcs. In their best moments they are even amusing. All they need is guidance, otherwise they are lost and helpless.

They are barely sentient at all. A despicable race beyond all hope. The minotaurs think they have them under control but it is only a matter of time before the orcs will crush them and revert to their old ways.

They were nearly extinct when we arrived. I understand that the minotaurs that pose a problem to us in these days are foreigners in this land. They think they can tame the orcs which I think is such an amusing assumption that I restrained myself from crushing them. I want to watch how they fall flat with this folly. They will fail in the end. It's only a question of how and when.

You are different than the humans here. The humans here are not better than the animals of the mountains and the steppes. You people on the other hand ... well, you might prove a worthy challenge one day. But first and foremost there are other issues to attend which will take a few centuries. Only then I might take a look at your land if I am still interested.

Once the trouble with this mad lizard priest is settled, I have to deal with the problem of the spreading corruption. I am sure I will find a suitable solution. Then the empire has to be restructured and the south to be retaken. After that a phase of rebuilding will begin. The empire lacks manpower and due to the corruption and the loss of land it lacks resources, this is certainly something that needs to be dealt with.

Even we dragons were not unified. We ... continued certain old habits that led to fights which in turn led to inevitable, irreplaceable losses. So by my power I bound the others to my will. Being the eldest and even more powerful than even most of my lesser brethren can imagine, it was my right to do so. In return I taught them to bind the lesser lizards to their will and so we reforged the empire.

I foresaw that with my ultimate demise the infighting would resume and destroy all what is left of us. So I decided that I was too important to die. My time was limited though and the only means of survival that I could come up with was to transform me into a lich, a creature of undeath. It was an ... unexpected experience. However, soon I learnt about the changes my new state of existence involved and the way how things work.

Through my connection to the other dragons, my undeath spread in an unexpected way. And it did not stop at the dragons. It went on through them to the lizards they had bound and through them to the land itself. It seems the land itself became the place where the undeathly influence was finally dumped as it suffered much more than the beings that functioned as transmitters. However, you see that what you call corruption is only an unwanted by-product of something far greater and more important.

It is certainly no ideal state but a necessity. I take it upon me for the sake of the land. Without me my people would perish and so would the civilisation of the lizards. Or worse, they would continue to worship that unspeakable snake thing that is willing to devour the whole world to become a god.

Those fools are misled by the snake god and its treacherous priests. If it weren't for us dragons, the lizards had perished long ago. It was our power that crushed their enemies and our guidance that ended centuries of intrigue and infighting. We deserve their respect and loyalty. They owe us these things like they owe us their existence.
They owe us their existence. Without us their empire would crumble. We are their only hope and the only hope of stability for this land.

If the lizard empire crushed, the orcs would turn on each other and sooner or later wipe out the minotaurs and humans. Then the land would lapse into bloodshed and barbarism. We are the only source of order in this land and the only ones who have the power to enforce such an order.
The tainted crystals work reversely to their actual intention. It will take a while to reconfigure them. One part of my consciousness is already working on this problem.
pages.title: Awareness of the Emperor

Ze great Zalamon iz our leader and a vizionary zat forezeez a gloriouz future for our people. He iz ze voize of ze Great Znake. ...
Zalamon iz an exalted being. He iz cloze to ze znake god. He iz ze lazt of ze anointed prieztz and never lozt ze blezzing of ze Great Znake becauze hiz faiz never wavered. ...
He haz taught me much of ze wayz of ze true faiz. One day I might become a priezt myzelf. I have yet much to learn about ze teachingz of ze Great Znake.
We are guilty az we have abandoned ze Great Znake. Zalamon'z teachingz are our only zalvation ...
He remindz uz about our heritage and our dutiez to ze Great Znake ...
We muzt repent, we muzt prove our worz to ze Great Znake by breaking ze shacklez of zlavery zat ze dragonz put upon uz ...
Zen ze Great Znake will onze again embraze uz.
Ze land haz lozt ze blezzing of ze Great Znake. We all zuffer for our failure in ze eyez of ze god. ...
When ze people return to ze true faiz, ze Great Znake will lift ze curze from ze land and our raze will experienze a new age of advanzement and power.
Ze planz finally will come to fruition.

pages.name: Smaralda
npc_lines: Welcome Jogador! Let us talk about fate.
Fate is a road that we all travel but rarely notice. Long ago I have bound my fate to that of a pirate whose name can't be spoken anymore. ...
I try to ease his gruesome fate with my abilities.
The good old captain was never one of the evil bandits of the seas but a gentleman robber who actually fought for freedom and against slavery. ...
Of all the things, good or bad he did in his life, the most fateful was a promise he made to his people to bring back a holy icon that other pirates had robbed while he was away. ...
He tracked the icon to the Mourning Isles but there he met his cruel fate and died without fulfilling his promise.

These isles seemed to be cursed by the gods even before the first living beings arrived there. Since then they've had a history of pain, treachery and desolation. But the lure of its treasures is still strong. ...
Many would try to brave the undead inhabitants of the isles to rob them of their treasure but there is no ship of the living that can still reach the isles.
No ordinary ship can hope to reach the legendary Mourning Isles. But there is one ship that could do it! It is the ship of the old pirate. ...
In these days he is looking for a crew of mortals to help him end his self-imposed curse.
The old pirate made a promise to return an icon from the Mourning Isles. A promise he could not fulfil. ...
Again and again he is looking for helpers that will allow him to summon his ship to this world and reach these cursed isles to finally find that icon. ...
You might be able to help him, but only after my soul seeing reveals which spirit mark will govern your life for the next cycle. ...
Even then you will have to find three others with the same spirit mark bound to them to provide the pirate with a strong and capable crew.
You are marked by the "Seu Espiríto".
There are spirits all around us. Some are close to the world of the living, some are far away. Some of them sympathize with our trials and sense some kind of familiarity to us. ...

These spirits attach themselves to us for a period of time when they feel that our fate corresponds with certain aspects of their own. I learned how to visualise those spirits and therefore can say a bit about the future that might await you. ...
Even more, I connected those spirits to a certain symbolism to make the concept more accessible. I learned that people that share the same symbols are somehow connected by fate. ...
We can use this fact to help the captain to find his crew. He needs people who are connected to each other to help him in his quest.
I am only known as Smaralda in these days.
My endeavours of the past are unimportant. I'm nothing but an old woman that sometimes dabbles with the mystic arts. ...
Now I'm just a fortuneteller and sometimes a helper of fate. And I know a few old stories.
I rarely use my gift in these days. I use it only to help the old pirate to find the rest that he deserves by finding a crew for his ship.
Of all stories that I could tell, there is only one that is of importance in these days. This is the story about the old pirate.
Now that you have captured enough of the spectral scum you may use my crystal ball to meet the captain. ...
But keep in mind that you need three others with the same soul mark to proceed.
This world was successful in xx journeys. 50 journeys are necessary to give the captain some peace for this month.
Good bye, Jogador.

pages.name: Minzy
npc_lines: Welcome. Good you're showing up
I've never considered to follow a profession. But people tend to call me a swamp witch because I sometimes make brews with unusual ingredients in my cauldron. So I guess that is what I am.
Not all witches are evil. Neither do all of us fit into such simple categories like good and evil at all. ...
In these days, several of us work for a common cause and put our differences aside for a greater goal. ...
I think there is a lot to learn from this and I hope it will somehow be an inspiration for others.
We need the ingredients and we need many of them. We gather supplies the whole year and prepare most of the brew in advance. ...
But with our numbers dwindling, we need more and more help of the Tibians to save the world. You might gain our favour by helping us in our mission.
The cauldron is ancient and sacred to us. It bears powerful enchantments and years of use in rituals have changed its very structure in the fabric of reality.
The brew is not ready by far. We are just beginning and there is much left to be done.
By sacrificing items for our cause or igniting the cauldron's fire you will gain some favour within our circle. ...
We are willing to trade certain potions to you. Your current favour is 2.

We offer mana potions, strong mana potions and great mana potions. We also offer health potions, strong health potions, great health potions and ultimate health potions. And we offer great spirit potions.
Sorry, your favour is not high enough.
I am known as Minzy.
We have to hold the ritual in these days when they are strongest. They might even manifest now and then harass us in our ritual with the help of rotten dead things . ...

But this is nothing compared to their wrath if we should fail the ritual. We would have to wait a whole year to try a new ritual and had to endure the malignant attacks of the bane bringers in the meantime.
The bane bringers work in a very subtle way. You might lose connection to a dear friend, have considerable streaks of bad luck or make new enemies. ...
Perhaps they'd let something of your possession vanish or make you look like a cheater or liar through some strange coincidence. The worst thing they do is eating away your luck and happiness though.
One would guess the trade barons could easily spare the ingredients for the brew, but they won't lift a finger and call us superstitious fools. ...
In the past, they even sent mercenaries to disrupt our ritual but our resistance proved too expensive for their tastes. Still, we failed to complete the ritual that year and many suffered.
I won't share my knowledge with strangers. Besides, there is little I know that would be of any practical use at all for you.
He has stolen much of his knowledge from several sources. The community of witches suffered particularly from his greed. ...
We will not forget this. Although, some misguided souls sell themselves to him for some of the stolen and now lost knowledge in return.
Weapons, weapons. Is this all you people care about? The bane bringer threat is a far more imminent event. This should be our focus.
Take care my friend.

pages.name: Ghost Captain
npc_lines: Greetings Jogador! Are you ready to help me?
Read the manuals that should be lying around here. Some of my former helpers wrote all that stuff down to assist those who might come after them. ...
It is IMPORTANT that you understand the procedure. As soon as we embark on our journey, we will have only a few moments to get to the battle stations until the trouble begins. ...
It's not easy to sail through the netherworld, so don't make it harder by missing vital facts.
You have to man all stations. Each station must be attended by one person. Read the manual over there, it will help you significantly. ...
You'll have to act swiftly and correctly, else we'll lose our chance to chart the waters of the nether. If you fail on your duties on the ship, we have lost this opportunity, too.
If we fail, I will have to gather new strength and we have to try it anew after a while.
I've lost my name along with the chance to pass into the afterlife. One day I may have a name again, but only to be mourned since I will finally rest in peace then.
What do you think? I'm dead and forgotten. I'm just a shadow of the man I used to be. I'm a ghost now.
Just like me, my ship is not from this world anymore. We belong to another world now and it's hard to pass into the world of the living. ...

I can twist myself through the barrier sometimes but to get my ship through it requires more power than I've got available. For this reason we needed the power of the spectral scum you caught earlier. ...

This way we do not only put those lost souls to rest, but also gather the energy that is needed to get the ship through the barrier of worlds. With my ship here, we might be able to reach the Mourning Isles.

The Mourning Isles are a place of dread and despair. Since ancient times it has been a place where pirates of many races and nations hid their treasures and left unwanted individuals to await their death. ...
Often the treacherous waters of the isles sunk ships and stranded their crews on these godforsaken rocks. Many people died and cursed the isles. ...
So these isles are haunted since the dawn of mankind. The ghosts there lured even more ships on the reefs and the dreaded fame of the isles made them a popular hiding and detention spot. ...
Nowadays, no ordinary ship would manage to reach this isle. But my ghost ship might make it. ...
I will not lie to you though. Our journey will probably be as futile as all others before. ...
But with each successful try we are getting a bit closer to the isle. We just have to stand the perils of the nether long enough so that I can complete my maps of the nether a bit more. ...
Even if I won't reach the isle during your lifetime, your help will never be forgotten my friend.
Over the centuries, my ship has become more of an entity than an ordinary ghost ship. ...
It's been my only ally throughout the ages, well almost. We've been through a lot of tough things and I want you to treat my ship with respect. ...
The most living parts of the ship, save for the hull itself, are the soul core and the spirit flame. ...
You can reach the ship by using the mechanism in the south. Four of you have to stand on the plates when one of you pulls the lever. All of you have to be aligned to the same spirit mark though.

The hull is made by spectral wood and can easily stand the spirit storms of the netherworld. Still, it is a great danger that the wood is satiated so much with spirit energy that is becomes a feast for those damn ghost rats. ...
Gladly we still have some good old ghost dusters in the ship, they'll teach them a lesson. Still, these rats can do considerable damage to the hull if no one takes care of them.
It's hard to describe what it is exactly. I'd call it the ship's heart and soul. ...
You can literally see the ship's health and well-being by inspecting the core. If the core is damaged, it is a really baaaad thing, you know!? ...
The good thing is that soul sparks, which are quite common in these parts of the netherworld, emit a strengthening aura that can fix any damage of the core. ...
They have to be led to the core though since they are only attracted by living creatures.
The flame is what keeps the ship moving. Elements are not common here in the netherworld and are a powerful source of energy. ...
The spirit flame charges itself on energy of certain elements. These elements have to be distributed to the corresponding shrines. ...
When a shrine obtains the correct energy charge, it fuels the spiritual force of the ship and reinvigorates the spirit flame in return. ...
If this delicate balance were ever to break, we would lose our energy source and couldn't continue our travel through the netherworld or even strand here.
Good bye, Jogador.

pages.name: Brian The Baker
npc_lines: Hi there Jogador. Are you here to help?
Too bad, I guess we could need some more.

I'm a member of the Magic Bakery Alliance. We are an order that is dedicated to further the knowledge of bakery for the benefit of mankind. Our goals are as numerous as the recipes we come up with each season.
Currently we are trying to reclaim another part of Kullu's wisdom. Year after year, we try our best to break the defences of Cake Keep Isle.

He was a great mage but an even greater cook. His recipes and spells are priceless. Sadly, even if we succeed in breaking the defences of Cake Keep Isle, we will only manage to decipher a tiny fraction of his knowledge. ...
And still, we don't know what happened to Kullu. He retreated from our world to fully concentrate on his research on cooking recipes and spells. ...
He was some sweet tooth for all that we know. And for sure a genius when it comes to baking and magic. ...
His kitchen magic was that amazing, you could not tell where baking ended and magic started.
To be undisturbed, he placed his keep on an isle that existed on a planar instability which allowed him to phase the isle out of existence for most of the time. ...
Additionally he surrounded the isle with a sorcery of his invention that defied most attempts to reach it. ...
It took us quite a while to figure out that he'd never be able to weave a protection spell against something he loved so dearly like cakes and bakery wares. ...
So we came up with the idea of the bridge.

After a few failed attempts with gingerbread boats and the like, we figured out how to reach Cake Keep Isle. We used the very ingredients we could derive from his cake golem attacks to build a stable cake bridge to his isle.
Ah well, that's an .. uhm .. funny story. ...
You see, after the first expedition reached the isle, they took so long trying to find a way to Kullu's secrets that the isle began to vanish into the void while they were still there. ...
The entire time, they were harassed by Kullu's cake golem guardians of the keep. In the last minute, they cast emergency teleports to their home cities. ...
The good thing is it was not too late and all escaped. Well, the bad thing is their spells somehow reacted with the void-rift of that place, building astral tunnels from the void to said cities. ...

Now, whenever the isle manifests, the tunnels manifest as well. The ugly part is that through this one-way tunnels the cake golem army that was apparently sucked into the void has access to the cities and can raid them. ...
But they are not only an annoyance but also our greatest chance. Nasty but tasty little buggers. They can be troublesome but we need them for our bridge construction.
The golems that raid the cities supply us with two major materials that we need to build our bridge to Cake Keep Isle. ...
One component is the sugary mass that can be gained if you slay one of them. We use it as a kind of mortar. ...

The second part is a bit trickier to get. It is the raw cake material. It is kind of challenging to gain it. We built extraction machines that can drain the base material from the still animated corpses. ...
We placed one in each of the raided cities. You will have to lure the golems into the machines, to extract the material from them. ...
We need it to have a stable base material that is resilient against wind, weather and salt water.
We accumulated ??? of 200 sugary mass. We can't fail this year! We will not allow it!
I'm somewhat worried. Getting the base material is always the tricky part. People are usually a bit too eager to kill. We accumulated ??? of 200 base material until now.
We are a mystic order of bakers who pursue goals for the benefit of all mankind. Don't even listen to the lies and propaganda spread by those who envy us.
We are a mystic baker order. Don't listen to those who envy us and spread ugly lies and propaganda. We are dedicated to uncover the greatest secrets about cooking and baking. ...
Baking is the only trade worth to be considered. Without bakers everyone would starve. We are what ties a society together, preferably with a thick, sticky and sweet mass made of fruits. ...
We are the momentum of culture. Baking is what divides civilization from barbarism.
