These objects can then be seen swirling around in their watery shapes.
If you want to send a letter or parcel to someone, ask Amra at the post office here in Moonfall.
Asphota sells tools at the market of Silvertides.
She is the love of my life, two-leg. Her scales are blue as the deep sea, shining bright like sapphires. Her voice is like music and she can be quite funny, too! ...
I'll spend the rest of my life with her, I don't care what is said about family by the elders.
He is one of the coastal nagas' beaver keepers.
If you want to sell some gems, Giri is the one you should ask. You can find him at the market here in Moonfall.
She is a young two-leg from Issavi and is selling two-leg friendly furniture at the market here in Moonfall.
Isika sells ammunition at the market of Silvertides.
Kaumudi is one of our hatch-mothers. That means she cares for the eggs of all of Moonfall's nagas.

He is the raja of the coast folk. You would call him a king, I guess. A kind and patient man who takes his responsibilities very seriously. He is very beloved by the coastal nagas as well as his daughter Candra.
Nipuna is selling wands and runes at the market of Silvertides.
She is my mother, the mountain folk's maharani. You would call her a queen, I guess. She is resolute and strong-minded but also very just towards all of her subjects.
He is Sissek's brother and arrived together with him from Zao, a long time ago. He runs the tavern in the House of Rest and Wisdom here in Moonfall.

He is a two-leg but a different kind of biped than you are. Scaly all over, like our lower bodies. He came here from Zao a long time ago. Until then we didn't know what a bank was. But he established one here in Moonfall.
She is a gifted alchemist and is selling potions at the market here in Moonfall.
He is the coast folk's shaman. He is a powerful wave shaper and one of the wisest tide sages, according to what I have heard.

Timira is a very well known sage and philosopher amongst my people. But I'm afraid, I can't talk about her at the moment. It's a rather unfortunate story but one my mother doesn't want me to discuss with everyone, I'm sorry.
She is our astronomer and has a laboratory slightly away from the city. She has vast knowledge about the night sky and the star constellations.
She is our shaman. You can find her high up above Moonfall in the sanctum of the mountain spirits. My mother Saraki highly appreciates her wise advice.
He has a magic carpet with which he can fly through the air. If you ask him, he might be able to fly you to other islands or continents.
Farewell and safe slithering.
pages.title: Nihaka

pages.name: Tarisu
npc_lines: The Cobalt Tides are near.
The water is not a threat but a blessing.
I hope the starleaf harvest will be plentiful this year.
May the tides always guide you safely.
I'm the coast nagas' shaman.
My name is Tarisu.
Cobalt Tides is a joyful holiday, celebrated each year around the summer solstice when the tidal currents bring warm and almost turquoise waters. ....
It is associated with inspiration, beautiful secrets and love. Our traditions include the public telling of stories and affirmations of relationships.

The Invocation is a holiday of the mountain folk celebrated on the third new moon of autumn. The celebration is associated with the mountain spirits and the mountain nagas ask them for their protection on this day. ...
Traditions include quiet contemplation, fasting and sacrifices.
While all nagas celebrate Rising Day, Cobalt Tides is a holiday special to the coast folk. The mountain folk on the other hand celebrates the Invocation.
There is a blessed pond from which you have to take the water. You will find it on a small island in the north, a silent and holy place where we lay to rest our departed.

Solid water has roundish, organic shapes, like waves that have solidified in motion. It can also take the appearance of large drops or water bubbles. The solid water is very receptive to magical energy and therefore often enchanted. ...
In the past, at the beginning of the Rising, it was mainly used to push back the water by casting repulsion spells on them. By now, we use them for a wide variety of purposes. ...
Partly to direct and guide water and to collect it in certain places, but also for entirely different purposes. And sometimes the solid water is only used for the aesthetic decoration of our cities.
Rising Day is a historical holiday. It commemorates the beginning of the Rising. Celebrations last thirteen days and traditions include celebratory meals and theatrical productions.
It began centuries ago but it progresses very slowly. We, the coast folk here in Silvertides, have strongly integrated the Rising into our culture and way of life. ...
We adapt to living with the water and take advantage of its benefits instead of resisting it. The mountain nagas, who live in the Stardance Mountains, have not yet been affected by the Rising. ...
Because of this, there are some cultural differences, for example in terms of religious customs, diet and lifestyle.
Silvertides is our city, home of the coast folk. At the beginning of the period we call 'the Rising', we still made great efforts to push the water back and keep it away from the island. ...
In the meantime, however, we have accepted that the water and the land coalesce more and more. We regard it as a part of our lives and even a part of ourselves. ...
Our connection to water and the sea is incomparably stronger than that of the mountain folk. Our buildings are now either submerged completely or rise out of the water only partially. ...
Nevertheless, these buildings are often still used, and we travel back and forth between them on small boats. There are also paths laid across the water, often made of large lily pads. ...
They are floating on the waves easily and at the same time they are stable enough for a naga to glide over them as if on solid ground.
The mountain folk lives high up in the Stardance Mountains, in a city called Moonfall. It got its name after a story which is very well kown amongst the nagas.

We also have different religious customs and celebrate different holidays.

This is why the mountains in the centre of Marapur are called the Stardance Mountains and our city Moonfall. For it was at this very spot that Amati had fallen.
Tide sages know everything about the tidal currents and can reliably predict when it is safe to navigate the sea with the small naga boats. ...
They know when schools of fish come close to the coasts, making it a good time to fish. And they can estimate which islands will be affected by the Rising soon.
Wave shapers are a kind of water-magicians who can create solid water, charge it with magic and also transform it into other forms. ...
They have a sort of water-empathy that allows them to solidify the water and then shape it as if it were soft wax.
We use the island's giant beavers as beasts of burden to transport timbers, star leaf and other material. ...
These beavers are taken care of by the beaver whisperers, who build a trusting relationship with the animals and thus get them to work for us.

We pray to Amati, the Moon Goddess - as do the mountain nagas. The Moon Goddess is a unifying element in our religion. But we here in Silvertides also worship the water spirits while the mountain folk still worships the mountain spirits.
We cast spells through gestures, called yukti. The more gestures a naga masters, the more spells they can cast. ...
While many nagas can only perform yukti with two arms at the same time, some are able to form these gestures with three or even all four hands simultaneously. ...
They are more powerful because they can combine more yukti at the same time to cast more powerful spells.
This is our home, two-leg. A group of several islands, and in the south lies the lagoon city Silvertides, where we are standing at the moment. ...
The lower regions here are mostly covered by jungle and submerged lush grass. The Rising steadily claims those areas. Thus, Marapur is very slowly but unstoppably flooded by the surrounding ocean.
It is time to be grateful for all the blessings the tides bring with them.

Or to one of the parents in case they are no longer in a relationship. Which happens quite often, because we rarely form longer, monogamous relationships.

If they spot these and can snatch them without major risk, the birds will often steal such items and hide them in their nests.

Be careful, though, two-leg: Parders prey on humanoid bipeds.

However, when we discovered that the giant beavers native to Marapur were easier to tame and less costly to care for and feed, we turned away from domesticating makara.

These objects can then be seen swirling around in their watery shapes.
If you want to send a letter or parcel to someone, ask Amra at the post office in Moonfall.
Asphota sells tools at the market here in Silvertides.
She is our princess, the daughter of our raja Nilavarna. A wonderful young woman, very educated and kind.
He's one of our best beaver whisperers.
If you want to sell some gems, Giri is the one you should ask. You can find him at the market in Moonfall.
She is a young two-leg from Issavi and is selling two-leg friendly furniture at the market in Moonfall.
Isika sells ammunition at the market here in Silvertides.
I have never heard of her.
He is the son of Saraki, the mountain folk's maharani. A prince and also a very likable and handsome young man, according to what I have heard.
He is our raja and very beloved by our people because of his kindness and wisdom.
Nipuna is selling wands and runes at the market here in Silvertides.
She is the maharani of the mountain folk. She is a charming and strong-willed woman who takes her responsibilities very seriously.
He is Sissek's brother and arrived together with him from Zao, a long time ago. He runs the tavern in the House of Rest and Wisdom in Moonfall.

He is a two-leg but a different kind of biped than you are. Scaly all over, like our lower bodies. He came to Marapur from Zao a long time ago. Until then we didn't know what a bank was. But he established one in Moonfall.
She is a gifted alchemist and is selling potions at the market in Moonfall.
I'm afraid, I can't talk about her at the moment. It's a rather unfortunate story but one I can't discuss with everyone, I'm sorry.
She is an astronomer in Moonfall and has a laboratory slightly away from the city.
She is the mountain folk's shaman. As far as I know, the maharani highly appreciates her wise advice.
He has a magic carpet with which he can fly through the air. If you ask him, he might be able to fly you to other islands or continents.
Farewell, stranger. May the water spirits protect you.
pages.title: Tarisu

pages.name: Emael
npc_lines: Not enough space for all my trophies...
Hello! Ever asked yourself who killed all the monsters for the wall trophies? Yeah, that was me, Emael the Beasthunter! I am an expert in displaying trophies. ...
So if you have at least some dangerous monster to show off I strongly advise you to aquire a podium of vigour.
My name is Emael.
My job is to showcase the trophies of slain monsters as aesthetical as possible. You can admire my work here in the Adventurers' Guild.
Do you want to appropriately show off your boss trophies and buy an additional podium of vigour for 1000000 Gold?
I wish you a good hunt. Goodbye!
pages.title: Emael

pages.name: Saraki
npc_lines: My son and his crazy ideas.
The asuri are back to cause trouble, I'm sure ...
We are lucky to have Timira. Her wisdom helped us many times.
Greetings, traveller. May the Moon Goddess bless you.
I'm the mountain nagas' maharani. You would call it queen, I guess.
My name is Saraki.
It is exactly horas.

His name is Nihaka. A good child, really, but he has some crazy ideas lately.
He's in love. Of course he is, he's a young man and it is quite normal for him to look for a mate. But it's Candra, a young coastal woman, he lost his heart to. ...
Don't get me wrong: I have nothing against this young woman and highly respect her father Nilavarna. But a mountain naga and a coastal naga - that's perhaps not the best idea. ...
Besides, he even talked about marriage! That's really the crazy idea of a lovestruck child. You have to know, two-leg, that nagas don't form families in the same way that you usually do.

The crazy idea of two adolescents - and with someone from the other culture at that. On the other hand ... Hm, such a union could indeed strengthen the cohesion of the nagas as a whole again. ...
I guess, if our shaman Vrisaki would give her blessing I would consent to this marriage. Feel free to talk about it with my son, that will do no harm, I guess.

That's what we call it, yes. The rising of the sea level and the flooding of Marapur began centuries ago. But it progresses very slowly, so we are not forced to flee. ...

The coast folk down there in Silvertides have strongly integrated the Rising into their culture and way of life. The so-called coastal nagas adapt to living with the water and take advantage of its benefits instead of resisting it. ...

We, the mountain nagas, live in the Stardance Mountains that have not yet been affected by the Rising. Because of this, there are some cultural differences, for example in terms of religious customs, diet and lifestyle.

The two-headed turtle has its name for a rather obvious reason: it has two heads. But otherwise it is a common, albeit very large, reptile. It is aquatic and lives mainly in the large reefs around and beneath Marapur. ...
Although it feeds mainly on plants and fish, it can become aggressive and dangerous if you intrude on its territory.
Moas are large birds with a striking, colourful plumage. Because of their strong legs, with which they can move quickly on land, you might think that moas are incapable of flight. ...
In fact, however, they are good flyers and prefer to build their nests in the high mountainous areas of Marapur.

The parder is a wild cat living here in Marapur. Its fur is of a dark ochreous ground-color, obliterated by a dark-brown blotched pattern on legs and flanks. A dark stripe also runs from the head across the neck and back. ...
Be careful, two-leg: Parders prey on humanoid bipeds.

Makara are native to the waters of Marapur. They look like a cross between a hippopotamus and a seahorse, but are clearly comparable to the former in size. Many two-legs call it a quite unusual creature, as I heard.
Foam stalkers are elemental water creatures. Here on Marapur they emerge from the spray of waterfalls cascading down from the mountains. ...
Since they cannot survive on land for long, they quickly retreat below sea level after their emergence and thus populate the reef caves beneath and around Marapur.
If you want to send a letter or parcel to someone, ask Amra at the post office here in Moonfall.
Asphota sells tools at the market of Silvertides.

She is the daughter of Nilavarna, the coastal nagas' raja. A very pretty girl and also polite and well educated. So yes, I can understand my son's feelings. But she is a coastal naga, after all, so I really don't know ...
I'm not quite sure, but I guess he is one of the coastal nagas' beaver keepers.
If you want to sell some gems, Giri is the one you should ask. You can find him at the market here in Moonfall.
She is a young two-leg from Issavi and is selling two-leg friendly furniture at the market here in Moonfall.
Isika sells ammunition at the market of Silvertides.
Kaumudi is one of our hatch-mothers. That means she cares for the eggs of all of Moonfall's nagas. You have to know, two-leg, that nagas don't form families in the same way that you usually do.
Yes, that's my son you are talking about. A good child, really, but he has some crazy ideas lately.

He is the raja of the coast folk. You would call him a king, I guess. A kind and patient man who takes his responsibilities very seriously. Despite our cultural differences I always appreciate his prudence.
Nipuna is selling wands and runes at the market of Silvertides.
He is Sissek's brother and arrived together with him from Zao, a long time ago. He runs the tavern in the House of Rest and Wisdom here in Moonfall.

He is a two-leg but a different kind of biped than you are. Scaly all over, like our lower bodies. He came here from Zao a long time ago. Until then we didn't know what a bank was. But he established one here in Moonfall.
She is a gifted alchemist and is selling potions at the market here in Moonfall.
He is the coast folk's shaman. He is a powerful wave shaper and one of the wisest tide sages, according to what I have heard.

Timira is a very well known sage and philosopher amongst my people. But I'm afraid, I can't talk about her at the moment. It's a rather unfortunate story but one I can't discuss with everyone, I'm sorry.
She is our astronomer and has a laboratory slightly away from the city. She has vast knowledge about the night sky and the star constellations.
She is our shaman. You can find her high up above Moonfall in the sanctum of the mountain spirits. Her wise advice is always guiding us safely through all imponderables.
He has a magic carpet with which he can fly through the air. If you ask him, he might be able to fly you to other islands or continents.
Farewell. May Amati guide your ways.
pages.title: Saraki

pages.name: Dhira
npc_lines: So loyal and industrious. Really the best mammals.
Beavers are a naga's best friend.
But this wooden fence worries me. The raja really should send someone to build a stone fence.
Greetings, two-leg.
I'm the keeper of the beavers here.
My name is Dhira.
It is beaver feeding time.
We use the island's giant beavers as beasts of burden to transport timbers, star leaf and other material. ...
These beavers are taken care of by the beaver whisperers, who build a trusting relationship with the animals and thus get them to work for us.
Silvertides is our city, home of the coast folk.
This is our home. A group of several islands, and in the south lies the lagoon city Silvertides, where we are standing at the moment.
The mountain folk lives high up in the Stardance Mountains, in a city called Moonfall.
Wave shapers are a kind of water-magicians who can create solid water, charge it with magic and also transform it into other forms. ...
They have a sort of water-empathy that allows them to solidify the water and then shape it as if it were soft wax.
Tide sages know everything about the tidal currents and can reliably predict when it is safe to navigate the sea with the small naga boats. ...
They know when schools of fish come close to the coasts, making it a good time to fish. And they can estimate which islands will be affected by the Rising soon.
It began centuries ago but it progresses very slowly. We, the coast folk here in Silvertides, have integrated the Rising into our culture and way of life.

The two-headed turtle has its name for a rather obvious reason: it has two heads. But otherwise it is a common, albeit very large, reptile. It is aquatic and lives mainly in the large reefs around and beneath Marapur. ...
Although it feeds mainly on plants and fish, it can become aggressive and dangerous if you intrude on its territory.
Moas are large birds with a striking, colourful plumage. Because of their strong legs, with which they can move quickly on land, you might think that moas are incapable of flight. ...
In fact, however, they are good flyers and prefer to build their nests in the high mountainous areas of Marapur.

The parder is a wild cat living here in Marapur. Its fur is of a dark ochreous ground-color, obliterated by a dark-brown blotched pattern on legs and flanks. A dark stripe also runs from the head across the neck and back. ...
Be careful, two-leg: Parders prey on humanoid bipeds.

Makara are native to the waters of Marapur. They look like a cross between a hippopotamus and a seahorse, but are clearly comparable to the former in size. Many two-legs call it a quite unusual creature, as I heard.
Foam stalkers are elemental water creatures. Here on Marapur they emerge from the spray of waterfalls cascading down from the mountains. ...
Since they cannot survive on land for long, they quickly retreat below sea level after their emergence and thus populate the reef caves beneath and around Marapur.
If you want to send a letter or parcel to someone, ask Amra at the post office in Moonfall.
Asphota sells tools at the market here in Silvertides.
She is our princess, very beautiful and educated. Her father is our raja Nilavarna.
If you want to sell some gems, Giri is the one you should ask. You can find him at the market in Moonfall.
She is a young two-leg from Issavi and is selling two-leg friendly furniture at the market in Moonfall.
Isika sells ammunition at the market here in Silvertides.
I'm sorry but I don't know her.
He is the son of Saraki, the mountain folk's maharani.
He is the raja of the coast folk. You would call him our king, I guess. He is very beloved by our people.
Nipuna is selling wands and runes at the market here in Silvertides.
She is the maharani of the mountain folk. She is said to be a charming and strong-willed woman who takes her responsibilities very seriously.
He is Sissek's brother and arrived together with him from Zao, a long time ago. He runs the tavern in the House of Rest and Wisdom in Moonfall.

He is a two-leg but a different kind of biped than you are. Scaly all over, like our lower bodies. He came to Marapur from Zao a long time ago. Until then we didn't know what a bank was. But he established one in Moonfall.
She is a gifted alchemist and is selling potions at the market in Moonfall.
He is our shaman, a powerful wave shaper and one of the wisest tide sages.
I'm afraid, I can't talk about her at the moment. It's a rather unfortunate story but one I can't discuss with everyone, I'm sorry.
She is an astronomer in Moonfall and has a laboratory slightly away from the city.
She is the coast folk's shaman. As far as I know, the maharani highly appreciates her wise advice.
He has a magic carpet with which he can fly through the air. If you ask him, he might be able to fly you to other islands or continents.
Farewell and warm waters!
pages.title: Dhira

pages.name: Ysbasra
npc_lines: Greetings my friend. It's a relief to see a friendly face in times of trouble.
I was in search of my lost brother. After a long investigation I found most disturbing hints that he amongst others has been abducted for nefarious purposes.
The ruffians that my mercenaries rounded up admitted that they sold their captives to a scientist, that conducts abominable experiments on those captives.
This amoral creature that is known as doctor Marrow has a more than questionable reputation amongst his peers in science.
His disregard of human life and single minded pursuit of his research had him expelled from several institutions despite his scientific genius.
I fear the worst for my dear brother. I beg you to pick up his trail. I've arranged for a passage to the remote island. ...
I plead to you to travel to the island and save my brother from the clutches of doctor Marrow.
A smuggler on Cormaya was the only one, brave enough to set sail to such a remote isle in unknown waters. I will instruct him to ferry you safely to that island. ...
Will you accept this mission? Yes or No?
Thank you so much. I beg you though, please hurry!
pages.title: Ysbasra

pages.name: Golem Servant
npc_lines: Failure is not an option!
You are too late, flesh unit! We must restart the repair procedure.
I am a servant and maintenance golem. I also operate the lift.
The lift is damaged, sir or madame flesh unit! I could initiate the repair process but I need the correct tools and parts for the repairs ...
If you wish to initiate the repair process ask me for repairs, male or female unit.
I require no name.
You must bring me the correct components or tools. The items deteriorate when they leave their conservation fields so you must be quick ...
Are you ready, flesh unit?
Good bye.
pages.title: Golem Servant

pages.name: Torkada
npc_lines: This is most peculiar.
My superiors must learn about this.
These are dark times.
Greetings! This isn't the time to chitchat though.
This expedition is here on an important mission for the inquisition.
Some nosy adventurers dug up more than they could chew, while exploring the drefian ruins. They discovered the entrance of some sort of temple of evil. ...
Now, places of evil is what this whole wretched place of Drefia consists of, yet this temple was foul, even for drefian standards. The adventurers returned .. twisted and tainted. ...

We couldn't save them but had to .. cleanse them in a permanent way. However by studying them we could create appropriate wards that should keep the corruption of the temple at bay .. for a time at least.
Most operations of the inquisition are classified information. But rest assured we are busy in all parts of the world. And we have to as these are dire times and heresy is on the rise!
You shouldn't concern yourself with such topics. Their filth might stick and taint. ...
Live a pious life and heed the teachings of the gods of good! Stay away from heretics and report them to the inquisition. We will handle them one by one and cleanse the world of their rot!
For long years I served the inquisition as high judge and advisor. I compiled books about the sacred laws and rooting out of heretics. ...
But our ranks are stretched thin in these times and I took it upon me to return to rather mundane field duties like this. ...
It might not be the most glorious task at hand but it has to be done and I'm up to it.
A vile place indeed. Yet it serves us as a constant reminder where demon worship and depravity will ultimately lead to.
For sure you already know about the good gods. I am not a preacher but a man of action!
Are you willing, to bring the fury of the inquisition to that foul place and eradicate all evil you find? Speak, yes or no?
Good bye.
pages.title: Torkada

pages.name: Tonar
npc_lines: What a beautiful day for a little boat trip.
Welcome, Sir.
I'm offering a little ferry service between Ankrahmun and the island nearby.
The city of Ankrahmun is located right here, my friend. It is composed of mostly pyramids. Previously they were used to house the dead, but today these structures serve as homes and shops.
Yes, an island south-west of here, called Oskayaat.
The island is geographically split into two quite different regions. In the west it is covered with jungle, and in the east there is a steppe. ...

A mountain reach in the centre divides the island into the dry east and the humid, overgrown west. Built into those mountains is the beautiful city Oska. In the south-east, on a smaller island, there is a still sometimes active volcano. ...
The humans living on the island are quite highly developed. Their civilization is one of art and beauty, well known for its rich culture and history. ...
But then something happened: A curse reached the island, that transformed people into feral creatures.
My name is Tonar.
That's my name, alright.
I saw creatures on the nearby island that kept me from going ashore there. Crocodiles, tigers and panthers that walked upright on two legs, dressed in scraps of clothing. ...
Really, it's true, I saw it with my own eyes! Something strange is happening on Oskayaat.
Not today, my friend. Perhaps another day.
Good bye.
pages.title: Tonar

pages.name: A Bloodshade
npc_lines: Mortal! If you are on a quest to serve the blood god, my master - be greeted!
I was once the greatest priest and prophet of the one true good of blood. I lead his followers through the dawn of our cult until the demise of our god.
The quest, that requires my continued existence in this plane, is to eradicate the festering wound that defiles this place.
The blood god's power has been corrupted and the spawn that festers in his former realms are a mockery of its grandeur. ...
It has to be exterminated and the realm must be cleansed from the festering presence that came to dwell here!
After the fall of the blood god unclean things arose from his carcass. They festered on his remaining essence and devoured it. Claimed to be his descendants, claimed to carry his legacy. ...
But to me it soon became obvious these abominable spawns were just parasites, maggots that desecrated the legacy of a true god. They have to be stopped once and for all. ...
Their rampant growth and spread is an anathema to the blood god. They are not his descendants, they are just rot that feeds upon divine essence.
We all could constantly feel the presence of our god in our very own blood. Then, all of a sudden, his presence ceased to be, the connection was lost. ...

For sure our lord has been slain by envious gods! But blood and slaughter are eternal. There is no end that can't be overcome by universal principle. He who has been slain will rise in slaughter once the time has come! ...
However, first the cleansing of this place has to occur!
You are not worthy to learn of the blood gods teaching, neither to receive his blessings.
Your body and your mind are not prepared to receive the blessings of the blood god.
Two sets of twins. Two represent the rot that spreads, tarnishes and dissolves. ...
The other pair represent the absence of light, the darkness that devours, the anti-light.
The foul thing must fall! Its presence and existence de-sanctifies the holy realm of blood. ...
To be able to challenge that thing, however, you have to handle its spawn. Slay that brood and the way to Bakragore is wide open.

You will have to defeat what calls itself Bakragore at least once to attack the core of its festering presence. You will be able to choose how much of the foul taint of Bakragore and its spawn you can endure. ...
Yet the more taint you put onto you, the harder the battle will become, yet the rewards will be greater.
The scar and void, that the blood gods demise created, still radiated with its divine power. It became an entity of its own. ...
A filthy thing of decay and rot. And it grew in power, unchecked. A malicious evil dwelt in its core, while it roamed the once holy grounds with all of its soiling presence. ...
It shambled and devoured. Its sustenance were the worshippers of the blood god, dead or alive. None of them escaped the hunger. Eventually even the most mighty gave in. ...
The most mighty of all were the dragons, magnificent species of their king. Dragons of might and the olden days. Not the pathetic shadows you know in these days. ...
The thing .. infected them, overtook them, made them his and made them him. ...
At some point, out of a conscious thought or raw instinct, perhaps even a physical necessity the thing gave birth to two sets of twins. ...
Not in any physical sense though. It split aspects of his own, that had befallen some dragons and made them entities of their own. ...
Thus, the twins of rot and the twins of 'the light that is not' came to be.
Though what is left of the powers, granted to me by my god and my extensive knowledge of his essence, I'm able to assist you in managing the taint that you obtained and you bear. ...
Mind you, however, I can only remove the burden that you are bearing. Once done you will have to acquire the taints anew.
You are not tainted, mortal.
I can help you with the taint that you wield. You just have to ask.
After your first victory, the healing of the place might slowly begin. Yet the wound that is Bakragore will still fester. More victories can weaken the festering even more, yet not without sacrifice.
You will acquire a taint, a certain corruption, a touch of decay when you kill the festering spawn and Bakragore, its source.
The taint of decay will wither and devour any lesser being. But you .. you might prevail.
You can't escape the taint entirely. Yet you can endure it - at a cost.
There are hindrances and weaknesses that come with the taint. ...
You will experience that things won't get as easy as they used to be. Only as long as you are in the contaminated areas, but still.
To enter the realm of the sanguine master and destroy its spawn, a sufficient sacrifice is imperative. ...
Find and slay the keeper of blooded tears and bring the nectar of his eyes before the blood god. Present your gift on the sacrificial altar. ...
After - and under no circumstances before - you have completed this procedure, you can enter the sacred fluid. You can, of course also take a slightly faster... detour.
Hm. I see. Well, I will be frank. Every blood sacrifice has its price. Blood money will please the blood god... just as well. ...
The sum would be five million gold pieces and I... my master will be pleased. Are you prepared for a sacrifice such as this?
I can still sense the growing power within the putrid realms beyond. Go and end that threat once and for all.
Farewell.
pages.title: A Bloodshade

pages.name: Niral
npc_lines: Greetings, traveller!
I'm a priestess of Amati, the Moon Goddess.
My name is Niral.
Farewell.
There is an old legend among my people: A small fragment of the moon fell upon this island, a long time before the larger shard came down. ...
It hit the volcano off our eastern coast and sank into its heart. There it remained, bound within the molten earth. And since then, the mountain remembers: ...
When the moon is full, Amati's lost fragment answers her call and the lava turns blue. That is what we need. The moonsilver energy is powerful. ...
Only something that has already endured the moon's power can seal it. Go to the volcano when the moon is full and gather some of the blue lava in a special vessel. ...
It isn't full moon at the moment, but time is of the essence and we cannot wait until Amati shines in all her glory. But there is a way out. ...
I know from the tales of travellers and adventurers that the fae of Feyrist craft objects in which they can capture the light of the sun, the stars or the moon. ...
In this case, you need a moon mirror. The moonlight captured within it is so concentrated that it could have the same effect as the full moon herself. ...
With the help of such a mirror, you could turn the lava in the volcano blue. But of course, this will only work for a brief moment, so you should hurry to collect the lava afterwards.
You need a special magical crystal flask that is able to contain even lava. Such vessels are rare and valuable. ...
However, I know that shortly before the outbreak of the were sickness, a ship carrying a cargo of such vessels arrived in Oska. ...
Unfortunately, it is now nothing more than a wreck that has run aground off the harbour. But if you're lucky, you might still find a flask there that can hold lava.
pages.title: Niral

pages.name: Cheaty
npc_lines: Be greeted, Jogador! My friend, the Draccoon, wants to have a talk with you!
I am Cheaty Chief, just call me Cheaty, no need for formalities like calling me Miss. <chuckles>
The Draccoon is a magnificent creature, somewhat like a rascoohan, somewhat like a dragon. ...
He taught me my first few spells when I was a little cub.
Ah, good old Venore, the city of trash.
The Draccoon has just returned after a longer inconvenient absence. He could use the help of some talented individuals and has a mission for them. Are you interested, yes or no?
Bye, bye, Jogador.
pages.title: Cheaty

pages.name: The Draccoon (NPC)
npc_lines: Hello, Jogador! I am glad to see you!
I'm just known as 'The Draccoon'! Like some famous artists, you know. I am one of a kind anyway!
Besides being awesome? I make plans.
The city has changed so much, since I left! I hardly recognized it!
I love it, when a plan comes together.
I need your assistance in a quest of mine!
Due to treachery and malice the evil dragon Nimmersatt managed to catch me in a trap and held me captive for 20 years!
As he is greedy and always hungry, he made me one of his cooks! I had to serve him the finest meals for 20 years, to his constant complaints!
He was never satisfied and always found something to criticise and his complaints never stopped! ...
Gladly over the years, he let his guard down and I managed to escape!
Now that I am free again, I am plotting my revenge... and this is where you enter the picture!
Even in captivity, I heard about all your exploits and deeds and decided you are just the person I need to bring my plans to fruition! ...
I hope you are ready for that mission!
Well, the dragon Nimmersatt managed to catch me off guard and entrapped me with the intention to devour me. ...

Knowing his insatiable appetite, I managed to talk him into accepting me as one of his cooks! Indeed, my cooking skills aren't garbage, so to say, and I managed to prolong my life for one year after the other. ...
Over the years, even Nimmersatt himself let his guard down, and I learned many of his secrets. After 20 years, I finally managed to trick myself out of his clutches and managed to escape! ...
Now the time of the revenge of the Draccoon has come! Nimmersatt will pay dearly for what he did to me! But not only that! ...
There are also old friends to be contacted, debts to be called in, and some other culprits to be punished for their role in my capture and imprisonment! ...
I'd like you to assist me in that mission.
My dearest human friend must yet be informed of my return. I am sure he will join us in our campaign! ...
He lives in an apartment in Kazordoon, as I understand he had some trouble in most other cities. I'm pretty sure you'll still find him there. ...
Just pay him a visit and tell him, his good old pal, the Draccoon is back!
Good bye, my friend!
pages.title: The Draccoon (NPC)

pages.name: Hector the Mentor
npc_lines: Hail, traveller and welcome! I can help you getting started and offer various services, what shall it be.
I am a philosopher from Thais, working both for king Tibianus as an advisor as well as mentoring new students of the Edron Academy. Which is also part of the reason why I'm here now.
My name is Hector, pleased to meet you, traveller!
It should be exactly Horário dentro do jogo by now.
Thank you for helping me out in finding the culprit behind the wolves in the cave and delivering the mushroom in time to bring closure to this. ...
There are also many fellow adventurers in Tibia, don't hesitate to ask them for help or even join forces with others to overcome the many perils of this world!
I offer what equipment is left from my fellow students for trade as well as banking services, I can also provide healing.
We can change money for you. You can also access your bank account or your guild account options.

There are three different coin types in Tibia: 100 gold coins equal 1 platinum coin, 100 platinum coins equal 1 crystal coin. So if you'd like to change 100 gold into 1 platinum, simply say 'change gold' and then '1 platinum'.
Every Tibian has one. The big advantage is that you can access your money in every branch of the Tibian Bank! ...
Would you like to know more about the basic functions of your bank account, the advanced functions, or are you already bored, perhaps?
Okay okay, no need to be rude! It seems you already know everything.
You can check the balance of your bank account, deposit money or withdraw it. You can also transfer money to other characters, provided that they have chosen a vocation and reached the mainland.
Your bank account will be used automatically when you want to rent a house or bid on an item on the market. Let me know if you want to know about how either one works.
Renting a house has never been this easy. Simply make a bid for an auction. We will check immediately if you have enough money ...

Please keep in mind that the sum you have used to bid will be unavailable unless somebody places a higher bid. Once you have acquired a house the rent will be charged automatically from your bank account every month.

If you buy an item from the market, the required gold will be deducted from your bank account automatically. On the other hand, money you earn for selling items via the market will be added to your account. It's easy!
You can transfer money from your account to the account of a guild via player guild transfer. If you are a member of a guild, you can deposit money on its account via guild deposit. ...
If you are leader or vice leader of a guild, you can also withdraw gold from your guild account via guild withdraw or use a guild transfer to transfer money from your guild to another guild. ...
As a leader or vice leader of a guild you can also transfer money from your guild account to a player account via guild player transfer. ...
Please keep in mind that we may need some time to process such requests.
Thais is the commercial and cultural centre of Tibia. There's a lot to see and do.
I've been teaching and lecturing at Edron's academy for decades. It's an honourable faculty with many bright and talented individuals such as my dear friend and colleague Spectulus.
A dear friend of mine who I have worked with many an hour on countless projects and experiments. He's quite the character, always busy but will grow on you over time.
King Tibianus is the righteous and wise ruler I have the honour of working as an advisor for.
He's a capable sorcerer, not too keen on my philosophical ramblings, however.
A delicate and dangerous topic, I prefer not to talk about him here as we have to deal with enough trouble here as it is.
Baxter was an adventurer like you once but then... something happened to him but I can't quite remember.
If you're looking for a fun companion, he might tell you a good joke or two - unless you fell victim to one of his pranks first...!
A troubled mind but he is kind at heart. He would lose his head if it wasn't firmly attached, however.
A formidable huntress, I'd not pick a quarrel with here if I were you.
A great knight who trained many heroes, such as yourself.
An evil fellow, you should be extra careful.
A well-known sorceress, kind of a bookworm like myself I might add.
Chief of the druids and a mighty one at that.
No more lessons from me, I'm afraid. The retirement is now calling, I always wanted to try fishing.
A tall tale, some warriors are quite obsessed with it.
Farewell, traveller and take care!
pages.title: Hector the Mentor

pages.name: Gunther
npc_lines: Oh my!
What a mess.
They have to believe me!
Oh, please excuse me, I am looking for a seasoned adventurer!
Greetings adventurer!
I am an overseas-trader by trade.
My name is Gunther Holz.
I hoped to meet an adventurer such as you! No one is listening to me, they claim I am mad, but I am not!
Yes, YES! I've seen IT!
It was a plant! On open seas!!! I swear! And it was humongous!
It was as big as a castle! And that was only the part I could see over water! And it moved!!!
Yes it was slowly but steadily heading straight for the mainland.
I can't tell where or when it arrives at the shores. But somewhere at some point it will! And it will be a disaster!
Can you imagine the damage a gigantic walking plant will cause? It will raze cities, stomp out armies! It has to be stopped!
I called in a few favours from the adventurer's guild and the explorer society to fund an expedition to seek out that monster. ...
All I need now is some brave souls to man the ships and destroy that monster!
Say, will you be one of the heroes to save the day? Yes or no?
Our time might be running out!
Take care, friend!
pages.title: Gunther

pages.name: A Captive Forest Fury
npc_lines: Free me!
I have to get out of here.
You, over there ... could you help me, please?
Better not talk to me. It could make them angry.
I'm a prisoner here, as you can see.
A forest fury never tells her real name.
Time seems endless in this cage.
Farewell. May your dreams be pleasant.
pages.title: A Captive Forest Fury

pages.name: Atui
npc_lines: Be greeted at this forsaken place!
It's yet another place that has been tainted by the vile touch of Doctor Marrow!
He somehow fused animals and humans into abominations like me! But I endured. I escaped! And I swore revenge!
I managed to follow Marrow and his new Quara allies to this thing here.
It's a gigantic walking plant that Marrow somehow stumbled upon. While in hiding, I could even hear his nefarious plans!
You see, Marrow and his henchmen are here to harvest a precious resin from the plant. Only the gods know what he might need it for.
Yes, they harvest the resin, which brought them in conflict with some native plant people. Yet while harvesting the resin, Marrow found out a horrible detail.
When they hurt certain plant veins, the giant plant reacts. Now he is misusing this fact, to make it walk towards the mainland.
Marrow figured he'd not only harvest the plant for its resin, he would also use the monster to pay back the society that shunned him and his amoral ideas.
He will use the plant monster as a weapon of mass destruction and to devastate whole cities!
I have no clue what could stop the plant monster from the outside, BUT we can kill Marrow here and now. ...
As soon as they stop harming the plant-thing it will probably get dormant again. So all we have to do, is to fight our way down to Marrow's lair deep down in the plant's stalk.
We better go separate ways. I have my own, stealthy methods. You will somehow have to handle Marrow's minions and the inhabitants of the plant.
There are some native species here. Some sentient plants and the usual giant insects, you know. ...
The plant people are a strange lot, however. They revere the plant as their ancestor and its amber as sacred. I know because I talked to them!
Well they don't talk like we'd do! They somehow communicate directly from mind to mind. This only works for plantlife though, as far as I can tell. ...
By chance, however, I found a way to communicate with them, so to speak.
Stranded here I was kind of desperate for food. I ate anything I could get. It gave me a bad stomach several times, I tell you.
But the worst was the demon root, as I called it!
As soon as you digest it, or rather try to, the thing will burrow its roots into your system! It will give you the headache of a lifetime!
Turned out, that's actually a good thing! That thing seems to be rather symbiotic. As the plant people told me, it will do me no harm.
And after death I'd become the fertiliser for a neat little tree it seems! Not that I'd care when I'm dead. However the thing has a side effect.
Remember those roots, that burrow into your brain? Well they allow the priests of the plant people to communicate with you. If they like to, that is.
Some of them are the only ones willing to interact with us! Without their help you probably won't make it to Marrow's lair.
Yes, they might be of help, but first things first! You'll need a demon root and devour it. ...
Luckily most plant creatures here might carry one around. They are rare but eventually you might loot one of them. Good luck.
pages.title: Atui

pages.name: A Floating Sugar Ball
npc_lines: *hummmm*
*buzzzz*
*This floating ball appears to be made of glowing red sugar. It moves gently up and down and emits a soft humming sound.*
pages.title: A Floating Sugar Ball

pages.name: A Stressed Sugar Cube Worker
npc_lines: No ... no no no, won't work.
Like this? No, this will cause the mechanism to jam.
This has to work ... somehow.
*The sugar cube worker does not give the impression of understanding you. And it seems to be rather busy.*
pages.title: A Stressed Sugar Cube Worker

pages.name: Dulcineo
npc_lines: It's like tilting at windmills.
There must be a way to resolve these disagreements.
Ah, the Candy Carnival ... one of the best festivities in Candia.
*The pastel-coloured faun greets you but you don't understand him. He makes a gesture as if to apply some lipstick. Then he is pointing to the east. But what does that mean?*
pages.title: Dulcineo

pages.name: Toffee
npc_lines: Buy fresh fruit for candying here!
Wafer paper flowers? Lime tart? Brigadeiros? Just bring them here, I have a use for them!
Freshly baked cakes and cookies!
*The globose cook greets you but you don't understand him. He makes a gesture as if to apply some lipstick. Then he is pointing to the east. But what does that mean?*
pages.title: Toffee

pages.name: Wyrdin’s Apprentice
npc_lines: Hm? Who's disturbing my perusal! I've just returned from Yalahar and have a lot of reading to do - make it short.
They discovered a new city to the far north. I've been there, it's huge and bustling, filled to the brim with exotic wares, magic and adventure. ...
I was an apprentice to the researcher Wyrdin in Edron, he sent me there. He wanted to retrieve some research from the explorer society's representative Timothy, who is stationed there. ...
However, after seeing what the city had to offer, I took matters in my own hands and started my own venture. Independence and stuff. ...
I am now translating scientific books from all kinds of sources in Yalahar and beyond. Once I have completed enough tracts, reports and encyclopedias, I will open a store. ...
I also cut Captain Bluebear a deal to provide passage to the city's harbour, a simple investment. He brings me there, he gets a cut of my published books. ...
And since I'm a man of business at heart, I could let you in, too - provided an appropriate sum of gold for my expenses of course. You in?
Great. To cover my expenses, you will have to pay me a... one-time fee. Let's make it 250 gold and you're good to go. What do you say?
Done deal! The password is 'whizzkid'. Say this to captain Bluebear in Thais and he will know. Please be on your way now, these books won't translate themselves.
Hm? Who's disturbing my perusal! I've just returned from Yalahar and have a lot of reading to do - make it short.
They discovered a new city to the far north. I've been there, it's huge and bustling, filled to the brim with exotic wares, magic and adventure. ...
I was an apprentice to the researcher Wyrdin in Edron, he sent me there. He wanted to retrieve some research from the explorer society's representative Timothy, who is stationed there. ...
However, after seeing what the city had to offer, I took matters in my own hands and started my own venture. Independence and stuff. ...

And since I'm a man of business at heart, I could let you in, too - provided an appropriate sum of gold for my expenses of course. You in?
